He listened "calmly" to Uncle Zhang’s report regarding the cutoff of the water supply and the mutiny of the troops. Immediately, he furrowed his brows and fell into a long, "deep contemplation."

After a long while, he slapped his thigh hard and said in a tone of sudden realization:

"This Prince knows what to do!"

All eyes were fixed upon him.

"This matter is absolutely not the work of man!" Xiao Cheng said with a grave face, his tone resolute. "To manipulate the river course and divert the water—this is the work of gods! That Ma Wanshan is a mere mortal; how could he possess such heaven-defying abilities?"

"It must be... it must be that we are newcomers who failed to pay our respects to the local spirits, and thus angered the deity of this land!"

As soon as these words were spoken, the entire place fell silent.

Even the soldiers who were causing the disturbance looked at this Prince as if he were a fool.

Xiao Cheng, however, was completely oblivious. He grew more excited as he spoke, as if he had found the only truth to solve the problem.

"I remember now! Ancient books record that all great rivers are governed by a Dragon King! The Yinma River running dry must mean the Dragon King of this place is enraged!"

"We have offended the Dragon King!"

"Immediately!" He waved his hand, issuing his "decree" to the stunned crowd in a tone that brooked no argument.

"Pass the order down: build a sacrificial altar nine feet and nine inches high at the highest point in the east of the city! Take all the cattle and sheep we brought and use them all as offerings!"

"This Prince shall personally set up the altar, observe a three-day fast, bathe, burn incense, pray to the heavens for rain, and beg the Dragon King for forgiveness!"

"As long as our sincerity moves the heavens, and the Dragon King is pleased, the water will naturally return!"

He spoke with such gravity, his expression suggesting not a banished Prince, but a high-ranking master about to save the masses from fire and water.

"Your... Your Highness..." Uncle Zhang’s lips trembled, unable to utter a complete sentence for a long time. "Now... now is not the time for this..."

"Foolish!" Xiao Cheng snapped sternly. "This is the foundation of our survival; it is a matter of utmost importance! Do you want this Prince to be like those common mortals, brandishing swords to fight with gods?"

"It is simply absurd!"

Having said this, he flicked his sleeves and left to return to his room to prepare for his "fast," leaving a room full of people in utter disarray.

Shen Li stood where she was, motionless.

She watched Xiao Cheng’s "concerned for the country and the people" back, watched him spouting nonsense with such a straight face, and the last spark of hope in her heart was completely extinguished.

Despair.

Utter, absolute despair.

She did not fear Ma Wanshan’s schemes, she did not fear the Crown Prince’s hidden arrows, and she did not even fear facing an army of thousands.

What she feared was having a teammate as useless as a pig.

An idiot who, at a moment of life and death, didn't think about how to break the deadlock, but instead thought about setting up an altar to pray for divine forgiveness.

She felt a wave of intense dizziness, born of both anger and helplessness.

She knew she could wait no longer.

If she waited any longer, her army would completely mutiny due to thirst and despair before Xiao Cheng’s ridiculous altar was even built.

She slowly drew the sword at her waist that had accompanied her for ten years.

In the dim light, the blade still shimmered with a cold, icy glint.

Bloodbath the Ma family.

Slaughter all the officials who colluded with them.

Use the most direct method to reclaim the water and take control of this city.

This was the only way.

Even if it meant she would bear the reputation of being "cruel," and even if it plunged the Zhenguo Duke’s Mansion into an irredeemable situation.

She had no other choice.

Because she was, first and foremost, a general, and she had to be responsible for the four hundred lives that followed her.

A murderous intent, thick and inseparable, began to permeate from her.

Every soldier present felt this suffocating killing intent; they subconsciously took a step back, silent as cicadas in winter.

Shen Li carried her sword and walked, step by step, toward the outside of the mansion.

Her back was resolute and lonely.

chapters.title: The Intelligence Network Arrives
chapters.content:
In the dilapidated courtyard of the Prince’s mansion, there was silence.

Four hundred elite soldiers held their breath, all eyes focused on the woman walking toward the mansion gate with a sword in her hand.

Shen Li’s back was resolute and lonely.

Each of her steps seemed to land on everyone’s heart, heavy and filled with a tragic sense of marching toward destruction.

Everyone knew what it would mean once she stepped out of this door.

Bloodbath the Ma family.

Slaughter all the forces in this city that stood against them.

Use the most tragic and direct method to reclaim the water and reclaim the right to survive.

They would win. With the combat power of their battle-hardened elite force, slaughtering the ragtag private soldiers of the Ma family would be as easy as turning over one's hand.

And then?

Openly slaughtering local powerful clans and harming imperial officials—how was this any different from rebellion? What awaited them would be the thunderous wrath of the imperial court and the total ruin of the Zhenguo Duke’s Mansion. They would transform from soldiers of the Great Zhou into rebels whom everyone had the right to kill.

But they had no choice. Because if they didn't take this step, they would die of thirst here today.

The veins on Uncle Zhang’s hand, gripping the hilt of his sword, bulged. A struggle flashed in his eyes, followed by reluctance, but in the end, it turned into a resolute determination to follow his commander to the death.

He prepared to speak, to issue the order he least wanted to give in his life—

"All troops..."

"Report—!!"

A panicked, almost distorted scream came from outside the mansion, abruptly cutting off Uncle Zhang’s words.

Everyone looked toward the sound and saw a scout of the Black Armored Army rushing in, disheveled and tumbling. His face was covered in mud, his helmet was nowhere to be found, and his expression was one of extreme panic, as if he had seen a ghost.

This scout was one of the hundred mysterious private soldiers of Xiao Cheng. They were known for their strict discipline and calm demeanor; when had they ever been so uncomposed?

Shen Li stopped and slowly turned around, her gaze falling on the scout.

The scout rushed into the courtyard, ignoring everyone else, even ignoring Shen Li, the highest-ranking officer present, and went straight to his knees with a "thud" before the dilapidated room Xiao Cheng used for "fasting and praying."

"Your... Your Highness! Your Highness, save me!"

He kowtowed desperately toward the closed door, his voice filled with sobbing and lingering fear.

"This lowly one... this lowly one is guilty! This lowly one deserves to die!"

This sudden scene, completely contrary to military regulations, left everyone stunned.

The door creaked open.

Xiao Cheng walked out, wearing the white plain clothes he had changed into for his "fast." He looked much thinner, his face pale, and the "charlatan" look of a man compassionate for the world and preparing to pray for the masses had not yet fully faded.

Seeing the scout kneeling on the ground, he was stunned for a moment, then frowned and scolded in a tone that was somewhat majestic and feigned composure:

"Panicked and flustered, what kind of decorum is this! This Prince is here, calming his heart to pray for the masses; how can I allow you to make such a loud noise!"

The scout cried even harder, saying incoherently: "Your Highness! This lowly one... this lowly one was ordered to patrol outside the city, and thinking that Your Highness was worrying for us to the point of losing appetite, I... I wanted to catch a rabbit for Your Highness to nourish your body, to show my devotion..."

As soon as these words were spoken, the soldiers of the Shen family army around them showed looks of disdain.

The army was out of water, mutiny was imminent, and he wasn't thinking about how to guard against the enemy, but actually had the heart to catch a rabbit to curry favor? Was this the kind of trash the Black Armored Army was made of?

"This lowly one deserves to die, this lowly one is incompetent! I didn't catch the rabbit, but instead got lost in the woods, slipped, and fell into a pitch-black dry well!"

The scout’s voice was filled with the fear of surviving a disaster.

"I was battered and bruised at the bottom of the well, thinking I was going to die in there! Just when I was in despair, I fumbled around and... and actually touched a loose brick! I smashed the brick, and behind it... behind it was a tunnel! At the end of the tunnel was a rotten wooden box. I smashed the box, and inside... inside there were no gold or jewels, only... only this!"

As he spoke, he tremblingly took out a roll of something tightly wrapped in oilcloth from his bosom and held it high above his head.

The oilcloth had long since rotted, revealing a yellowed scroll inside, made of either sheepskin or cowhide.

Xiao Cheng looked at the scroll, his expression shifting from confusion to curiosity, and then to a kind of ecstasy as if struck by fate!

"Heaven... Heaven's will!"

He lunged forward, snatched the scroll, and carefully unfolded it. His movements carried a tremor that was almost devout.

It was a map. A map drawn with an extremely ancient technique, with ink blurred in many places.

Xiao Cheng spread the map on the ground and examined it closely. He looked at it with such focus, such immersion, as if what was drawn on it were not lines, but an elixir that could save lives.

Shen Li stood where she was, coldly watching this farce that was so clumsy it was laughable.

Catching a rabbit? Falling into a dry well? Touching a brick? Finding a treasure map?

He could actually act out this nonsense, which only a three-year-old would believe, with such a straight face!

The disdain in her heart had reached an insurmountable level.

"Hahaha! Heaven will not destroy me! Heaven will not destroy me!"

Just then, Xiao Cheng on the ground suddenly burst into a wild laugh. He held the tattered map high, facing the heavens, acting like a madman.

"Found it! Found it! We are saved!"

He leaped up from the ground, rushed to Shen Li, shoved the map into her hands, his face filled with uncontrollable ecstasy.

"Princess! Look! Look!"

"This... this is a secret military map from the previous dynasty! On it... it marks an underground river! It’s in a valley thirty miles west of the city! As long as we find the entrance, we will have water to drink!"

"And there’s more! There’s more!" He stuttered from excitement. "The map also says that at the end of the underground river, there is... a secret granary left by the army of the previous dynasty! Inside... inside is hidden enough grain to feed ten thousand people for a year!"

An underground river? A secret granary?

Shen Li’s gaze fell upon the so-called "treasure map." The map was drawn crudely, yet several key terrains and landmarks were exceptionally clear. A winding blue line snaked through several mountain ranges, with one branch flowing directly beneath Cangbei City. At the end of that line, a granary symbol was drawn.

Everything was too coincidental. So coincidental that it felt as if it had been forged specifically to resolve the current predicament.

Shen Li looked up at Xiao Cheng’s face, which was flushed red with excessive "excitement." She wanted to find even a trace of acting in his eyes.

She failed.

The ecstasy in his eyes was so real, so infectious, that the surrounding soldiers, who had already been in despair, felt a glimmer of hope reignite in their eyes upon hearing his words.

"Is it real? An underground river?"

"And a granary?!"

Suppressed murmurs broke out among the crowd.

Shen Li’s heart sank.

She knew this was a trap. A clumsy trap woven with hope.

Yet, she had no choice. Compared to charging out with blades to fight to the death with the Ma family and earning the charge of treason, verifying a nebulous hope was undoubtedly the only way to pacify the troops at this moment.

"Uncle Zhang," she said, putting away the map, her voice returning to its usual calm.

"This subordinate is here!"

"Pick one hundred men. Bring every container that can hold water and come with me."

"Yes!" A glimmer of excitement also flashed in Uncle Zhang’s eyes. Clearly, he, too, had chosen to believe in this "miracle."

Half an hour later, Shen Li led an elite squad to the desolate valley thirty miles west of the city, following the markings on the map. Guided by the map, they found a cave entrance hidden by vines and rubble beneath a cliff in the deepest part of the valley.

The entrance was small, allowing only one person to pass at a time. It was pitch black inside, with cold, chilling gusts of wind blowing out from time to time.

"Stay sharp!" Shen Li drew her sword and was the first to enter.

The cave was pitch black, the air damp and oppressive. They lit torches and cautiously explored nearly a hundred meters downward when, finally, a faint "swishing" sound reached their ears.

It was the sound of water!

Everyone’s spirits lifted! They quickened their pace, rounded a bend, and suddenly, the view opened up!

An underground river, several meters wide, appeared before them! The water was crystal clear, shimmering with rippling light under the glow of the torches!

"There’s water! There really is water!" A soldier could no longer contain himself; he rushed to the riverbank, cupped a handful of water, and gulped it down recklessly.

"It’s sweet! It’s sweet!" he shouted excitedly.

The despair that had been suppressed for days erupted at this moment! The soldiers cheered and rushed to the riverbank, drinking their fill of this hard-won sweet spring.

Shen Li did not move. She just quietly watched the very real underground river before her, but the clouds of suspicion in her heart grew heavier.

Everything was too real. So real... that it made her feel terrified.

"Your Highness! Look over there!" Following the direction of Uncle Zhang’s finger, Shen Li saw, on the opposite bank of the underground river, an artificial structure built of giant stones. It was a gate. Behind the gate lay the secret granary of the previous dynasty mentioned on the map.

They waded across and pushed open the heavy stone door together. A stale scent, a mixture of grain and dust, rushed toward them. The light of the torches illuminated the interior of the warehouse.

The entire warehouse was unimaginably huge. Rows of tall shelves were piled high with sacks wrapped tightly in oilcloth. Uncle Zhang rushed forward and sliced open a sack with his blade. Golden, slightly aged but still plump and dry grains of rice poured out with a rustling sound.

Grain! A mountain of grain! Enough to feed their army for a year, or even longer!

Water and food—the two greatest problems that could have driven them to a dead end—had both been solved in the span of a single hour in the most incredible way!

The morale of the army was completely secured!

When the convoy loaded with fresh water and grain returned to the dilapidated prince’s mansion, the entire camp was in an uproar! The soldiers cheered, lifting Shen Li and Uncle Zhang high, venting the joy of surviving a disaster in the most simple and honest way.

And the greatest hero of this "miracle," the Seventh Prince Xiao Cheng, stood on the steps, watching all of this with a face full of "gratification." He announced publicly that this was all a gift from the heavens, the result of his sincere prayers moving the gods.

Immediately after, he loudly announced that he would heavily reward the "lucky" scout who had discovered the treasure map.

A reward of one hundred taels! A promotion in rank!

Amidst the cheers of everyone, the scout knelt before Xiao Cheng, kowtowing to receive his reward. On his face was a perfectly measured look of surprise and being overwhelmed by favor.

Shen Li stood outside the crowd, watching this scene coldly.

Her gaze passed over the cheering crowd and locked firmly onto the soldier kneeling to receive his reward.

His expression was seamless.

His movements were humble and respectful.

His eyes... those eyes that had been filled with "terror" and "panic" during his report, now, when facing Xiao Cheng, held only one emotion.

It was a kind of fanaticism and loyalty, refined to the bone, without any impurities.

Just like the most devout believer looking up at his only god.

Shen Li’s heart sank to the bottom in an instant.

She suddenly understood.

From beginning to end, there was no "lucky" scout, nor was there any "treasure map of the previous dynasty."

All of this was a setup.

A seamless setup directed by Xiao Cheng himself, keeping everyone in the dark!

He wasn't acting at all. He was truly "praying" and "waiting."

He was waiting for an opportunity!

A dead end that would force her and the four hundred soldiers into a desperate situation, leaving her no choice but to draw her sword and rebel! The perfect moment to let everyone experience the deepest despair, only for him to personally bestow "divine miracles" and hope!

He wasn't relying on luck at all; he was playing with human hearts!

The so-called water shortage, the so-called grain crisis—from the very beginning, it had all been within his calculations! He wanted to use this method to drive her to a dead end, to push her determination to take full control of this army to its peak, and then use a "miracle" he had manufactured himself to harvest everyone’s loyalty!

This underground river, this secret granary—they were not relics of the previous dynasty!

This was his trump card! It was a contingency he had prepared long before arriving in this barren land!

This was the first "delivery list" presented to him, their true master, by his intelligence network!

Shen Li’s gaze slowly moved away from the scout and landed on her husband, who was still enjoying the cheers of the crowd.

She felt a chill run through her entire body.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Previous Dynasty’s Grand Scholar
chapters.content:
That perfectly timed "miracle" completely turned the situation in Cangbei City around.

With sufficient water and grain, the morale of the prince’s mansion’s isolated army solidified as never before. Panic and despair were swept away, replaced by the relief of surviving a disaster and a high fighting spirit for the future.

The soldiers were full of energy. They repaired the collapsed courtyard walls, cleared the waist-high weeds in the garden, and even cleared a plot of land to sow the grain seeds they had brought, looking forward to harvesting a bit of green of their own in the cold northern winds.

Overnight, the entire dilapidated mansion gained a vibrant sense of life and a stable foundation.

Shen Li saw all of this, but there was no joy in her heart.

Her gaze would involuntarily fall upon the one hundred Black Armored soldiers.

Their discipline and execution were far superior to ordinary elites. Especially that "lucky" scout, who, after being "heavily rewarded" by Xiao Cheng, was promoted to a centurion, responsible for guarding the granary and the water source.

He was meticulous in his work, taciturn, and kept his emotions hidden. But whenever Shen Li saw him, she would remember that day, when he knelt before Xiao Cheng, the fanaticism and loyalty that flashed in his eyes—the kind that went deep into the marrow.

That was not the awe of a subordinate for a master.

That was a believer looking up at his god.

This thought pricked at Shen Li’s heart every moment. The more she observed, the more alarmed she became.

She discovered that it wasn't just that scout; all the Black Armored soldiers had the same thing hidden deep in their eyes when they looked at Xiao Cheng.

And Xiao Cheng, whom they worshipped as a god, had quickly returned to being that incompetent, pleasure-seeking, useless prince after the crisis was resolved.

"This won't do! This porridge isn't thick at all! And the rice isn't the new pearl rice offered as tribute from the capital! I can't drink this!"

"And this bed! Is this a bed? It's harder than the wooden planks in a death row cell! I want silk quilts! I want pillows stuffed with clouds!"

"Where are the people! Where have they all died? In such a huge mansion, there isn't even a maid to serve tea, pour water, or massage my shoulders! How is one supposed to live like this! Did the Emperor send me to a monk’s temple?"

His greatest joy every day was lying in the only room that had been cleaned properly, nitpicking at the air, complaining about the hardships of life in Cangbei, and using every word in his vocabulary to reminisce about the luxury of the capital.

Shen Li had always turned a deaf ear to his unreasonable tantrums.

She was busy enough that her feet barely touched the ground.

She quickly consolidated the four hundred troops in the mansion. She arranged for the most reliable Shen family soldiers to be responsible for internal security and granary defense, while the one hundred mysterious Black Armored soldiers were broken up and sent out as scouts, infiltrating, reconnoitering, and mapping day and night. An intelligence network covering the entire city of Cangbei and its surroundings was quietly spreading under her hands.

She had to seize the initiative; she had to have all variables under her control before Xiao Cheng’s next "performance."

She had no time to deal with the man who only knew how to throw tantrums in his room.

Until this day, when Xiao Cheng started making a scene again.

He complained that the mansion was too cold and lifeless, lacking any human warmth, and clamored to go to the city’s largest slave market to buy some maids.

This time, he was making an exceptionally loud scene.

First, he rolled on the ground, wailing about his bitter fate and claiming that no one in the entire world could be more miserable than he, a prince. Seeing that no one paid him any mind, he began a hunger strike. Whoever brought him food would be thrown out along with the bowl, while he muttered, "You just want to starve me to death! So you can usurp my princely estate! You insolent peasants!"

Shen Li felt as if her head were splitting from his incessant noise.

She did not fear marching into battle, but against this kind of shameless, thick-skinned rogue, she was truly at a loss.

She knew this man was a difficult scoundrel. If she did not satisfy him, he would use this most tedious and undignified method to turn the entire estate upside down, severely affecting the morale of her troops.

"Uncle Zhang, saddle the horses."

In the end, she compromised.

She stood up and cast a cold look at the room from which the wailing still emanated, her expression filled with disgust and murderous intent.

Rather than letting him affect the bigger picture within the estate, it would be better to take him out and find an excuse to make him shut up forever.

The slave market of Cangbei City was located in an open area in the south of the city. It was less of a market and more of a massive human dumping ground. The air was thick with a foul stench, a mixture of sweat, blood, excrement, and despair.

Ragged, sallow-faced slaves were locked in low wooden prisoner carts or crude pens. Rusty iron chains were locked around their necks, and their eyes were dull and lifeless.

Slave traders brandished their whips, shouting loudly to sell their "wares" to the scattered buyers.

"Come take a look! Strong, sturdy laborers, only half a bag of rice each! Buy them to clear land and farm, it’s a bargain!"

"Women who can cook and bear children, two for a bolt of cloth! Satisfaction guaranteed!"

Xiao Cheng was dressed in a luxurious brocade robe that looked completely out of place in the dilapidated surroundings, swinging a flamboyant white jade folding fan in his hand. With an unconcealed look of disdain and pickiness, he strolled slowly past row after row of prisoner carts, followed only by the expressionless Shen Li and two personal guards.

"This one is too ugly, pitch black; looking at him ruins my appetite."

"This one is too thin, a gust of wind could blow him away. What kind of work can he do? Buying him would just be a waste of my grain."

"Tsk, this one has too fierce a look. What if he loses his mind one day and tries to murder me?"

He was nitpicking and passing judgment, his haughty posture even more nauseating than the slave traders brandishing their whips.

Shen Li followed behind him, arms crossed, her face growing colder by the second.

Watching the slaves in the carts tremble and lower their heads as Xiao Cheng passed, she was reminded of the citizens of Great Zhou who had been captured by enemy forces on the battlefield.

A surge of intense killing intent welled up within her.

She truly wanted to pierce the throat of the man before her with a spear, right here, in front of everyone.

Just as she was on the verge of snapping, Xiao Cheng suddenly stopped. He halted in the most inconspicuous corner of the market, in front of a small, broken prisoner cart.

The cart sat alone, as if it had been forgotten for a long time. Only one person was locked inside.

A young woman.

The woman was covered in filth and dried blood, her long hair matted together, making it impossible to tell its original color. She was curled up in the corner of the cart, so thin she was nothing but skin and bones. The rags on her body could barely cover her, and she was extremely weak.

She did not move.

Seeming to sense someone approaching, she slowly raised her head.

The moment she saw the woman's face, even Shen Li couldn't help but be startled.

It was a face covered in grime and bloodstains, but those eyes were startlingly bright.

In those eyes, there was no numbness, no despair, no pleading, and not even hatred. There was only calmness, and a deep-seated, unyielding stubbornness and wisdom.

She met Xiao Cheng’s gaze calmly, without flinching.

A shrewd, middle-aged slave trader, who had been following from a distance, immediately hurried over with a face full of smiles the moment he saw Xiao Cheng stop. His sycophantic grin was enough to make one feel disgusted.

"Oh! Your Highness, you truly have a sharp eye!"

He pointed at the woman in the cart, spitting as he boasted.

"Don't look at her in this wretched state; she's a treasure! A true golden branch and jade leaf! Her name is Su Wan, the only daughter of the former dynasty's Grand Scholar, Su Zhe! You know Su Zhe, right? A man of immense learning, the most famous Grand Scholar of the previous dynasty! His daughter inherited his true mantle; since childhood, she has been well-versed in the classics and histories, and is proficient in the zither, chess, calligraphy, and painting! She is a true lady of quality, a talent among talents!"

"If it weren't for her father’s foolishness in getting involved in the former dynasty's treason case and being executed along with his entire family, how could a woman of her status end up in this godforsaken place?"

The daughter of the former Grand Scholar, Su Wan.

Shen Li frowned. She felt she had heard this name somewhere before.

Xiao Cheng stared at the woman in the cart. In those peach-blossom eyes of his, which usually appeared cowardly or foolish, a sharp, piercing glint—one that saw through everything—flashed, unnoticed by anyone else.

He smiled.

It was still the same devil-may-care, playboy expression, but he seemed greatly interested in the slave trader's words.

"Oh? The descendant of a fallen dynasty's 'femme fatale'?"

He walked around the cart, tapping the wooden bars with his white jade folding fan, producing a rhythmic *thump-thump* sound.

A frivolous, teasing smile played on his lips.

"Sounds like an interesting story."

He stopped, his gaze once again falling on Su Wan’s calm eyes.

Then, he suddenly smiled.

That smile was no longer merely teasing; it carried a deeper, colder meaning.

A look of knowing that made Shen Li feel uneasy from the bottom of her heart.

chapters.title: This Prince Likes This Kind
chapters.content:
That smile set off alarm bells in the deepest part of Shen Li’s heart.

It was no longer simple mockery, nor was it a pretense of stupidity.

It was the certainty of a predator seeing its prey fall into a trap; it was the confidence of a chess player placing a decisive piece.

This man had been aiming for this woman named Su Wan from the very beginning.

Buying a maid, the estate being too quiet—it was all just an excuse.

His true goal was to take this daughter of a disgraced former official into his own hands.

"Oh? The descendant of that former Grand Scholar?"

Xiao Cheng swung his white jade folding fan, took a step forward, and pointed the tip of the fan vaguely at Su Wan in the cart, his tone as frivolous as if he were discussing a rare piece of merchandise.

"You sound like a treasure. This Prince likes women with stories." He scanned the crowd of onlookers and deliberately raised his voice. "How about this? I’ll give you a chance. If you can answer one question for me, I will give you a chance to live."

He paused, a teasing smile on his face, and slowly posed the question that sounded utterly absurd to outsiders.

"Since you are a talented woman, let me test you: how can one force the Ma family, who are acting so arrogantly at the city gates, to willingly hand over all their assets without using a single soldier?"

As soon as these words were spoken, a burst of irrepressible, uproarious laughter erupted from the crowd.

"Haha, did I hear that right? Is this prince a fool? Asking a dying slave girl how to deal with Ma Wanshan?"

"The Ma family are the local tyrants of Cangbei, with thousands of private soldiers under their command. He says 'without using a single soldier'? Is he dreaming?"

"I think he just wants an excuse to flirt with the woman! These nobles from the capital have so many tricks!"

Jeers and mockery rose one after another. Even the sycophantic slave trader laughed along, treating it as nothing more than a bored noble’s pastime, not taking the question seriously at all.

Shen Li’s face was cold as frost.

She thought Xiao Cheng was absolutely insane. On the Ma family’s turf, asking such a question in front of so many people not only completely exposed his hostility toward the Ma family but also placed himself in a foolish, ridiculous position, open to ridicule.

Just then, amidst the commotion, a hoarse but exceptionally clear voice pierced through the noise and sounded calmly.

"Attack the heart first."

In the prisoner cart, Su Wan slowly raised her head. Her bright eyes, peering through the dirty, tangled hair and rusty wooden bars, landed precisely on Xiao Cheng’s face, as if everyone and everything else around them had ceased to exist.

The laughter stopped abruptly.

Everyone’s gaze subconsciously focused on the emaciated slave girl who looked as if she could be blown over by a gust of wind.

Su Wan ignored the crowd; she only looked at Xiao Cheng, as if this conversation existed only between the two of them.

"Ma Wanshan rose from the grassroots, starting out by smuggling salt and iron. He is greedy, suspicious, and a coward at heart," her voice remained hoarse, but every word was incredibly clear and resonant. "He appears to control Cangbei, but in reality, he is beset by internal and external troubles; he is already walking on thin ice."

"Internally, he has his younger brother, Ma Wanhai. This man is braver and fiercer than Ma Wanshan and holds great prestige among the Ma family’s private soldiers. He has achieved many military merits, but because of this, he has long been suspected and suppressed by Ma Wanshan, who stripped him of his military command. He is already deeply resentful."

"Externally, there is the Black Wind Stronghold in the north of the city. The leader of the Black Wind Stronghold, 'One-Eyed Dragon,' has a long-standing grudge against Ma Wanshan over a woman from their youth. For years, he has made constant provocations, only holding back and waiting for an opportunity to retaliate because his strength is slightly inferior."

Her words dissected the Ma family’s background with absolute clarity, shocking some of the local onlookers. These things were not secrets in Cangbei, but no one had ever been able to articulate them so precisely and thoroughly.

Su Wan paused, her eyes becoming sharp.

"Your Highness only needs to... forge a secret letter suggesting that Ma Wanhai is colluding with the Black Wind Stronghold to seize the position of the Ma family head from the inside out, and then arrange for this letter to be 'accidentally' intercepted by Ma Wanshan’s most trusted confidant."

"Given Ma Wanshan’s greed and suspicion, he will never investigate the truth. He will only believe that his brother has finally bared his fangs. The first thing he will do is strike first, using the most ruthless methods to eliminate this greatest threat to his power."

"At that point, the Ma family will inevitably fall into internal chaos. Driven to a dead end, Ma Wanhai will surely bring in the Black Wind Stronghold as reinforcements to fight Ma Wanshan. We need only sit on the mountain and watch the tigers fight. Once they are both severely weakened, the Princess Consort can then lead troops out under the name of 'suppressing the rebellion in the city,' and without shedding a drop of blood, you can wipe out both the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold—the two biggest tumors of Cangbei—in one fell swoop."

"At that time, their assets will naturally be yours, Your Highness."

Her words flowed like a stream, interlocking perfectly, with a logic so meticulous it was chilling.

The entire slave market fell into a deathly silence.

The onlookers who had been mocking just moments ago now stood with their mouths agape, staring blankly at the frail woman in the prisoner transport cart as if they had seen a ghost.

Such a vicious scheme—how could a mere prisoner have conceived it? This was clearly a lethal trap that could only be laid by a master strategist who had spent years steeped in the arts of power.

Shen Li felt a sense of profound shock.

Having spent ten years on the battlefield, she excelled in overt tactics—the head-on clashes of vast armies. She felt an instinctive disgust and disdain for these hidden, underhanded schemes that exploited the weaknesses of the human heart.

Yet, she had to admit that this woman’s strategy was insidious, yet every move was fatal, striking directly at the most vulnerable parts of the human spirit.

It was a hundred times more brilliant than her own approach of drawing a sword to fight the Ma family head-on.

"Haha... Hahahaha!"

Xiao Cheng suddenly burst into loud laughter. He snapped his white jade folding fan shut with a "clack" and pointed at Su Wan in the cart, his face filled with undisguised admiration and wild delight.

"Good! A truly excellent strategy of attacking the heart! A brilliant way to kill two birds with one stone!"

He turned abruptly to look at the slave trader, who was now stunned into silence, and said in an indisputable tone, "I want this woman."

"Name your price."

The slave trader, as if jolted awake from a dream, rolled his eyes and immediately realized he had struck gold. He opened his mouth wide to demand an exorbitant sum: "Your Highness! This... this is a miraculous woman capable of pacifying the world! This price..."

"Fifty taels of gold."

Xiao Cheng cut off his rambling, pulled a heavy money bag from his robes, and tossed it onto the ground.

The bag hit the dirt with a dull thud. The opening loosened, and several gleaming gold ingots rolled out, shimmering in the dim light of the market.

Fifty taels of gold!

At this price, let alone buying one scrawny, half-dead female slave, one could easily purchase half the slaves in this entire market!

A spendthrift! A complete and utter spendthrift!

"Enough! Enough! More than enough!" The slave trader scrambled onto the ground, clutching the gold to his chest like a dog, nodding his head like a pestle pounding garlic.

"Wait."

At that moment, Shen Li’s icy voice rang out.

She stepped forward, blocking Xiao Cheng’s path, and glared at him.

"Your Highness is certainly generous," she said, enunciating every word. "Do you know that these fifty taels of gold are enough to feed four hundred soldiers for half a month?"

"You are using the money meant for military provisions—money I obtained by selling my dowry—to buy a woman of unknown origin who does nothing but stir up trouble?"

That day, to trade for grain, she had exhausted all her private assets. Where these fifty taels of gold came from went without saying. It was the last of her dowry, the military funds she had reserved for the most critical moment!

The smile on Xiao Cheng’s face stiffened slightly.

Then, as if he had heard the greatest joke in the world, he laughed until he doubled over.

He leaned in close to her, lowering his voice so that only the two of them could hear, and whispered.

"Princess, have you forgotten?"

"From the moment your dowry was carried into the Prince's Mansion, it became mine."

"Is there a problem with me using my own money to buy my own things?"

These words were like a red-hot branding iron, searing deep into Shen Li’s heart.

All her anger, all her questioning, dissolved into a pale sense of powerlessness at that moment.

Yes, in this world, a married daughter is like spilled water. Everything she had belonged to her husband.

Even if he was a good-for-nothing.

Shen Li closed her eyes. When she opened them again, there was no emotion left, only a chilling void.

She said nothing more, watching indifferently as the greedy slave trader fumbled with the locks of the cart and dragged the frail woman out of the filthy cage like a dead dog.

"Take her. We’re returning to the mansion."

Xiao Cheng shook his fan with satisfaction. Without so much as a glance at Shen Li, he turned and walked away, as if everything that had just happened had nothing to do with him.

Two personal guards stepped forward, one on each side, hoisting up the barely standing Su Wan and following him in silence.

From beginning to end, Su Wan did not say another word. Her gaze swept calmly over the dazzling gold ingots on the ground, then over Shen Li’s face, which was cold with humiliation, and finally landed on Xiao Cheng’s back—a back that appeared carefree but was, in reality, filled with calculation.

For the first time, a flicker of complex emotion crossed those bright eyes.

Shen Li did not follow immediately.

She stood in place, watching the three figures gradually recede into the distance.

One was her husband in name, a man she found increasingly unfathomable.

The other was a woman who had just won a new lease on life through wit and ruthlessness.

They... seemed to be of the same kind.

And she, a mere warrior who only knew how to wield a blade, felt like an ill-fitting intruder in this world built on schemes and calculations.

An unprecedented sense of unease and vigilance surged within her.

This woman named Su Wan was definitely not as simple as she appeared on the surface.

Keeping her in the mansion, by Xiao Cheng’s side—she did not know if it would be a blessing or a curse.

chapters.title: Dual Strategies of Yin and Yang
chapters.content:
Inside the Prince's Mansion, the atmosphere had become strange due to the arrival of one woman.

The woman named Su Wan was not treated as a slave or a servant. She was placed directly in the main courtyard of the mansion, in a guest room next to Xiao Cheng’s, which had been cleaned to the highest standard. Hot water, clean clothing, and high-quality medicine were all provided; her treatment was even better than that of the accompanying officials.

This special honor was seen by everyone, sparking endless discussion.

"A woman bought from a slave market—what is the Prince trying to do?"

"Didn't you see at the market? That woman opened her mouth and stripped the Ma family bare! She’s got real talent!"

"Talent? I think it’s demonic! Look at her eyes—they’re eerily bright; she doesn't look like a good person. The Princess letting her into the house is like inviting a wolf into the fold!"

The soldiers' whispers reached Shen Li’s ears, word for word.

She ignored them.

She sat alone on the stone steps of the training ground, wiping her bright silver spear—the weapon that had earned her so much face at the city gates—over and over again. The spear shaft was cold, just like her mood.

Uncle Zhang walked over to her with a bowl of ginger soup, his face etched with deep worry.

"Young Lady, drink some hot soup to warm yourself." He paused, then couldn't help but add, "That Su Wan... the Prince invited her directly into his study, and she has been in there for nearly an hour."

"Young Lady, this woman is deep and treacherous, certainly not a good sort. Keeping her by the Prince's side is likely... a disaster."

Shen Li’s hand, as she wiped the spear, paused for a moment.

She knew, of course, that Su Wan was no saint. A woman who could calmly analyze a situation in the face of death and offer a lethal scheme to trade for her life must possess a heart of immense resilience and ruthlessness.

She loathed such people.

What made her even more restless was Xiao Cheng’s attitude.

Since returning from the slave market, he had been uncharacteristically quiet. He no longer cried or threw tantrums; he spent his days locked in his study, seeing no one, claiming he needed to "reflect," as if he were troubled by some monumental matter.

And now, he had summoned that woman alone.

Shen Li put down the spear and stood up.

"I’ll go take a look."

She didn't know if she wanted to see what tricks that woman was planning, or if she wanted to see what clumsy act her "good husband" was about to perform.

The door to the study was ajar, casting a warm glow of candlelight.

Shen Li’s footsteps were light; when she reached the door, the people inside were unaware of her presence.

She hadn't intended to eavesdrop; she simply wanted to push the door open and interrupt the secret talk between two people she disliked. But just as her hand was about to touch the door panel, the conversation from within made her freeze in place.

"Su Wan, a commoner, pays her respects to Your Highness. Thank you for saving my life."

It was Su Wan’s voice. It was still hoarse, but clearer than it had been at the market, and carried a calm, neither humble nor arrogant tone.

"No need for formalities."

Another voice spoke.

Shen Li’s heart gave a violent jolt.

That voice was steady, deep, and carried a sense of composure and wisdom that seemed to see through everything.

It was Xiao Cheng’s voice.

Yet, it was completely unlike the Xiao Cheng she knew—the one who only knew how to weep and wail in front of her!

Shen Li subconsciously held her breath and pressed her ear against the crack in the door.

Inside the room, sandalwood incense for calming the spirit was burning.

Xiao Cheng was not lying on the couch or rolling on the floor as he usually did; he was sitting upright behind his desk. The gaudy, impractical brocade robe he usually wore had been replaced by a simple black gown.

His handsome face, which always wore an expression of foolishness or frivolity, was now devoid of any emotion. His eyes were deep and sharp, stripped of all pretense. His entire aura had undergone a earth-shattering change.

His presence had shifted from being flighty and unstable to deep and unfathomable.

Su Wan had bathed and changed into a simple, elegant cyan dress. Her face, washed clean of grime, was stunningly beautiful, and her bright eyes held a calmness that mirrored his own.

She did not seem surprised by Xiao Cheng’s transformation at all.

"What you said at the slave market was good," Xiao Cheng said, getting straight to the point, his fingers tapping lightly on the desk. "But it is not enough."

Su Wan bowed slightly: "Please, Your Highness, enlighten me."

"Your strategy can only resolve a temporary crisis; it cannot solve the dangers of a lifetime," Xiao Cheng’s voice was devoid of emotion. "Even if the Ma family falls, there will be the Li family, the Wang family. This land of Cangbei is a place of harsh terrain and fierce customs; relying solely on fighting and killing will not allow us to gain a firm foothold."

"Currently, we have no grain inside and no reinforcements outside. We may have established some authority at the city gates, but in reality, we are already surrounded by enemies. I ask you, how do we break this deadlock?"

These words were clear, logical, and far-sighted—where was there any trace of the good-for-nothing he had been?

Outside the door, Shen Li’s mind was shaken to its core.

For the first time, a look of admiration appeared on Su Wan’s face. She spoke slowly, offering the strategy of "pacifying the interior and resisting the exterior" that she had already prepared.

"Your Highness is absolutely right. In my humble opinion, to break this deadlock, we must act on two fronts."

"First, to pacify the interior."

"To deal with the Ma family, one cannot use brute force; one must use wisdom. What I said at the market was merely the beginning; the actual implementation requires much more careful planning."

"We need to forge two letters. The first, written by Ma Wanhai to 'One-Eyed Dragon,' the leader of the Black Wind Stronghold, will bitterly denounce his brother’s suspicion and injustice. In it, he will express his willingness to work with the Black Wind Stronghold from within to seize the Ma family, promising that once successful, he will hand over half of the family's assets and the women who were abducted years ago."

"The second letter will be the reply from 'One-Eyed Dragon,' setting a date three days hence to act in unison, using the smoke signal from the beacon tower west of the city as the sign."

"This second letter is the key. We must find a way to make it 'accidentally' fall into Ma Wanshan’s hands."

"Given Ma Wanshan’s greed and suspicious nature, once he sees the contents, he will not doubt their authenticity. The three-day deadline will leave him no time to investigate. The only thing he will do is strike first to gain the advantage, secretly executing his own brother before the appointed day arrives!"

"As for us, we need only send someone to the western beacon tower on the third day to light the signal fire."

"At that moment, Ma Wanhai’s remnants, pushed to the brink, will think the Black Wind Stronghold has acted early and will launch a desperate counterattack. The Black Wind Stronghold, seeing the smoke, will believe Ma Wanhai has already succeeded and will swarm into the city to seize the spoils of victory. Ma Wanshan, seeing the smoke, will be even more convinced that his brother’s plot has succeeded and will lead all his private troops in a frantic counter-offensive."

"A three-way melee, fighting to the death. When that happens, the Princess Consort can then lead the Prince’s elite forces, under the guise of 'suppressing the rebellion and protecting the city’s people,' and intervene with thunderous force. She will be able to wipe out all three factions in one fell swoop and take control of everything in Cangbei with full legitimacy."

This strategy was even more sinister, vicious, and seamless than what had been discussed at the slave market.

It calculated everyone into the scheme, even turning Shen Li and her troops into the sharpest blade in the plan.

Outside the door, Shen Li felt a chill run through her entire body.

The thing she hated most in her life was this kind of conspiracy hidden in the shadows. In her view, a true man should act openly and honorably, facing enemies head-on in the field of battle.

Yet, she had to admit that this woman’s strategy was a hundred times more brilliant than her own idea of just taking a blade to kill Ma Wanshan.

Inside the room, Xiao Cheng listened without a change in expression, merely asking noncommittally, "This handles internal affairs, but what of external ones?"

In Su Wan’s eyes, a light of confidence and composure flickered.

"Dealing with external threats does not mean going to war with the Northern Barbarians, but utilizing them."

"As far as this commoner knows, the Northern Barbarians are not a monolith. Besides the 'Golden Wolf' tribe, which has been a perennial enemy of the Great Zhou, there is a smaller, weaker tribe called the 'Snow Eagle' three hundred miles north of Cangbei."

"The Snow Eagle tribe is frequently oppressed by the Golden Wolf tribe and struggles to survive. What they lack is not warriors, but grain and ironware. And we have grain, we have iron, and what we lack are warhorses and intelligence."

"Your Highness can send men to secretly contact the Snow Eagle tribe. Use our surplus grain to trade for their warhorses and all intelligence regarding the Golden Wolf tribe. We can even provide them with weapons to support their resistance against the Golden Wolf tribe."

"In this way, not only can we rapidly build a cavalry of our own, but we can also make the Northern Barbarians fight the Northern Barbarians, causing them to exhaust themselves with internal strife, leaving them no time to look south. We can watch the fire from across the river, reap the benefits, and buy the most precious time for Your Highness’s true rise in Cangbei."

The two strategies—"securing the interior" and "dealing with the exterior"—one internal and one external, one yin and one yang, seemed to firmly grasp the future of all Cangbei.

The study fell into a long silence.

Xiao Cheng looked at this woman, who, though frail, seemed to hold the entire world in her eyes, and finally, he nodded slowly.

"Good," he said, just one word.

"These two strategies, I approve."

Outside the door, Shen Li’s heart sank, bit by bit.

She finally understood what his knowing smile at the slave market that day had meant.

So, he had known Su Wan’s value all along. What he had bought for fifty taels of gold was not a slave, but a top-tier strategist capable of securing his nation and stabilizing his reign!

They were people of the same world.

A world composed of conspiracies, calculations, power plays, and intellect—a world she could never step into, and one she even disdained to enter.

And what of herself?

What was she?

A tool—someone he would only mock as a "blank sheet of paper," someone fit only to clear the path for him with brute force, serving as the sharpest and most ignorant butcher’s knife in his grand plan?

All her pride, her honorable convictions forged in blood and glory on the battlefield, seemed at this moment to have become a joke.

An unprecedented sense of humiliation and alienation surged in her heart.

She felt like an outsider, a redundant person.

Shen Li did not listen any further.

She turned around, silently.

The wind of the north blew against her face, cold and painful.

But no matter how painful, it could not compare to the coldness in her heart, of being completely shut out. She looked at the sword at her waist, which had never been tainted by conspiracy, and for the first time, her faith in the path she had steadfastly followed began to waver.

chapters.title: A Strategy of Open Intent as the Blade, Conspiracy as the Scabbard
chapters.content:
Ever since that night, after hearing the heart-stopping conspiracy outside the study, Shen Li had fallen into complete silence.

She no longer questioned Xiao Cheng, nor did she attempt to interfere with his dealings with Su Wan. She was like a dormant beast, training her soldiers with a near-masochistic intensity. On the training grounds, the clashing of blades and the exhausted gasps of the soldiers rang out from dawn until deep into the night, never ceasing.

She was accumulating strength, and she was waiting.

Waiting for the bloody massacre that would be opened by this conspiracy, waiting for the moment she would be handed out as the sharpest blade.

On the morning of the third day, that moment arrived.

Xiao Cheng did the unexpected and "invited" both Shen Li and Su Wan to the study to "discuss matters."

This was the first time the three of them were truly in the same room together.

In the study, Su Wan stood quietly to the side. She had changed into clean clothes; though still frail, the wisdom and composure in her eyes gave her an aura that could not be underestimated.

As for Xiao Cheng, he had reverted to being the "useless" Prince. He sat restlessly, his face full of worry, as if the sky were about to collapse.

"Princess Consort... Su... Miss Su..." he stammered, his gaze shifting between the two women. "Miss Su’s strategy... I thought about it all night, and I keep feeling... is it not too sinister? It harms the harmony of heaven..."

As he spoke, he looked at Shen Li for agreement: "Princess Consort, you are a veteran of many battles, a person of honor, what do you think? Using such underhanded methods... if word gets out, won't people laugh at us?"

This performance was masterful.

He distanced himself completely, cleverly kicking the ball to Shen Li. It was as if adopting this poisonous plan was the ruthless choice of Shen Li, the "commander," and if she didn't adopt it, it meant she had no better way to break the deadlock.

Shen Li sneered inwardly, but her face remained calm.

She couldn't even be bothered to give the man a glance. She simply crossed her arms and coldly spat out five words: "Everything is as the Prince arranges."

She did not take the bait, nor did she argue.

These five words hit like a heavy punch into cotton, leaving all of Xiao Cheng’s prepared rhetoric about "benevolence and morality" stuck in his throat. He coughed awkwardly twice, and in the end, could only let out a long sigh, putting on a pained expression of being "forced into a corner."

"Fine! Fine! To survive, I... I shall be a villain for once!"

He turned to Su Wan, saying in a tone of disdain and impatience: "Do as you said! But... this matter must be done flawlessly! If there is the slightest mistake, I will hold you accountable first!"

"This commoner obeys," Su Wan bowed slightly, her face as calm as an ancient well.

The tacit performance finally came to an end.

That afternoon, two secret letters, forged by Su Wan herself to imitate different handwritings, were sent out by the Xuanjia Army’s top scouts.

One, a "plea for help" written by Ma Wanhai to the Black Wind Stronghold, was "accidentally" dropped on the path the Black Wind Stronghold must take to reach Cangbei City, where it was picked up by a minor leader of the stronghold.

The other, the forged "reply" from the Black Wind Stronghold to Ma Wanhai, was delivered to Ma Wanshan in an even more ingenious way.

A Xuanjia Army scout, disguised as one of Ma Wanshan’s trusted aides, snuck into the courtyard where Ma Wanhai was being held late at night. He "accidentally" dropped the letter in front of the guards and then fled in "panic." The guard dared not delay and immediately presented this "evidence of guilt" that had fallen from the sky to Ma Wanshan’s study.

At the same time, Shen Li received her first and only task in this grand play.

Using the excuse that "traces of bandits have been found around the Prince’s estate, threatening the water source," Xiao Cheng ordered her to lead three hundred of the Shen Family Army to the mountains thirty miles west of the city for "bandit suppression."

And that location happened to be the site of the Ma family’s largest private mine.

Shen Li said nothing. She took the order, which was practically written with the word "provocation," gathered her troops, and departed immediately.

Her actions were like a red-hot iron rod thrusting fiercely into a hornet’s nest.

Under the guise of "searching for bandits," the Shen Family Army arrogantly blockaded the entire mining area, driving out all the miners and managers to "thoroughly search" the mine shafts. They acted roughly, "accidentally" smashing smelting furnaces, "accidentally" collapsing newly dug tunnels, and even arresting several Ma family managers on the grounds of being "suspected accomplices of the bandits."

When the news reached the Ma estate, Ma Wanshan was so furious he smashed his favorite teacup on the spot!

However, before he could go to confront Shen Li, another event occurred that made his heart and gallbladder split with terror.

The secret letter from the Black Wind Stronghold to Ma Wanhai, presented by his trusted aide, lay on his desk.

In the letter, "One-Eyed Dragon" of the Black Wind Stronghold fully agreed to Ma Wanhai’s "cooperation," setting a date three days hence, using the smoke signal from the western beacon tower as the sign. One would act inside the city, the other would strike from outside, working in tandem to hack him, Ma Wanshan, into pieces and divide the Ma family together!

"Rebellion! Rebellion! That ungrateful dog!"

Ma Wanshan looked at the familiar, wild cursive handwriting of "One-Eyed Dragon" on the letter, along with his unique blood-handprint mark, and then thought of Shen Li currently "suppressing bandits" in his mining area...

He instantly "understood"!

This was all a trap!

It was his good brother, colluding with outsiders, and even roping in the new Prince’s estate, all to drive him to his death!

The three-day deadline was like a death warrant, leaving him absolutely no time to contemplate the flaws in the situation.

Given Ma Wanshan’s greed and suspicious nature, he could never trust his own brother. In his eyes, this younger brother, with his illustrious military record and considerable prestige among the troops, had long since become a grave threat!

"Come here!" A murderous glint flared in his eyes as he growled at his confidant outside the door. "Pass on my order: at the hour of the Rat tonight, you are to... clean house!"

He could not wait until the third day; he had to eliminate this internal threat completely before then!

That night, a bloody internal struggle erupted quietly within the Ma estate.

Ma Wanshan used a "family banquet" as a pretext, attempting to poison Ma Wanhai with tainted wine. But Ma Wanhai had long been on guard and struck back on the spot. The old troops loyal to him and Ma Wanshan’s henchmen engaged in a brutal slaughter within the residence.

For a time, the Ma estate was ablaze with fire, and the sounds of killing and screams echoed through the night sky.

Though Ma Wanhai was brave and fierce, he had, after all, been stripped of his military command and had only a few loyal followers by his side. Under Ma Wanshan’s relentless siege, he was eventually severely wounded. With a few remnants, he broke through the encirclement and fled frantically toward the outskirts of the city.

There was only one place he could think of as a path to survival—Black Wind Stronghold!

He had to find "One-Eyed Dragon." He needed to borrow troops; he needed to kill his way back and reclaim everything that belonged to him!

At that moment, Black Wind Stronghold was already in total chaos.

Just an hour earlier, one of their merchant caravans transporting looted goods had been completely wiped out by a group of masked men outside the city! The attackers were ruthless, every move lethal, and the leader had even deliberately left behind a Ma family waist token!

"Ma Wanshan! You have gone too far!"

"One-Eyed Dragon," the leader of Black Wind Stronghold, looked at his heavily wounded and dead brothers, his eyes splitting with rage. He and Ma Wanshan had a grudge over a stolen wife, and while there had been constant minor conflicts over the years, there had never been such a devastating loss!

Just as he was preparing to muster his men to fight the Ma family to the death, a minor leader presented him with a "plea for help" letter that had been "accidentally" found, written by Ma Wanhai.

The contents of the letter left "One-Eyed Dragon" stunned at first, then plunged into ecstasy!

An internal struggle in the Ma family? Ma Wanhai wanted to rebel? And he promised that once successful, he would return half the family fortune and the woman he had pined for for twenty years?!

"One-Eyed Dragon’s" greed instantly overwhelmed his reason.

He had been fretting over finding an excuse to move against the Ma family, and now, the opportunity had been delivered to his doorstep!

Just then, in the west of the city, a thick plume of wolf-smoke, mixed with the glow of fire, shot straight into the night sky!

That was... the agreed-upon signal!

"One-Eyed Dragon" had no more doubts! He assumed Ma Wanhai had already succeeded and had triggered the signal early!

"Brothers! Grab your weapons!" He drew the broadsword at his waist and shouted, "Ma Wanhai has already made his move! Charge into Cangbei City! Seize the money! Seize the grain! Seize the women!"

Inside the stronghold, thousands of fierce bandits, like a pack of wolves smelling blood, roared and surged madly toward Cangbei City!

In the west of the city, on the beacon tower, a scout of the Black Armored Army watched calmly as the bandits surged like a tide beneath the mountain. He glanced at the direction of the Ma estate, which had already descended into chaos, and sneered.

He tossed his torch into the pile of wolf dung and dry firewood that had been prepared in advance.

The mission was complete.

The three forces, like three blindfolded beasts, began the bloodiest and most insane mutual slaughter within the same trap.

Seeing the wolf-smoke, Ma Wanshan assumed the reinforcements from Black Wind Stronghold had arrived. He gathered all his private soldiers and set up a defensive line in the city, preparing to annihilate the invading enemy and the remaining "traitors" within the city in one fell swoop.

Ma Wanhai, having escaped the city, saw the wolf-smoke and assumed "One-Eyed Dragon" was responding to him. Excitedly, he led his remnants to meet the Black Wind Stronghold army, intending to join forces and launch a counterattack.

The Black Wind Stronghold, meanwhile, assumed the city gates were wide open and charged headlong into the inescapable net Ma Wanshan had laid out.

When Ma Wanhai’s remnants and the Black Wind Stronghold army "victoriously joined forces," both sides were bewildered.

Before they could even figure out the situation, Ma Wanshan’s army had already surrounded them from all sides.

A battle of extreme brutality erupted instantly.

The entire Cangbei City had completely devolved into a living hell.

Just then, the urgent sound of horns came from the direction of the Prince’s Mansion.

Shen Li stood on a temporarily erected command platform, dressed in military attire, holding a long spear, her expression as calm as water.

Before her stood three hundred Shen Family troops and one hundred Black Armored Army soldiers, who had been fully prepared and rested for three days.

Xiao Cheng came scrambling over, his face painted with a look of terror, his voice distorted by "fear."

"Princess! It’s bad! It’s terrible!"

"The Ma family and Black Wind Stronghold... they have colluded with Northern Barbarian spies and are... they are going to massacre the city!"

He shoved a "secret letter" into Shen Li’s hand—bearing a fake Northern Barbarian seal, obtained from who knows where—and, in a voice laced with tears, issued the order for which the script had long been written.

"Princess! This Prince... this Prince orders you! Lead the troops out immediately to quell the rebellion! Protect... protect the people of our Great Zhou!"

Shen Li took the ridiculous "evidence of crime" without even glancing at it.

Her icy gaze drifted past the man still performing his heart out and fixed on the district engulfed in flames.

A justified cause.

She slowly raised the bright silver spear in her hand, its tip shimmering with a chilling, lethal light in the firelight.

"All troops, advance!"

With the order given, the four hundred elites, like tigers descending a mountain, charged into the chaotic battlefield with the force of a thunderbolt.

chapters.title: Please Announce Yourself Before Entering My Study Next Time
chapters.content:
The smell of blood, mixed with the scent of charred wood and dust, hung over the entire sky of Cangbei City.

The slaughter had ended.

The once arrogant private soldiers of the Ma family and the notorious bandits of Black Wind Stronghold had now become cold corpses on the streets. The survivors had long since discarded their armor and weapons, kneeling on the ground, shivering under the cold blades of the Shen Family troops and the Black Armored Army.

Shen Li stood at the end of the long street. The blood on the tip of her bright silver spear was dripping, one drop at a time, into the small stream of blood forming at her feet.

She had won.

With four hundred elites facing thousands of chaotic troops, she had fought a miraculous battle of annihilation.

Behind her, the soldiers were high-spirited, cheering for victory.

Yet, there was no joy in her heart.

This victory did not belong to her.

It did not belong to the daughter of the General of the North who fought openly and honorably on the battlefield. It belonged to the man hiding deep within the Prince’s Mansion, weaving a net with human hearts and schemes.

She and the four hundred elite soldiers under her command were merely the butcher’s knives responsible for slaughtering the prey when the net tightened.

"General! The heads of Ma Wanshan and that One-Eyed Dragon have been taken!"

Uncle Zhang walked over quickly. His face was stained with blood, but his eyes revealed a sense of hearty excitement.

"All those who resisted have been executed on the spot! Those who surrendered have all been detained!"

Shen Li nodded, her voice devoid of any emotion.

"Count the casualties, clear the battlefield, confiscate the weapons and armor, and seal the treasury."

She issued the post-battle instructions with the briefest of commands, every word clear and calm.

"Yes!"

Uncle Zhang accepted the order and left.

In a single day, she had eradicated the two great tumors of Cangbei. This military achievement was enough to make any general famous.

But Shen Li only felt it was absurd.

She loathed this kind of victory. She loathed this dishonorable result gained through schemes and tricks. Yet, she had to admit that without it, they could never have so easily controlled this city in their desperate situation of lacking both men and supplies.

The result was good.

She could only use this phrase to numb herself.

She suppressed the churning nausea and discomfort in her heart, took off the heavy, blood-stained armor, and changed into clean, casual clothes.

She had to report back to Xiao Cheng.

This was the rule. No matter how much she despised him in her heart, in name, he remained the master of this city, her husband, and her Prince.

The night was deep, but the Prince’s Mansion was brightly lit.

The joy of victory had dispelled the oppression of the past few days. The soldiers cheered and jumped for joy before the distributed wine and meat, loudly praising the Princess’s bravery and the Prince’s "destiny to rule."

These sounds, reaching Shen Li’s ears, felt incredibly grating.

She avoided the noisy crowd and walked alone toward the study that represented the center of power.

She had walked this path many times.

But never had it felt as long as it did tonight.

She did not know if what awaited her was the good-for-nothing who only knew how to cry while clutching her leg, or the ambitious hero who pointed out the direction of the world with his strategists behind closed doors.

The study was near.

The door was left ajar, revealing warm candlelight and the faint sound of voices.

It was the voices of Xiao Cheng and that woman.

Shen Li’s footsteps subconsciously lightened. As if possessed, she walked to the door and looked inside through the narrow gap.

With just one glance, the blood in her entire body seemed to freeze instantly.

Inside the study, Xiao Cheng and Su Wan were standing side by side in front of a massive map of Cangbei.

Their heads were almost touching.

Xiao Cheng’s finger traced slowly across the map, from the private mines they had just seized from the Ma family, to the mountain peaks occupied by Black Wind Stronghold, and finally to the trade route leading to the Northern Barbarians.

On his face was a genuine, heartfelt smile that Shen Li had never seen before.

It was the appreciation of finding a kindred spirit, the confidence of someone in total control, and the high-spirited vigor of a king commanding the situation.

That smile was so bright it was somewhat blinding.

"The output of this mine far exceeds our estimates. Starting tomorrow, we can resume extraction. The iron obtained will be prioritized for forging weapons."

"The mountain pass occupied by Black Wind Stronghold is the throat of the route to the Northern Territory; it must be firmly under our control."

"And here..."

Every time he spoke, Su Wan would immediately follow up, using her clear, bright voice to supplement every detail.

"For weapon forging, the craftsmen need to be reorganized into an assembly line; efficiency can be increased by thirty percent."

"On the mountain pass, three beacon towers must be established, acting as mutual support to ensure the trade route is absolutely secure."

"Your Highness, this commoner believes the urgent priority is to win the hearts of the people. We can take half of the wealth gathered by the Ma family and Black Wind Stronghold, open the granaries, and provide disaster relief to the entire city..."

One pointed out the layout, the other perfected it.

One planned, the other refined.

Between them, there existed an invisible, tacit understanding, as if the grand strategy of the world could be clearly outlined in the few words they exchanged.

They were the ones who resembled a true monarch and his strategist—a true pair of companions capable of conspiring to conquer the world together.

And what of her?

What of her, who had just been fighting bloodily outside, clearing away every obstacle for them?

She was merely an outsider standing outside the door, not even qualified to participate in their conversation.

An uncontrollable rage, mixed with a bitterness and humiliation she hadn't even realized herself, surged violently to her head.

She did not hesitate again.

She raised her hand and pushed the door open with force.

"Creak—"

The harsh sound of the door hinges turning was like a sharp blade, slicing through the harmonious and tacit atmosphere within the study.

The two intimate figures before the map startled like frightened birds and abruptly pulled apart.

The smile on Xiao Cheng's face froze the instant he saw the cold countenance at the door. The genuine radiance in his eyes faded rapidly, replaced by a cold, detached indifference at being disturbed.

Su Wan took a step back, lowered her eyes, and bowed slightly toward Shen Li, masking all the emotions in her gaze.

Shen Li stood at the doorway, seemingly still carrying the lingering aura of slaughter.

She did not look at Su Wan; her gaze was fixed straight upon Xiao Cheng, and she began to report in a purely military tone, devoid of any emotion.

"Your Highness."

"The rebellion has been quelled. Ma Wanshan and 'One-Eyed Dragon' have been beheaded, and the remaining remnants have all been taken into custody."

"Please, Your Highness, give your orders!"

Her voice, in the quiet study, sounded exceptionally loud and exceptionally cold.

Xiao Cheng looked at her.

His gaze lingered for a moment on her face, which appeared all the more cold and beautiful due to her anger.

He offered no praise.

No comfort.

Not even the slightest hint of joy at her decisive victory.

He simply nodded calmly and slowly, as if what she had reported was nothing more than a trivial matter.

"The Princess has worked hard."

He spoke, his tone polite and flat.

Then, he paused, his gaze shifting from her to the door she had pushed open.

"But next time," he said, in a slower, clearer tone, enunciating every word, "please announce yourself before entering my study."

He said these words with an air of nonchalance.

Yet, every word was like a red-hot needle of ice, stabbing fiercely into Shen Li's heart.

*Worked hard?*

*Please announce yourself?*

She had fought through blood and gore to win this city for him, and in return, she received only this perfunctory, dismissive politeness and a warning laden with the intent to expel her?

In this moment, she seemed unable to even feel the sword wounds the enemy had inflicted upon her on the battlefield.

All the pain converged on that single point in her chest.

*Princess, my study is not a place you can enter at will!*

He had not said these words aloud.

But Shen Li heard them clearly.

So, from beginning to end, she had always been an outsider. An outsider who could charge into battle for him, but who could never step into his inner world.

An invisible wall rose up between them with a crash.

Shen Li stood where she was, motionless. She looked at the man who had turned his back to her again, as if she no longer existed. Her lips moved, but she could not utter a single word.

She had won the war.

But here, with him, she had lost everything.

chapters.title: The Princess Slaughters the City, Su Wan Attacks the Heart
chapters.content:
The air seemed to have solidified.

That phrase, "please announce yourself," stood like an invisible, icy wall between Shen Li and Xiao Cheng, completely isolating them into two different worlds.

She stood outside the door, the war-god Princess who had fought through blood.

He stood inside the door, the calculating emperor.

Though only a short distance apart, it was as if they were separated by a chasm.

Shen Li did not say another word. She did not even glance at the man with his back to her again. She simply turned around slowly and silently, pulling the door—which represented alienation and expulsion—shut behind her.

She did not return to her bedchamber.

She returned to the training ground, which smelled of rust and sweat.

Under the night sky, the empty field appeared exceptionally desolate. She stood in the center of the training ground, letting the cold northern night wind blow through her clean, everyday clothes, trying to blow away the humiliation and rage in her heart.

But she could not.

In her mind, Xiao Cheng’s polite and cold "you have worked hard" echoed repeatedly.

Repeatedly, the image of him and Su Wan standing side-by-side before the map, intimate and inseparable, surfaced.

They were the ones who were truly of the same kind.

And she was merely a convenient weapon. When needed, he would not hesitate to praise her as "sharp"; when not needed, she would be ruthlessly cast aside, not even granted the qualification to draw near.

Shen Li slowly closed her eyes.

She had been at war for ten years, seen the most vicious enemies, and suffered the most grievous wounds. She had never been afraid, nor had she ever retreated. Yet, at this moment, she felt an unprecedented exhaustion and chill.

She did not know how long she had been standing there when hurried footsteps approached from behind.

"General!"

It was Uncle Zhang. His face still bore the excitement of the aftermath of battle, but upon seeing Shen Li’s lonely figure, his voice involuntarily carried a trace of worry.

"You... why are you here alone?"

Shen Li did not turn back, only asking faintly, "What is it?"

"General, the battle results have been tallied. In this battle, our army lost twenty-seven men, with fifty-four severely wounded. Over thirteen hundred men from the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold were killed on the spot, and we have taken... nearly two thousand prisoners!"

When he said the word "prisoners," Uncle Zhang’s tone became grave.

"Additionally, a large number of family members were found in the residences of the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold—men, women, and children, totaling nearly a thousand. Currently, these surrendered soldiers and their families are all detained in the empty camp west of the city. How should they be handled? Please, General, give your orders!"

This was the most thorny issue after quelling a rebellion.

The disposal of thousands of people was enough to determine the future safety of Cangbei.

Shen Li slowly opened her eyes.

When she opened them again, only the iron-blooded resolve of the Northern General’s daughter remained.

Personal emotions must never influence a commander's judgment. This was the first lesson her father had taught her.

"Pass on my military order."

Her voice was as cold as ice in the frigid night.

"All leaders and managers among the surrendered soldiers, anyone who held a key position in the Ma family or the Black Wind Stronghold, are to be... executed on the spot. Hang their heads at the city gates as a warning to others!"

Uncle Zhang’s heart tightened, but he did not hesitate. "Yes!"

This was standard military practice: execute the ringleaders to intimidate the remnants.

"As for the remaining surrendered soldiers, anyone who has the blood debt of our Great Zhou citizens on their hands is to be executed as well!"

"The rest of the able-bodied men are to be conscripted as slaves and sent to the mines for hard labor until they die of old age!"

"As for those family members..." Shen Li paused, her expression calm, "The elderly, the weak, women, and children are all to be expelled from the territory and left to fend for themselves. We do not feed idlers, and we certainly do not feed the descendants of rebels!"

This order was ruthless, decisive, and left no future trouble.

This was the Shen family’s way of governing an army, and the iron rule of the Great Zhou military in dealing with rebels. If you cut the grass, you must remove the roots! Any shred of mercy would, in the future, become a blade pointed at one's own heart!

Uncle Zhang clasped his fists heavily. "This subordinate obeys!"

Just as he was about to turn to pass the order, a cold, clear voice drifted faintly from not far away.

"Your Highness, please reconsider."

Shen Li turned abruptly to see Su Wan standing gracefully at the entrance of the training ground. She was draped in a thick cloak that fluttered in the night wind, and her bright eyes shone like cold stars in the darkness.

"If this matter is handled according to the Princess's method, Cangbei will likely never know peace again."

Shen Li’s gaze instantly became as sharp as a blade.

What she detested most were these strategists who wagged their tongues behind people's backs.

"Are you questioning my military order?"

Su Wan bowed slightly, her posture humble, yet her tone neither servile nor overbearing. "This commoner would not dare. This commoner is merely speaking on the merits of the matter."

"The Princess's method is a method for governing an army; using it on the battlefield is beyond reproach. But we are not on the battlefield now; we are governing a city. Governing a city requires the way of governing a nation."

"The way of governing a nation?" Shen Li let out a cold laugh. "Then tell me, what is your way of governing a nation?"

"Attacking the heart is paramount."

Those four words again!

Shen Li’s rage could no longer be suppressed.
