"Enough!" she barked. "I am not that useless Prince who can be easily deceived by you! Put away your ghost stories meant to bewitch people! Let me tell you, the most effective way to deal with an enemy is to make them feel fear! Let them know that the consequence of betrayal is to die without a burial place!"

"Womanly benevolence only invites disaster!"

Facing Shen Li’s fury, Su Wan’s face remained as calm as water.

She simply looked at Shen Li quietly and spoke slowly.

"Does the Princess know how many of the two thousand surrendered soldiers are native-born people of Cangbei? Their kin and friends are scattered in every corner of this city. If you kill them, you make an enemy of the entire city."

"If you expel their wives, children, and elderly, the vast wilderness will immediately gain a thousand new deadly enemies who harbor a blood feud against us!"

"Princess, slaughter may indeed bring momentary fear. But fear can never buy loyalty. It will only act like a seed, burying hatred in everyone's heart, waiting for the moment to take root and sprout wildly, eventually consuming us completely!"

"You!" Shen Li was momentarily rendered speechless by her words.

Just then, the central figure of their argument appeared.

Xiao Cheng, wearing a thin sleeping robe and surrounded by a few servants, walked over, yawning incessantly. He rubbed his sleepy eyes and looked at the two confronting women with a blank expression.

"What... what are you arguing about in the middle of the night? Can't a person get any sleep?"

He complained first, then seemed to realize something, and asked with a "nervous" look, "Is it... is it about those prisoners? Did something happen?"

Shen Li kept a cold face and repeated her disposal plan in a stiff, blunt tone.

Xiao Cheng listened, his face turning "dead pale" with fright. He waved his hands repeatedly, saying, "Kill... kill so many people? Princess, this... is this really okay? It’s too cruel..."

Su Wan immediately stepped forward and laid out her own "strategy to win hearts" in full.

"...In this commoner's opinion, a policy of benevolence should be adopted. Tomorrow, we can hold a public trial in the city square. We need only execute the ringleaders who have committed heinous crimes and incited great public outrage in front of everyone to appease the people."

"Afterward, we announce that the assets confiscated from the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold will be distributed to the townspeople who have been oppressed by them for years, as well as to the families of the surrendered soldiers, allowing the entire city to share in this victory."

"Finally, we announce that any surrendered soldiers willing to swear allegiance to the Prince’s estate may retain their original rank and even receive better rations and pay than before, so that they may serve you, my Prince!"

"In this way, not only will we avoid creating thousands of enemies, but we will also gain the support and loyalty of the entire city's military and civilians within a single day! My Prince, what you will gain is not just a city, but the hearts of tens of thousands of people who will follow you to the death!"

After listening, Xiao Cheng wore a look of "conflicted" distress on his face. He looked at Shen Li, then at Su Wan, pacing back and forth with a furrowed brow.

"The Princess makes a valid point; only by cutting the weeds and digging up the roots can we prevent future trouble..."

"But what Miss Su says also seems... also correct. Those who win the hearts of the people win the world, after all..."

His performance was so dedicated, so realistic.

Shen Li watched with cold eyes, feeling a wave of nausea. She knew he had already made his decision. This posturing was merely for her benefit, and for everyone else’s, to highlight the "benevolence" and "greatness" of his final choice.

Sure enough, after struggling "painfully" for a long time, Xiao Cheng stomped his foot, gritted his teeth, and made his final "decision."

"Enough! Heaven has the virtue of cherishing life, and this Prince... this Prince will trust Miss Su just this once! I will take the gamble!"

He looked at Shen Li and said in a tone that was almost pleading, "Princess, let’s... let’s do as Miss Su says, shall we? Consider it... I’m begging you..."

Shen Li looked at his face, which was plastered with "cowardice" and "benevolence," and found it incredibly ironic.

She did not argue further.

Because she knew that arguing was meaningless.

"Everything shall be as the Prince decides."

She squeezed these words out one by one, then turned and left without looking back.

She did not want to see those two figures, who cooperated so tacitly, for even a second longer.

The next day, the central square of Cangbei City was packed with people.

A temporarily constructed high platform stood in the center of the square. Thousands of surrendered soldiers and their families were held under the platform by soldiers, their faces ashen, awaiting the judgment of fate. The townspeople surrounded the area, watching everything nervously.

At the hour of the Horse (noon), the trial began.

Dozens of Ma family leaders and Black Wind Stronghold bandit chiefs, who had committed heinous crimes and acted like tyrants, were identified and beheaded in public!

As the heads rolled to the ground, a suppressed cheer erupted from the crowd!

However, just when everyone thought a bloody massacre would follow, a turning point occurred.

Su Wan walked onto the platform and, in the name of the Seventh Prince, announced the subsequent decisions.

When she announced that all the granaries and silver vaults of the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold would be distributed to all the people present, the entire square fell silent.

Immediately afterward, as carts filled with grain and copper coins were pushed into the square, the crowd went completely wild!

"Long live the Prince! The Prince is benevolent!"

"Heaven has eyes! We are saved!"

The people rushed forward like madmen. They knelt on the ground, kowtowing desperately toward the platform. Cries of weeping and gratitude echoed through the sky!

And when Su Wan announced that all surrendered soldiers willing to submit would not only be spared from death and slavery but could join the Prince’s army and receive double rations, the thousands of soldiers who had been in despair completely broke down!

They could not believe their ears.

After a brief moment of stupor, one soldier threw down his weapon, was the first to kneel, and wailed toward the platform.

"I am willing to surrender! I am willing to die for the Prince!!"

One, two, a hundred...

In an instant, a sea of people knelt before the platform! Those thousands of soldiers, who were fierce bandits just moments ago, were now all crying like children, using every ounce of their strength to swear their allegiance toward the platform.

The roar of allegiance, like a mountain of sound, surged into every corner of the city.

Shen Li stood on a pavilion not far away.

She watched the fanatical scene in the square coldly. She looked at Xiao Cheng on the platform, wearing a "benevolent" smile as he accepted the worship of thousands, and Su Wan beside him, looking calm and confident.

They were bathed in the adoration and gratitude of the masses, like a match made in heaven.

And her iron-blooded principles, the strict military laws she had forged with blood and life, seemed so pale and so... ridiculous in this moment, amidst the deafening cheers.

For the first time, she felt doubt toward the beliefs she had held for half her life.

chapters.title: Monopolizing the Economy of Cangbei
chapters.content:
That grand public trial ended with a scene of almost fanatical adoration from the masses.

The cry of "The Prince is benevolent" echoed through the streets and alleys of Cangbei City for the next several days. The people, who had once been crushed by the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold, now that they had received grain and money, spontaneously set up longevity tablets for the Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, burning incense day and night to sing his praises.

Overnight, the Prince’s estate became the undisputed center of faith in this city.

However, beneath this flourishing facade, a silent crisis had quietly arrived.

Inside the Prince’s study.

The atmosphere in the study was extremely oppressive.

Xiao Cheng no longer played the role of the submissive wastrel. He had changed into dark casual robes, sitting in the main seat with a face as calm as water, his fingers tapping on the table rhythmically.

In front of him lay a ledger that had just been submitted.

"Speak, how much is left in the treasury?" his voice was cold.

At the lower end, Uncle Zhang, who was in charge of money and grain, had a fine layer of cold sweat on his forehead. He bowed his body, his voice dry.

"Replying... replying to the Prince. Since the day we opened the granaries to distribute grain and gave away the wealth, we have already... already spent seventy percent of the silver confiscated from the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold."

"The remaining thirty percent, plus the military supplies brought by the Princess, must support nearly a thousand soldiers in the city, as well as the expenses of the entire Prince’s estate... If there is no new income, we can... we can only last for half a month at most."

Half a month.

This number was like a giant rock, weighing heavily on everyone's heart.

The seemingly glorious Prince’s estate was actually on the verge of exhaustion. They had won the hearts of the people, but they had lost the foundation upon which they relied for survival.

Su Wan, standing to the side, frowned slightly and interjected: "It is not just that. This commoner has discovered that since the public trial, the prices of all necessities such as rice, salt, cloth, and iron in the city have been skyrocketing at an abnormal rate. In just three days, the prices have nearly doubled."

"The money and grain that the people just received have been swallowed up by the high prices in the blink of an eye. Now, there are complaints everywhere in the city."

"It is the Merchant Alliance."

Shen Li, who had been standing in the corner like an outsider, spoke coldly.

Ever since she witnessed that "heart-winning" drama from the pavilion that day, she had not taken the initiative to say a word to Xiao Cheng or Su Wan. She was merely fulfilling her duties as the Princess.

"In Cangbei City, there are seven major merchant firms that have dealt in salt, iron, rice, and grain for generations, controlling over ninety percent of the local economy. They have formed an alliance, acting in concert. When the Ma family was here, they were submissive; now that the Ma family has fallen, they believe they can become the new masters of this city."

"They are... forcing our hand."

Su Wan’s eyes sharpened.

"On the surface, they are respectful to the Prince’s estate, sending gifts and congratulations without fail. In secret, however, they have joined forces to raise prices, attempting to hollow out the Prince’s authority in this way. They have calculated that our treasury is empty and we lack the power to regulate prices, hoping to force us to bow to them and ultimately seize the actual control of Cangbei from our hands."

"A bunch of insatiable wolves!" Uncle Zhang cursed bitterly. "My Prince, I request permission to lead troops to seal them up! I don't believe they would dare to be so presumptuous in the face of our blades!"

Xiao Cheng did not speak; he simply cast his gaze toward Su Wan.

Su Wan shook her head gently: "No. We have just won the hearts of the people with 'benevolence and righteousness.' If we strike at the merchants without solid evidence, it will only cause all our previous efforts to go to waste. It will also confirm our reputation as an evil foreign power, causing the entire city's people to turn against us."

"Then what should we do?" Xiao Cheng showed a perfectly timed look of "anxiety." "Are we just going to watch them wear us down to death?"

Su Wan smiled confidently.

"Instead of pulling the firewood from under the cauldron, why don't... we become the firewood ourselves?"

She stepped forward, her voice clear.

"This commoner has a plan. We can imitate the Datong Bank of the capital and, using the reputation of the Prince’s estate as an endorsement, establish the 'Cangbei Chamber of Commerce.'"

"Anyone who joins can receive credit notes issued by the Prince’s estate. With these notes, they can freely exchange for supplies and money within the Chamber of Commerce. If we control the issuance of the notes, we control the purse strings of Cangbei."

"At the same time, the Prince’s estate will step forward to coordinate all supplies in the city and stabilize prices. Most importantly, we promise all merchants that we will use the power of the Prince’s estate to open up a safe trade route with the Northern Barbarian tribes."

"The cattle, sheep, furs, and warhorses of the Northern Barbarians are hard currency that is highly sought after in the Great Zhou. And our grain, ironware, and cloth are life-saving supplies for them. Once this trade route is opened, the profits will be more than tenfold. Facing such huge interests, I do not believe they will remain unmoved."

This plan was undeniably tempting.

It struck precisely at the lifeline of the merchants—profit.

However, after listening, Shen Li only felt a cold sneer in her heart.

Another one of these ethereal castles in the air. Using a bounced check to paint a massive pie. Would these cunning, old merchants believe it?

Sure enough, three days later, the recruitment notices of the Prince’s estate were plastered all over the streets and alleys of Cangbei.

Xiao Cheng personally stepped forward to host a banquet for the heads of the seven major merchant firms at the largest restaurant in the city.

At the banquet, Xiao Cheng announced his plan to establish the "Cangbei Chamber of Commerce" with a beaming face, warmly inviting the seven guild masters to become the chamber's founding elders.

The seven masters were led by a gaunt old man with the nickname "Old Man Qian the Scraper." After hearing Xiao Cheng’s plan, they wore respectful smiles and uttered flattering words about the "Prince’s far-sightedness," yet their eyes were filled with contempt and mockery.

"Your Highness, your idea is good," Old Man Qian said, stroking his goatee with a smirk. "However, these notes... to put it bluntly, aren't they just pieces of paper? We businessmen deal in real gold and silver. This paper, I’m afraid, won't be of much use."

Another fat guild master immediately chimed in, "That’s right, Your Highness! And that Northern Barbarian trade route is extremely dangerous. The Northern Barbarians are savages who drink blood and eat raw meat; they have no sense of honor. Doing business with them is like putting your head on the chopping block! We cannot afford such a risk."

"Our small businesses prefer the security of cold, hard cash."

"We appreciate your good intentions, Your Highness."

They echoed each other, using soft yet firm words to reject Xiao Cheng’s proposal directly.

In their eyes, this useless Prince, who only knew how to squander wealth to buy a reputation, had reached the end of his rope. He actually thought he could use a piece of paper to swindle away the gold and silver they had spent half a lifetime accumulating? It was a colossal joke!

The banquet ended on a sour note.

The next day, prices in the city rose even more sharply.

The Merchant Alliance used the most direct action to express their disdain for the Prince’s Mansion. They wanted to tell Xiao Cheng that in Cangbei, money was more effective than power.

Inside the Prince’s Mansion, the atmosphere was gloomy.

Even the surrendered soldiers who had just pledged their loyalty began to waver.

Everyone believed that this time, the Prince was truly out of options.

That night, Xiao Cheng summoned everyone for a meeting once again. He looked utterly decadent, even pointing at Su Wan’s nose and flying into a rage in front of everyone.

"This is your brilliant plan?! Look at this now! The whole city is laughing at me! You’ve made me lose all face!"

Su Wan kept her head down, silent, letting him vent his anger.

After his outburst, Xiao Cheng slumped into his chair, as if all his strength had been drained. He looked at the woman who had been watching coldly from the sidelines with a gaze of near-despair.

"Princess..."

His voice was choked with tears, reverting to the familiar "useless" persona.

"Did I... did I make a mistake? They... they are all bullying me..."

Shen Li looked at him without speaking.

"Princess, tell me... are these people just like the Ma family, all bad guys?" Xiao Cheng asked pitifully, wiping away non-existent tears with his sleeve. "I heard... that old man named Qian was closest to Ma Wanshan... could they... could they also be hiding weapons, wanting to... wanting to rebel like the Ma family?"

This sentence was like a bolt of lightning, piercing through the fog in Shen Li’s heart.

She suddenly raised her head and looked at Xiao Cheng’s tear-streaked face.

She understood in an instant.

When an overt strategy failed, it was time for a covert one to take the stage.

No.

This was not a covert strategy.

This was another way of using an overt one.

Su Wan’s "strategy of winning hearts" was the scabbard.

And the blade in Shen Li’s hand was the true edge!

Using a gentle scabbard to package the sharpest blade—this was their true plan!

They needed an excuse. An excuse for her, the blade, to be unsheathed legitimately to cut down all obstacles!

And now, Xiao Cheng had personally handed that excuse to her.

"Suppress the remnants of the Ma family, search for hidden weaponry, and maintain the peace of Cangbei City."

This reason was righteous, open, and beyond reproach.

In Shen Li’s heart, the usual repulsion and disgust were gone, replaced by a cold, near-cruel calm.

She looked at the "weeping" Xiao Cheng and slowly nodded.

"Rest assured, Your Highness."

Her voice was calm.

"With me here, no one in Cangbei shall dare to plot rebellion."

As soon as she finished speaking, she turned and left, her military uniform emitting a cold, metallic luster under the candlelight.

Xiao Cheng’s "sobbing" stopped abruptly.

He looked up at Shen Li’s resolute back and exchanged a knowing glance with Su Wan beside him.

Midnight.

Cangbei City had long since fallen into a deep sleep.

Suddenly, the sound of rhythmic, heavy footsteps shattered the silence of the night!

Shen Li, clad in silver armor and holding a long spear, personally led four hundred fully armed elite soldiers, appearing on the city’s most prosperous commercial street like a ghost troop descended from the heavens!

They moved with speed and discipline, immediately sealing off every intersection.

"By order of the Prince! Thoroughly search for remnants of the Ma family; anyone found harboring them will be treated as an accomplice!"

The cold command echoed throughout the long street in the quiet night.

The next moment, the heavy, vermilion wooden doors of the Qian family’s firm were smashed to pieces by soldiers using a battering ram with a thunderous "boom"!

The soldiers charged in like wolves and tigers!

Old Man Qian, still in his dreams, was startled awake. He scrambled out in his undergarments, and upon seeing the scene before him, he was terrified out of his wits.

"Yo... Your Highness the Princess! What are you doing?! I... I am a law-abiding citizen!"

Shen Li sat on her horse, looking down at him, her eyes colder than a blade’s edge.

"Search!"

She uttered only one word.

The soldiers immediately rushed into the warehouse in the backyard. A moment later, an officer rushed out holding a long saber, reporting loudly.

"Reporting to the Princess! In the false wall of the Qian family’s warehouse, we found hidden contraband: fifty Mo-dao sabers and thirty heavy bows!"

"And this!" Another soldier presented a letter. "This is... this is a handwritten letter from Old Man Qian to Ma Wanshan! It says he intends to help him make a comeback!"

Both human and material evidence were "complete."

Old Man Qian looked at the letter he had never written and the weapons that had appeared from nowhere, his face turning ashen as he collapsed to the ground.

"I’m... I’m wronged..."

His defense was so feeble.

Shen Li gave him no chance at all.

"Take him!"

Two words passed the death sentence on the Qian family firm.

At the same time, the other six major firms received the same "courtesy."

"Hiding armor!"

"Communicating with foreign enemies!"

"Attempting to assassinate the Prince!"

One trumped-up charge after another, accompanied by "evidence" that had been prepared long ago, was quickly "discovered."

The gentleness of the overt strategy was torn to shreds at this moment. What emerged were the naked, violent fangs of a conspiracy.

By daybreak, the masters of the seven major firms had all been thrown into prison on charges of "treason." Their shops were all sealed.

When the news spread, the entire Cangbei business world was shaken to its core!

The remaining small and medium-sized merchants were terrified out of their wits. They finally understood that this Seventh Prince was no benevolent sheep. He was a tiger with the sharpest claws and teeth! Obey, and prosper; defy, and perish!

They no longer dared to harbor any wishful thinking.

Before the mid-morning hour, the area in front of the Prince’s Mansion was already packed with people kneeling.

All the merchants in the city, big and small, had come. They scrambled to kowtow, crying and begging, only asking to join the "Cangbei Chamber of Commerce," only asking to offer their loyalty to the Prince.

The chamber notes that had been treated like trash yesterday were now, in their eyes, life-saving talismans.

Inside the study, Xiao Cheng sipped his tea leisurely.

Su Wan stood by his side, refilling his cup with a faint smile on her face.

"Your Highness, the economic lifeline of Cangbei is now entirely in your hands."

Xiao Cheng set down his teacup and looked out the window at the crowd kneeling outside.

"No," he said slowly.

"It is entirely in our hands!"

At this moment, on the training grounds, Shen Li was wiping her long spear alone.

She had won.

Once again, she had cleared the obstacles for him in the way she knew best.

This victory, which she had personally executed and which was filled with framing and entrapment, left her feeling no joy at all.

The thunderous sounds of allegiance and the grateful cries of the commoners still echoed in her ears.

But her blade was stained.

chapters.title: The Prince of Ning Comes to Congratulate
chapters.content:
In that operation, she had used the most dishonorable means to clear the final obstacles for Xiao Cheng. The blade in her hand had, for the first time, been tainted by the stains of framing and entrapment.

She had won, but she felt as though she had lost something more important than victory.

For these past few days, she had not stepped foot into that study again. She confined herself to this small training ground, as if only the cold touch of her weapons could bring a moment of peace to her chaotic heart.

"Princess."

Uncle Zhang’s footsteps sounded behind her, carrying an unusual weight.

"The Prince of Ning has sent an envoy, saying... he is here to congratulate Your Highness on taking control of Cangbei, and has brought gifts."

The Prince of Ning.

Xiao Cheng’s fifth brother, Xiao Yuan. His fief bordered Cangbei, and he was the most powerful vassal king in the Northern Territory. This man was ambitious and no good person.

Shen Li’s hand, wiping the spear, paused slightly.

Gifts?

A weasel paying respects to a chicken—it boded no good.

"What did the Prince say?" she asked coolly.

"The Prince... the Prince is overjoyed and has ordered a grand banquet to be prepared. Tonight, he will personally host the Prince of Ning’s envoy." Uncle Zhang’s tone was tinged with helplessness.

Shen Li was silent. She could already envision Xiao Cheng’s "useless" persona, trembling with fear and bowing obsequiously.

She placed her spear back on the rack and turned to walk toward her bedroom.

"Prepare my armor."

Regardless, she was his Princess in name. She had to be present at this "Hongmen Banquet." She wanted to see exactly what this neighbor was planning to pull.

At nightfall, the main hall of the Prince’s Mansion was brightly lit.

A "grand" welcome banquet was underway.

Xiao Cheng sat in the seat of honor, his face full of smiles, raising his cup frequently. His humble and enthusiastic demeanor was exactly like that of a bandit leader who had just occupied a mountain and was eager to curry favor with the neighboring mountain lord.

Sitting below him was a middle-aged man in luxurious robes with an arrogant expression. He was the envoy of Prince Ning, Li Yuan.

Li Yuan’s gaze swept across the hall without any attempt at concealment; his eyes did not look like those of a guest, but rather like someone inspecting his own territory. A trace of contempt hung at the corners of his mouth.

Shen Li, dressed in military attire rather than women’s clothing, sat quietly beside Xiao Cheng, her face as cold as frost, not saying a word. She was like a beautiful ice sculpture, completely out of place in the warm, bustling atmosphere.

After three rounds of drinks, Li Yuan set down his wine cup with a soft "thud."

The noisy hall fell silent in an instant.

"Seventh Prince."

Li Yuan spoke, not even bothering to use an honorific; his tone was as if he were addressing a servant.

"I hear that since Your Highness arrived in Cangbei, you have acted with great vigor, wiping out the Ma family and subduing the Chamber of Commerce. Truly... how joyous and congratulatory."

Though he spoke of joy and congratulations, there was not a hint of happiness on his face; instead, he carried the oppressive air of an interrogator.

Xiao Cheng stood up, looking "flattered," holding his wine cup and bowing, smiling like a complete lackey.

"Not at all, not at all! It is all thanks to the blessing of my fifth brother, thanks to the blessing of His Highness, Prince Ning! I am new here; if not for the support of Prince Ning, how would I have had the courage?"

Seeing his humble demeanor, the contempt in Li Yuan’s eyes grew even deeper.

He said slowly, "Your Highness is too modest. My Prince said that since we are brothers and neighbors, we should help each other. However... Cangbei is located on the frontier, plagued by bandits, and the Northern Barbarians often harass the borders. With your meager troops and few generals, I fear this vast estate is difficult to defend."

The point of the conversation had finally arrived.

The smile on Xiao Cheng’s face stiffened, and he stammered, "Then... then in your opinion, Magistrate Li..."

Li Yuan smiled. It was a cruel smile, like a cat toying with a mouse.

"My Prince is benevolent. He is willing to send troops to protect the safety of Cangbei and block all invading enemies for you, Seventh Prince."

"Of course, the cost of provisions for tens of thousands of troops is not a small sum..."

He drew out his tone, extended seven fingers, and waved them in front of Xiao Cheng.

"My Prince’s meaning is that the newly established Cangbei Chamber of Commerce is highly profitable. Your Highness only needs to set aside seventy percent of the annual profits as a 'protection fee' for my Prince. In this way, it resolves your worries and fulfills the brotherly bond between our two houses. Isn't that wonderful?"

Seventy percent!

As soon as these words were spoken, the expressions of all the Cangbei generals present changed drastically!

This was no protection; this was blatant, daylight robbery!

Uncle Zhang’s fists clenched instantly, the veins on the back of his hands bulging.

Xiao Cheng looked as if he had been frightened silly by the number; the hand holding his wine cup trembled slightly, and his face turned deathly pale.

"Se... seventy percent? This... this is too much... Magistrate Li, look... can we... discuss this further?"

Seeing his pathetic appearance, Li Yuan no longer bothered to hide his disdain. He leaned back in his chair and said in a tone of condescension:

"Seventh Prince, my Prince is doing this to help you. Otherwise, with your few men, let alone the Northern Barbarians, even those bandits swarming the mountains would be enough to give you a hard time. This seventy percent profit is the price for your peace of mind. This is a very good deal!"

After speaking, his gaze turned flirtatiously toward Shen Li, who was beside Xiao Cheng.

"Furthermore, in this Cangbei, the one who truly calls the shots is likely not you, Seventh Prince, is it?"

His eyes swept unscrupulously over Shen Li’s exquisite figure in her military uniform, filled with undisguised greed and lewdness.

"I have long heard that the daughter of the General of the North, General Shen Li, is a peerless, heaven-sent goddess of war. Seeing you today, the reputation is well-deserved. However..."

He changed the subject, looked at Xiao Cheng, and let out a sneer.

"For such a delicate, thorny rose to be paired with a... well, 'unambitious' prince like you, it is truly... such a pity!"

"Boom!"

A cold, murderous aura erupted from Shen Li!

Her hand, hidden under the table, had already gripped the hilt of her sword!

This piece of trash—he dared to humiliate Xiao Cheng in public and harass her! He was courting death!

Just as Shen Li was about to draw her sword!

"Ah!"

With a terrified shriek, Xiao Cheng, who was in the main seat, seemed to have been scared out of his wits by Li Yuan’s words. He shuddered violently, and the wine cup in his hand slipped away!

A full cup of wine splashed squarely onto Li Yuan!

"So... sorry! Sorry! Magistrate Li! I... I didn't mean to!"

Xiao Cheng "scared" himself right out of his seat, flustered and pale as paper.

Li Yuan, drenched in wine and looking wretched, was about to lash out, but saw Xiao Cheng rushing over in a panic.

"I... I'll wipe it off for you! Let me wipe it off!"

Xiao Cheng apologized profusely while frantically digging for a handkerchief in his robes.

He pulled too hard and moved too abruptly.

Along with the snow-white handkerchief, a yellowed parchment scroll tied with a thin string "accidentally" slipped from his wide sleeve and fell to the floor with a "thud."

This sudden turn of events left everyone stunned.

The parchment scroll looked quite ancient, but the massive seal stamped in cinnabar at one end of the scroll appeared exceptionally striking under the lamplight.

It was a vigorous and powerful wolf-head pattern, the wolf’s mouth wide open as if roaring at the heavens!

The Khan’s seal of the Snow Eagle Tribe of the Northern Barbarians!

Shen Li’s pupils contracted sharply!

She recognized this seal! In ten years of fighting the Northern Barbarian tribes countless times, she knew their flags and seals by heart! This was, without a doubt, the personal seal of Batu, the current Great Khan of the Snow Eagle Tribe!

Li Yuan’s gaze naturally fell upon that seal as well.

His expression changed violently the moment he saw the wolf-head pattern!

"Pri... Prince! You dropped something!" A nearby palace guard "quickly" picked up the scroll and respectfully presented it to Xiao Cheng.

At the moment of presentation, the scroll opened slightly due to gravity.

Although it was only a corner, the large characters written in the Northern Barbarian script clearly entered Li Yuan’s eyes!

"Military... Mutual... Assistance... Covenant..."

Li Yuan’s breathing stopped instantly!

The Snow Eagle Tribe!

That was the most valiant and battle-hardened of all the Northern Barbarian tribes! Although they had been suppressed by the Golden Wolf Tribe in recent years, the combat power of their cavalry remained an inescapable nightmare for all the princes of the North!

This useless prince, how... how could he be involved with the Snow Eagle Tribe? And even signed a military mutual assistance covenant?!

How is this possible!

"Ah! My things!"

Xiao Cheng seemed to have just realized what happened. He snatched the scroll back, acting like a thief with a guilty conscience, and stuffed it back into his robes in a panic. As he stuffed it, he looked around nervously, as if terrified of being seen.

To Li Yuan, this attempt to cover up only served as the most definitive proof!

Li Yuan’s expression shifted uncertainly.

His mind was in chaos.

No wonder!

No wonder this piece of trash dared to wipe out the Ma family so easily!

No wonder he dared to spend his wealth without hesitation to win the hearts of the people!

So, he was not alone at all! Behind him stood the hungry wolf that was the Snow Eagle Tribe!

Once the Prince Ning’s estate went to war with him, the iron cavalry of the Snow Eagle Tribe could drive straight in and strike at the heart of Prince Ning’s territory! This was a consequence that the Prince Ning’s estate could not afford!

He looked again at Xiao Cheng’s still "panicked" face and felt a chill rise from the soles of his feet, rushing straight to his head!

This man was no piece of trash! He was clearly a most cunning and treacherous wolf in sheep’s clothing! All his previous humility, all his cowardice and incompetence, were all an act! It was all to show him this "great gift" at the moment he was most arrogant and off-guard!

Li Yuan broke out in a cold sweat.

He dared not stay any longer. He felt that his life was in danger with every extra moment he stayed.

"Ah... haha, Seventh Prince, look at my memory..." Li Yuan forced a smile that was uglier than crying and stood up from his seat. "I... I suddenly remembered there is urgent business back at the estate. Regarding the protection fee... well, I was too abrupt. Let us... discuss it at length, discuss it at length! I shall take my leave for today!"

After speaking, he didn't even care about etiquette; he fled the hall with his entourage as if he were a stray dog.

The envoy, who had been arrogant and overbearing just a moment ago, had turned into a pathetic wretch in the blink of an eye.

This dramatic turn of events left everyone unable to react.

It wasn't until Li Yuan’s figure completely disappeared that Xiao Cheng let out a "long" sigh of relief. He slumped back into his chair, patting his chest, looking genuinely shaken.

"Scared... scared me to death... finally gone..."

He turned his head to look at Shen Li beside him, who was still gripping her sword hilt, and revealed that familiar, cowardly smile again.

"Princess, thanks to you, your murderous aura just now scared them all away..."

Shen Li did not speak.

Her gaze was fixed on Xiao Cheng’s hand, which was still tucking the scroll into his robes.

She saw it clearly.

That piece of parchment was new.

The ink on it was also new.

Only the seal was old.

It was a forgery.

From beginning to end, it was a meticulously planned play. A perfect, flawless play that used her rage as the fuse and his "cowardice" as the cover to finally reveal his lethal trump card.

He had scared a fierce and aggressive enemy into running away with their tails between their legs without spending a single soldier or shedding a drop of blood.

His methods were far more brilliant than her sword, and also... far cleaner.

How many more trump cards did this man have that she didn't know about?

chapters.title: The Transaction
chapters.content:
Li Yuan, the envoy of Prince Ning, disappeared outside the gates of the Prince’s estate as if fleeing for his life.

The contrast between his arrogant arrival and his panicked departure left the banquet hall, which had been tense and united just moments before, in an eerie silence.

The Cangbei generals in the hall looked at each other, their faces filled with the relief of having survived a disaster and an unmistakable sense of bewilderment.

They had won.

They had won in a way that was baffling, in a way that defied belief.

They didn't even understand what had just happened. Why had that arrogant envoy, after the Prince "accidentally" dropped a scroll, been so terrified that he lost his wits and fled in a panic?

Only Shen Li remained where she was, motionless.

Her gaze passed over her bewildered colleagues, cut through the flickering candlelight, and locked firmly onto the man who was patting his chest, wearing an expression of "lingering fear."

"Princess, thanks to you..."

Xiao Cheng was still acting. He turned his head, wearing that familiar, cowardly, and ingratiating smile, as if everything that had just occurred had nothing to do with him.

Shen Li did not respond to him.

In her mind, she replayed every detail of the moment over and over again.

The cup of wine that was "accidentally" spilled.

The scroll of the alliance that "accidentally" fell out.

And his appearance of being "guilty as a thief," trying to cover up his tracks.

One link after another, seamless and perfect.

He had calculated Li Yuan’s arrogance, calculated her own anger, and even more so, calculated how much psychological impact a forged "military alliance" with the Northern Barbarian tribes would have on the other side in such a tense atmosphere.

Winning without a fight, repelling the enemy invisibly.

This was no longer a scheme; this was art. A chilling art that played with the human heart in the palm of one's hand.

This man...

For the first time, a feeling called "fear" toward him arose in Shen Li's heart.

The banquet ended hastily.

Xiao Cheng, however, had no intention of resting. He directly ordered all core generals to report to the study for a meeting immediately.

This time, he did not exclude Shen Li.

Inside the study, the massive map of Cangbei was spread out once again.

Xiao Cheng stood before the map, the cowardice and panic on his face completely faded away. He had changed into crisp, casual attire; his expression was cold and stern, his gaze sharp—he was a completely different person from the "useless" man at the banquet.

The generals, seeing him like this, felt somewhat uncomfortable and sat up straight, not daring to make a sound.

Shen Li stood at the back of the crowd, arms crossed, watching coldly. She wanted to see what he was planning to do next.

"I believe you all saw what happened today."

Xiao Cheng spoke, his voice steady and carrying an unquestionable majesty.

"Prince Ning is a wolf. Today he sent an envoy to test us; tomorrow, he will lead his army to our gates. We must make full preparations before he makes his move."

Uncle Zhang stepped forward and cupped his hands, saying, "The Prince is right! This subordinate requests to immediately strengthen the city defenses and put the entire army on combat readiness!"

"Not enough." Xiao Cheng shook his head, his finger slowly tracing the border of Cangbei on the map, finally stopping on the vast grasslands further north.

"Defense is always passive. If we want to keep the wolves from daring to pounce, we must first become tigers ourselves."

He raised his head, his gaze sweeping over everyone present.

"We must expand our army. We must build a powerful cavalry capable of contending with Prince Ning, or any enemy!"

Cavalry!

These two words caused the breath of every general to hitch.

In the Northern Territory, whoever possessed a powerful cavalry held the initiative in war. Everyone understood this principle.

However...

"Your Highness," one general couldn't help but speak up, "Building a cavalry requires a massive number of warhorses. Cangbei is poor and does not produce horses. We only captured a mere hundred from the Ma family; it is simply not enough to form an army."

"There will be horses."

Xiao Cheng’s gaze turned to Su Wan beside him.

Su Wan stepped forward, her cold, clear voice echoing in the study.

"The Prince already has a perfect plan. This plan is called 'Expelling the Outsiders'."

"To expel the outsiders, one must first pacify the interior; we have already pacified the interior. Now is the time to expel the outsiders. The alliance document at the banquet today, though forged, has pointed us in the right direction."

Her finger pointed to the area on the map named the "Snow Eagle Tribe."

"This tribe is a force with considerable combat power among the Northern Barbarian tribes. They possess the best grasslands and the fiercest warhorses. It is a pity that in recent years, they have been repeatedly oppressed by the 'Golden Wolf Tribe,' the largest of the Northern Barbarian tribes. Beset by internal and external troubles, they are struggling to survive, almost on the verge of extinction."

"The enemy of an enemy is our friend. Our next step is to turn this forged alliance into a real one!"

Hearing this, the faces of the generals showed excitement. If they could form an alliance with the Snow Eagle Tribe, it would be equivalent to adding a natural barrier to the northern border of Cangbei!

However, Su Wan's next words made everyone's smiles freeze on their faces.

"To show our sincerity, the Prince has decided to immediately organize a caravan. They will carry thirty thousand shi of grain and ten thousand catties of ironware to the Snow Eagle Tribe to trade with them."

Thirty thousand shi of grain! Ten thousand catties of ironware!

The entire study fell into dead silence.

Everyone looked at Xiao Cheng and Su Wan as if they were looking at lunatics.

Grain was their lifeline, which they had only just recovered from famine!

Ironware was a strategic resource for forging weapons and armor!

Now, they were going to give these life-saving treasures to a group of savage barbarians?

"This... this is absolutely impossible!" Uncle Zhang was the first to jump out, his face flushed with anxiety. "Your Highness! Miss Su! Do you know that to get from Cangbei to the Snow Eagle Tribe, one must pass through the territory of the Golden Wolf Tribe! A caravan as large as ours, loaded with grain and iron, is nothing but walking fat in their eyes! This isn't forming an alliance; this is going to our deaths!"

"Exactly!" Another general echoed excitedly. "Even if we were lucky enough to reach the Snow Eagle Tribe, why would they trade with us? The Northern Barbarians only recognize scimitars and fists; they never talk about honor! If we give them the grain and iron and they turn on us, what can we do?!"

Voices of opposition rose one after another.

The entire study became a chaotic mess.

Xiao Cheng just listened quietly, his face devoid of expression. It was not until everyone had finished speaking that he spoke slowly, asking a question.

"Then what are we going to trade this grain and iron for?"

Everyone was stunned.

Su Wan smiled slightly and took over.

"For warhorses."

"The Snow Eagle Tribe has nothing else, only warhorses in abundance. They have the best horses in the Northern Territory, but they cannot feed enough warriors. To them, on the verge of extinction, these warhorses are just a useless burden. And what we lack most is warhorses."

Trading grain for warhorses?

This idea was too crazy, too whimsical!

Shen Li finally couldn't help it and stepped out from behind the crowd.

"Absurd!"

She spat out the two words coldly, instantly silencing the noisy study.

Her gaze was fixed on Xiao Cheng, sharp as a blade.

"Your Highness, do you know that the grain and fodder consumed by a thousand-man heavy cavalry in a year is enough to support five thousand infantry? We are taking life-saving grain to trade for a bottomless pit that consumes fodder—this is digging our own graves!"

"Do you know that the journey from Cangbei to the Snow Eagle Tribe is eight hundred miles long? The route is nothing but desert and Gobi, and we must constantly guard against raids by the Golden Wolf Tribe. It would be a miracle if thirty percent of this caravan reaches the destination alive!"

"Do you also know that the Northern Barbarians view their warhorses as their lives! You want to trade their lifeline for some food? Is this an insult to me, a general who has fought in the Northern Territory for ten years, or an insult to all the soldiers who died defending the border?!"

Every word of hers was like a heavy hammer, smashing hard into everyone's hearts.

This was reality! This was war! Not some light, empty talk on paper by a strategist!

Xiao Cheng looked at the furious Shen Li, but instead of being angry, he showed that "innocent," infuriating smile again.

"Princess, what you've said is all too complicated; I don't understand."

He waved his hand, speaking in a tone almost like a child's.

"I just know that they are starving to death, and we have food. If we want to be friends with them, we have to show some sincerity, right? Sending some food, sending some ironware for hunting—this is the etiquette of our Great Zhou! We are good to them, and they will naturally be good to us, won't they?"

"You!"

Shen Li’s chest heaved with anger at his rogue-like rhetoric.

She had never seen such a... shameless person!

To speak of such a dangerous and significant military operation as lightly as children playing house!

Who was he insulting?!

"Your Highness!" Uncle Zhang and the others were so anxious they were about to kneel. "Please, Your Highness, think twice! This is no different from sending our soldiers to their deaths in vain!"

"Enough!"

The smile on Xiao Cheng's face suddenly vanished.

A kingly pressure radiated from him, instantly suppressing all the noise.

"On this matter, I have made my decision."

His gaze swept across the room, his voice not loud, but carrying unquestionable resolve.

"I know you think I'm crazy. Sometimes, only a madman can accomplish what ordinary people cannot."

"I am going to use this thirty thousand shi of grain to gamble on a future! To gamble on an iron cavalry that can trample the Northern Territory!"

"Whoever dares to speak more, will be dealt with by military law!"

The meeting broke up in discord.

The generals left one by one, dejected, their eyes filled with disappointment and confusion. In their hearts, this Prince, who had just shown a glimpse of the stature of a great ruler, had turned into a stubborn, whimsical madman in the blink of an eye.

Shen Li was the last to leave.

She walked to the door and stopped, but did not turn back.

"If the entire caravan is wiped out, how will you answer to the soldiers who died in vain?" she asked coldly.

Behind her came Xiao Cheng's calm voice.

"Then I, this madman of a Prince, will go to them myself and kowtow in apology."

Shen Li's heart trembled for no reason.

She did not say another word and strode out of the study.

That night, in Shen Li's bedroom, the candles were burning bright.

A young scout with a lean build and eyes like a hawk knelt on one knee before her.

He was the commander of the scout battalion and the most trusted confidant handpicked by Shen Li, known as "Zhuiyun."

"General, what are your orders?"

Shen Li handed him a secret letter sealed with red wax and a token for mobilizing troops.

"Tomorrow, the Prince's caravan will depart. You are to select twenty of the best men in the battalion, change into plain clothes, take the finest crossbows and sabers, and set out after them."

Zhuiyun took the letter and the token, a flicker of doubt crossing his eyes. "General, do you mean... to protect the caravan?"

"No." Shen Li shook her head, a complex expression flashing in her eyes.

"It is to monitor them."

"Your mission is to follow them from a distance. Unless it is an absolute last resort, you must never reveal yourselves. I want you to record everything that happens along the way, down to the smallest detail."

"I want to see exactly what kind of medicine he is selling in his gourd."

She paused, her voice turning icy.

"If the caravan truly faces total annihilation, you have the token here; you may... act as you see fit."

"Understood!" Zhuiyun tucked the secret letter and the token into his tunic, bowed deeply with his fists clenched, and then vanished into the night like a phantom.

Shen Li walked to the window and pushed it open; the cold night wind rushed in.

She gazed toward the depths of the Prince's estate, at the study where the lights were still burning, her expression shifting uncertainly.

A madman? Or a genius?

This time, she would witness the answer for herself.

The next morning, a massive caravan slowly rolled out of the city gates under the worried and bewildered gazes of countless Cangbei citizens.

The wagons were fully loaded with precious grain and ironware.

On the faces of every guard in the procession, there was a tragic air, as if they were marching toward the execution ground.

Shen Li stood atop the high city wall, dressed in military uniform, her posture as straight as a pine.

She watched the lonely procession gradually disappear into the vast morning mist of the North, remaining silent for a long time.

chapters.title: Negotiation
chapters.content:
As the caravan drove out of Cangbei City, it was as if they had entered a desolate, dead wasteland.

The northern wind scraped against everyone's faces like a knife. The wheels ground over the frozen, hardened earth, emitting a monotonous creaking sound. In the procession, apart from the wind and the sound of the wheels, there was no other speech.

Every guard wore the heavy expression of a man heading to the gallows. They did not understand why the Prince had ordered them to escort the lifeblood of the entire city along a path of certain death.

The caravan's leader was a steward from the Prince's estate. He wrapped his fur coat tightly around himself, his eyes constantly scanning the surrounding barren ridges, his heart filled with despair.

Su Wan sat in an inconspicuous carriage in the middle of the procession. She did not lift the curtain, just sat quietly, as if the bitter cold and danger of the outside world had nothing to do with her.

The atmosphere in the group was stifling to the extreme.

After five days of travel, they had penetrated hundreds of miles into the grasslands. Along the way, piles of white bones and abandoned camps were visible everywhere, silently telling of the cruelty of this land.

Just as everyone began to feel a sense of numbness, danger descended without warning.

"Awoo—"

A shrill, excited wolf howl came from behind a hill not far away.

Immediately following, countless cavalrymen surged out from all directions like a black tide! They were disheveled, wielding scimitars, their faces painted with hideous oils.

It was the Golden Wolf tribe's cavalry!

"Enemy attack!"

The lead steward let out a hoarse roar.

The guards instinctively drew their sabers and formed a crude circular formation, protecting the wagons filled with grain and ironware in the center. But their faces were filled with terror.

The enemy's numbers were at least five times their own.

The Golden Wolf cavalry did not charge immediately. They circled the caravan, galloping and howling, using their skilled horsemanship and provocative gestures to dismantle the guards' morale.

A Golden Wolf rider suddenly leaned down, scooped up a stone from the ground, and hurled it fiercely at a guard.

The guard raised his saber to block, but the immense force sent him stumbling back several steps, his hand splitting open.

More stones and bone spears rained down like a downpour. The caravan's circular formation instantly fell into chaos.

"Charge!"

The centurion of the Golden Wolf tribe issued the order.

Hundreds of cavalrymen let out beastly howls, waving their scimitars as they charged from all sides. The sound of hooves was like thunder; the earth itself trembled.

This was a slaughter with no suspense.

Although the guards fought to the death, their blades could not stop the high-speed charge of the warhorses. In one encounter, the outer defensive line was torn open by a massive gap.

Blood splattered, and screams rose one after another.

A guard was struck in the shoulder by a scimitar; he roared and used all his strength to plunge his long blade into the horse's belly. The warhorse collapsed with a mournful cry, pinning him underneath.

More scimitars immediately descended upon him.

The lead steward's eyes were bloodshot. He watched his brothers fall one by one, his heart aching like it was being sliced by knives. He knew everything was over.

Just as the Golden Wolf cavalry was about to scatter the entire caravan and reach Su Wan's carriage:

"Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!"

A series of sharp, teeth-gritting sounds of air being pierced came from the hillside on the flank!

Dozens of black shadows, moving at a speed the naked eye could barely capture, shot precisely into the ranks of the Golden Wolf cavalry.

The dozen or so Golden Wolf riders at the front didn't even have time to scream before they tumbled from their saddles. Each of them had a pitch-black crossbow bolt embedded in their throat.

The sudden turn of events caused the Golden Wolf tribe's offensive to stall.

Everyone looked toward the hillside in astonishment.

There, twenty warriors dressed in black tight-fitting clothes with black cloth masks stood on the slope in a cold and efficient manner. The military crossbows in their hands had a peculiar design, gleaming with a cold metallic luster.

They did not shout, nor did they make any unnecessary movements. They simply, silently, drew the strings, aimed, and fired.

Every vibration of a crossbow string was inevitably accompanied by a Golden Wolf rider falling from their horse.

It was not a battle; it was a slaughter.

The Golden Wolf tribe's centurion's face changed drastically. He had never seen such terrifying weapons or such precise marksmanship!

"Charge! Kill them!"

He roared, turned his horse, and personally led dozens of cavalrymen to charge toward the hillside.

However, they were met with another round of deadly volley fire.

The cavalrymen at the front fell in swathes, like wheat being harvested.

Just as they reached the halfway point of the slope, the twenty men in black simultaneously put away their crossbows and drew the sabers at their waists.

The leader of the black-clad men had eyes like a hawk. It was Zhuiyun, Shen Li's confidant.

"Kill."

A cold word escaped his lips.

The twenty men, like a drawn sword, did not retreat but advanced, charging down to meet the dozens of Golden Wolf riders!

Their formation was simple and effective. In groups of five, covering each other, every swing of their sabers carried a deadly, cold light.

The Golden Wolf tribe's scimitars, striking their armor, only produced dull thuds and sparks. Yet their own sabers easily cleaved through the enemy's crude leather armor, kicking up sprays of blood.

Zhuiyun's figure was like a phantom. His blade moved so fast it left only a blur. A Golden Wolf rider charged past him, and he didn't even look back, simply striking with a backhand blow.

The rider galloped ten paces further before his head rolled from his neck.

In just a quarter of an hour, the battle had undergone a shocking reversal.

The Golden Wolf tribe's centurion had his arm severed by Zhuiyun's blade. Looking at these devil-like men in black in terror, he finally broke down.

"Retreat! Retreat!"

He let out a shrill cry, turned his horse, and fled in a panic.

The remaining Golden Wolf cavalry, their spirits already broken, shrieked and fled in all directions.

Zhuiyun watched their pathetic retreating backs and coldly raised his hand.

The men in black immediately stopped their pursuit.

"Let one go back to report."

"Understood."

The battle ended. Nearly a hundred corpses of Golden Wolf cavalrymen were left on the ground. As for the twenty men in black, not a single one was injured.

They silently cleared the battlefield, reclaiming their crossbow bolts as if they had just performed a trivial task.

The caravan guards stared at all this, as if in a dream.

Just then, the curtain of Su Wan's carriage was lifted.

She stepped down, glanced at the corpses littering the ground, and then at the silent men in black on the hillside, a knowing smile appearing on her face.

She walked up to Zhuiyun and nodded slightly.

"Thank you."

Zhuiyun simply bowed his fists and said nothing.

Su Wan did not say more. She turned to the terrified caravan steward and said calmly, "Continue forward."

This bloody ambush seemed to be nothing more than a minor interlude. After a brief rest, the caravan set off on its journey once more.

Two days later, they finally arrived at the territory of the Snow Eagle tribe.

From afar, one could see countless dilapidated tents scattered across the withered yellow grassland. Most of the tribespeople were sallow and emaciated, their eyes numb. The cattle and sheep were gaunt and few in number.

An air of decay hung over the entire tribe.

The arrival of the caravan, and the glorious victory that had taken place at the border, had already spread throughout the Snow Eagle tribe.

When the grain-laden caravan appeared on the horizon, the entire tribe erupted.

They viewed the caravan as saviors descended from the heavens.

The leader of the Snow Eagle tribe, a weather-beaten middle-aged man named Batu, personally led the tribal elders to welcome them at the entrance of the camp.

His eyes held undisguised excitement and gratitude. Yet, he still tried to maintain the dignity and pride of a tribal leader.

"Welcome, friends from the East." Batu's voice was booming. He opened his arms as if to embrace Su Wan. "Eternal Heaven heard my prayers, sent you, and even sent divine soldiers to punish our enemies!"

Su Wan stepped down from the carriage and gave Batu a polite but distant smile.

"Leader Batu, greetings."

She did not accept Batu's embrace, simply standing there calmly.

Batu retracted his arms, feeling somewhat awkward, and let out a hearty laugh to cover his loss of composure.

"Quick! Quickly invite our honored guests into the Golden Tent! I have already prepared the fattest lambs and the most mellow mare's milk wine for you!"

He extended an invitation with enthusiasm, his posture that of a host prepared to receive a gift.

Su Wan, however, shook her head.

The smile on her face slowly faded.

"That won't be necessary, Chieftain Batu."

Her voice turned cold, devoid of any warmth.

"We are not here as guests. I am here on behalf of my master, the Prince of Cangbei, His Highness Xiao Cheng, to negotiate a deal with you."

The smile on Batu’s face froze.

Su Wan reached out and pointed to the carts of grain and ironware behind her.

"These can be yours. But they are not a gift; they are for trade."

She paused, looking directly into Batu’s eyes, which were beginning to show signs of shock, and said, word by word:

"Chieftain Batu, on our way here, our scouts have already determined the movements of the Golden Wolf Tribe’s main force. In ten days at most, their army will be at your camp. When that time comes, your tribe will be razed to the ground. Your men will be made slaves, your women will be sold into prostitution, and your skull will be turned into a wine vessel."

These words hit Batu like a bucket of ice water poured from head to toe.

The blood drained from his face in an instant.

Su Wan revealed a cruel smile.

"Now, you have two choices."

"First, accept my deal and trade the most useless things in your tribe for this grain that will keep you alive and the ironware that will allow your warriors to take up arms."

"Second, reject my deal. In that case, my caravan will turn around immediately and seek out the King of the Golden Wolf Tribe. I believe he would be very happy to cooperate with us and divide your pastures, cattle, and sheep between us."

"Chieftain Batu, my master does not have much patience."

Su Wan’s voice was not loud, but it struck the Snow Eagle Tribe’s vital point with precision, completely exposing their desperate situation.

chapters.title: My Princess Is Not for Use as a Hostage!
chapters.content:
Batu’s face turned deathly pale.

Every word of Su Wan’s was like a steel needle dipped in ice, piercing his heart and nearly freezing the blood in his veins.

The tribal elders behind him looked equally ashen. Some instinctively gripped the hilts of their swords, only to release them powerlessly.

Anger, humiliation, and... bone-chilling fear.

These emotions were intertwined in the hearts of every high-ranking member of the Snow Eagle Tribe.

They were the eagles of the grasslands; when had they ever been subjected to such blatant threats and humiliation?

"Are you... you Da Zhou people all as arrogant as you?" Batu’s voice was hoarse with extreme rage. He stared fixedly at Su Wan, his eyes burning as if he wanted to tear her apart.

The smile on Su Wan’s face did not change in the slightest.

"No," she shook her head gently, "it is just that my master does not like to waste time."

As if she did not see Batu’s murderous gaze, she continued on her own: "Chieftain, I know what you are thinking. You are thinking that we are merely a single caravan, so how dare we spout such nonsense here."

Her gaze moved past Batu and landed on the scout team not far away, standing silently on the hillside like black statues.

"I think you saw the battle just now quite clearly. Over a hundred cavalrymen from the Golden Wolf Tribe didn't even touch the hem of their clothes before they became corpses on the ground. And our people were completely unscathed."

"Chieftain Batu, how many men do you think my master would need to send if he wanted to wipe out your tribe?"

This sentence hit Batu’s heart like a heavy hammer.

Indeed.

The combat power displayed by that god-like troop had exceeded his understanding of warfare. That wasn't a battle; it was a one-sided slaughter.

He did not doubt for a moment that if they wished, those twenty men alone could turn his entire tribe upside down.

"Do you think we really need to trade with you?"

Su Wan’s voice grew colder.

"My master could just as easily go directly to the Golden Wolf Tribe. I am sure the Golden Wolf King would be very happy to trade the horses and livestock he has plundered for the grain and fine weapons in our possession. By then, your Snow Eagle Tribe wouldn't even qualify to be a bargaining chip on our table."

"We are giving you this chance not out of mercy, but because my master thinks you are slightly smarter than that greedy Wolf King. At the very least, you know how to weigh the pros and cons."

Batu’s body swayed.

Some of the elders behind him were already emitting sounds of despair.

This woman was a devil.

She had completely shattered the dignity of the Snow Eagle Tribe and then laid the cruel reality before them.

They had no room for choice.

Batu closed his eyes and took a deep breath of the cold grassland air.

When he opened them again, all the anger and resentment had faded, leaving only the coldness and decisiveness of a warlord.

"Fine."

He squeezed the word out through his teeth.

"I accept your deal."

"We want the grain and the ironware. We will trade you our warhorses!"

The smile on Su Wan’s face finally held a hint of sincerity.

"The Chieftain is a smart man."

"Tell me, how many warhorses can you provide?"

Batu straightened his chest, the pride of a tribal chieftain returning to his face.

"Three thousand!"

He held up three fingers, his voice booming.

"The toughest warhorses raised on the best pastures of my Snow Eagle Tribe! Each one can travel eight hundred li a day! This is the greatest sincerity of my Snow Eagle Tribe!"

Three thousand warhorses!

This number made even the manager of the caravan behind Su Wan gasp.

That was the prototype of a cavalry force capable of sweeping across the Northern Frontier!

A glint of light flashed in Su Wan’s eyes.

"Very good."

She nodded and was about to speak.

But Batu suddenly changed the subject.

"However, I have one condition."

His gaze became sharp, staring fixedly at Su Wan.

"We people of the grasslands do not trust verbal alliances."

"Your grain and ironware can be transported into my tribe immediately. But when will the fine weapons you promised to arm our warriors with arrive?"

Su Wan replied indifferently: "Once the alliance is reached, the first batch of five hundred military crossbows and the accompanying armor can be delivered within half a month."

"Half a month?" Batu sneered. "Half a month is enough for you to join forces with the Golden Wolf Tribe and swallow us whole, skin and bones."

He looked around, his gaze sweeping over the silent, solemn caravan guards and the black-clad scouts, finally settling on a figure in the distance who had arrived at the scene at some unknown moment.

It was a woman.

She wore light silver armor, her posture as straight as a spear. Even standing there quietly, she exuded an aura of the battlefield that could not be ignored.

Although there was a distance between them, that cold and stunning face, and those eyes brighter than the stars, had already spread throughout the Northern Frontier along with her illustrious reputation.

The daughter of the General who Guards the North, the Princess of Cangbei, Shen Li.

The woman who made countless barbarian warriors tremble in fear on the Northern Frontier battlefield.

A gleam of light flashed in Batu’s eyes.

"To show the sincerity of our alliance and to ensure this deal proceeds smoothly, I hope that before the first batch of weapons arrives, a noble person from your side can stay in my tribe as a guest."

He paused, raised his hand, and pointed from afar toward Shen Li.

"I think nothing represents your sincerity better than Her Highness, the Princess of Cangbei."

As soon as these words were spoken, the entire scene fell into silence.

Everyone’s eyes snapped toward Shen Li.

The caravan guards’ expressions changed drastically.

The Princess was their backbone, the symbol of Cangbei’s military strength. To let her stay as a hostage? That was pure delusion!

Su Wan’s brows also furrowed slightly.

This Batu was not entirely a fool. He knew that by detaining Shen Li, he would be holding the lifeline of the Prince of Cangbei’s estate.

Shen Li herself, however, remained expressionless.

Meeting everyone’s gaze, she took a step forward and walked slowly toward them.

She did not look at Batu, nor did she look at Su Wan; she simply looked calmly at the land before them where an agreement was about to be reached.

Three thousand warhorses.

The price was too high.

High enough for her to ignore her own personal honor and safety.

"Very well."

She spoke lightly, her voice not loud, yet clearly reaching everyone’s ears.

"I will stay."

A triumphant smile appeared on Batu’s face.

A complex emotion flickered in Su Wan’s eyes.

Just when everyone thought the matter was settled,

"Hahaha... Hahahahahaha!"

A burst of wild, unbridled laughter suddenly came from nearby, shattering the frozen atmosphere!

Everyone looked toward the sound and saw a young man in dark, casual attire standing with his hands behind his back, a wild and mocking smile on his face.

It was Xiao Cheng.

He had appeared here silently, without anyone noticing.

He walked over with long strides, ignoring Batu and Su Wan, and went straight to Shen Li.

In the astonished gaze of everyone, he suddenly reached out, grabbed Shen Li’s arm, and pulled her behind him with a forceful tug.

The movement was rough, yet carried an unquestionable sense of possessiveness.

Caught off guard, Shen Li stumbled and bumped into his back. She was stunned, her senses filled with the unfamiliar, masculine scent radiating from him.

"You..."

She was about to struggle when she heard Xiao Cheng’s arrogant voice ring out across the entire grassland.

He turned around, looking at the horrified Batu with the eyes of someone watching a clown.

"My Princess is for fighting on the battlefield, not for being a hostage to the likes of you!"

His voice was filled with royal dominance and contempt.

"What kind of thing are you to deserve to have my woman stay in your tent?"

Batu’s face turned the color of liver in an instant. The elders behind him drew their scimitars in unison.

"How dare you insult our Chieftain!"

Xiao Cheng, however, seemed not to see those gleaming blades. With a cold sneer, he took a step forward.

That single step, devoid of any overt display of power, nonetheless caused every barbarian warrior who had drawn his blade to subconsciously take a step back.

"What? You want to draw steel on this Prince?"

Xiao Cheng’s gaze swept over the elders, who were fierce in appearance but cowardly at heart, before finally settling back on Batu’s face.

"Batu, put away your pathetic little tricks. I am standing here today to negotiate with you, and that is me giving you face. Do not be ungrateful."

He extended a finger and pointed it at Batu.

"If you want an alliance, show some sincerity! Leave the three thousand warhorses! Take your grain and ironware! In half a month, my weapons will be delivered on time! If they are a day late, I will personally lead my troops to trample your tribe into the ground!"

"As for the hostage..."

Xiao Cheng laughed arrogantly.

"I can promise you this: when my son comes of age, he shall take the most beautiful pearl of your Snow Eagle Tribe as his wife. Our two houses shall be bound in an eternal alliance of marriage!"

"Is this guarantee enough?"

These words exploded like a thunderclap above everyone’s heads!

Batu was completely stunned.

The elders behind him were equally dumbfounded.

They had seen arrogant men, but never one this arrogant.

A useless prince who could barely hold onto his own fiefdom dared to speak to their chieftain in such a commanding tone on their own turf?

Yet...

For some reason, looking into the deep eyes of the man before them and hearing his incomparably domineering words, they could not summon a single thought of resistance.

It was a sense of absolute pressure!

It was not the aura a mere vassal king should possess.

It was... the aura of an emperor!

Su Wan watched Xiao Cheng’s back, her beautiful eyes shimmering with strange brilliance.

As for Shen Li, she was completely frozen.

She stood behind Xiao Cheng, entirely shielded by his broad shoulders. This was the first time she had stood behind him in the posture of one being protected.

She watched the man’s back, her heart surging with waves of emotion.

This man...

What did he just say?

His princess is meant for the battlefield to kill enemies?

His woman?

When my son comes of age?

In an instant, countless chaotic thoughts flooded her mind. Shame, shock, absurdity, and a trace of... a strange, fluttering sensation she had not even realized herself.

This man, whom she had always viewed as a coward and a good-for-nothing, was now standing before her like a towering mountain, shielding her from everything.

The domineering aura radiating from him was so unfamiliar, yet... so incredibly reassuring.

Shen Li stared blankly at his back, forgetting to struggle, forgetting to speak.

chapters.title: Who Exactly Are You?
chapters.content:
The journey back was even more silent than the journey there.

The wind on the grasslands remained biting, but the atmosphere inside the carriage was colder and more oppressive than the wind and snow.

Batu’s face—which had shifted from shock to humiliation, to unwillingness, and finally to submission—remained clearly imprinted in everyone’s minds.

Especially the elders of the Snow Eagle Tribe; after Xiao Cheng’s domineering declaration, the entire process from drawing blades to respectfully seeing them off felt like a surreal, magical dream.

Su Wan sat in her own carriage, a faint smile playing on her lips. Clearly, she was satisfied with the Prince’s performance to the extreme.

Shen Li, meanwhile, shared a carriage with Xiao Cheng.

From the moment they left the Snow Eagle Tribe’s camp, she had not said a word.

She did not look at him, keeping her gaze fixed outside the window at the endless, withered yellow grasslands. Yet, her peripheral vision never left the man beside her.

He had already put away his arrogant and unbridled demeanor, returning to his usual gentle, even somewhat lazy self. He leaned against the carriage’s soft cushions, eyes closed, as if he had fallen asleep.

If she hadn't seen it with her own eyes, who would believe that this man, who appeared so harmless, had just used a few words to completely trample a rebellious grassland tribe under his feet?

Shen Li’s heart was a tangled mess.

"My princess is meant for the battlefield to kill enemies, not to be a hostage for the likes of you!"

"What kind of thing do you think you are, to be worthy of keeping my woman in your tent?"

"When my son comes of age, he shall take the most beautiful pearl of your Snow Eagle Tribe as his wife!"

Those words echoed in her mind over and over again.

Every word struck deep into her long-frozen heart, causing the ice to crack inch by inch and stirring up monstrous waves.

There was shame.

"My woman," "When my son comes of age"—these words were flippant and overbearing, full of offense toward her as an independent warrior.

There was absurdity, too.

How dared he? By what right? A good-for-nothing who had always relied on her and the Shen family for protection, a coward who didn't even dare to breathe loudly in her presence—how dared he make decisions for her in such a matter-of-fact tone, claiming her under his own wings?

When he pulled her behind him and used his not-so-sturdy back to block all the scrutinizing and calculating gazes, that unprecedented sense of security was so real.

So real that it made her heart panic.

She, Shen Li, daughter of the General of the North, had grown up amidst the flash of blades and shadows, fighting in mountains of corpses and seas of blood. She was accustomed to charging into battle, accustomed to protecting others.

In her life, the words "being protected" had never existed.

This man was the first.

With the most brutal actions and the most arrogant words, he had done something... that she could not resist.

Shen Li’s fingertips trembled slightly.

She realized she was finding it increasingly difficult to understand him.

From using schemes to force back the Ning Prince’s envoy to today’s bloodless subjugation of the Snow Eagle Tribe, every move he made overturned her past perceptions.

He hid too deeply.

So deeply that it made her feel fear.

For a man who could disguise himself as a good-for-nothing for over a decade, fooling the entire world, how terrifying must his heart be?

The caravan moved in silence.

Finally, two days later, the familiar silhouette of Cangbei City appeared on the horizon.

News of the merchant caravan’s successful return had already reached the city. The remaining generals and officials gathered at the city gates, waiting expectantly.

When they saw the massive, magnificent herd of three thousand warhorses following behind the caravan, everyone was stunned.

They rubbed their eyes, unable to believe what they were seeing.

Madness! That mad prince had actually succeeded!

He had truly used that grain and ironware to trade for a cavalry force capable of changing the landscape of the Northern Territory!

Thunderous cheers erupted from the crowd.

Yet, all this excitement had nothing to do with Shen Li.

The carriage came to a halt, and Xiao Cheng stepped out first, accepting the worship and cheers of the crowd.

Shen Li followed closely behind.

She ignored everyone, not even glancing at the warhorses that made even her eyes burn with envy. Her gaze was sharp, locked firmly onto Xiao Cheng’s back.

Under the bewildered gazes of everyone, she wove through the crowd and, without a word, followed behind Xiao Cheng, heading straight into the depths of the Prince’s Mansion.

The icy aura of "no strangers allowed" kept everyone who wanted to step forward and offer congratulations at bay.

Xiao Cheng had already anticipated this.

He did not stop, nor did he look back, walking at a steady pace through the courtyard until he finally pushed open the doors to the study.

He had just stepped into the study, not yet having time to turn around.

"Bang!"

The door behind him was slammed shut with immense force.

Shen Li stood behind the door, blocking the only exit with her body.

She did not angrily question him as she usually would, nor did she draw her blade.

She simply stood there, looking at him with a gaze so calm it was terrifying.

The study was dim.

The two of them stood in a silent standoff.

After a long while, Shen Li finally spoke.

Her voice was hoarse and soft, yet carried a power that could pierce the heart.

"Who exactly are you?"

Xiao Cheng turned slowly.

He looked at the woman before him.

She was still wearing that silver-white light armor, her long hair tied high, looking heroic and spirited. In those eyes that always burned with fire, there was now only coldness and confusion.

He knew that from this day on, all pretense had lost its meaning.

The gentleness and laziness on Xiao Cheng’s face faded away bit by bit.

Those eyes, which had always carried a hint of cowardice and sycophancy, became deep and sharp.

For the first time, he met her gaze with a look of complete equality, even carrying a hint of scrutiny.

"In the capital, a prince who is too clever does not live long."

His voice was calm and indifferent, devoid of any emotion.

"I am merely a clever man who wants to survive."

Shen Li’s body trembled slightly.

This answer was beyond her expectations, yet it made perfect sense.

Imperial infighting, brothers slaughtering one another—she had heard and seen too much of these dirty dealings. For an unfavored prince to survive in the man-eating imperial palace, playing the fool was indeed the best way to save his life.

"Just... wanting to survive?" A mocking curve appeared on Shen Li’s lips. "Being able to play the Ning Prince’s envoy in the palm of your hand, being able to make a northern barbarian warlord bow in submission—this does not look like something a man who only wants to survive would do."

Xiao Cheng did not refute her.

He did not speak of love, did not mention ambition, and certainly did not offer any defense or apology for his past deceptions.

He simply walked silently to his desk and took out roll after roll of blueprints and documents from a locked secret compartment.

He spread them out one by one on the massive desk.

Shen Li walked over subconsciously.

When she saw the contents of those blueprints and documents, her pupils contracted sharply.

It was... an incredibly complete development plan for Cangbei!

"Draft for Cangbei Military Reform"—detailed plans on how to combine existing infantry with the newly acquired warhorses to form a brand-new army with coordinated operations between infantry, cavalry, archers, and crossbowmen.

"Policy for Parallel Military and Civilian Tilling"—reorganizing thousands of surrendered soldiers and refugees in the city to reclaim wasteland, training while producing, in order to achieve self-sufficiency in grain in the shortest possible time.

"Cangbei Mineral Distribution and Mining Plan" — On the map, every unknown iron mine, copper mine, and even a small silver mine within Cangbei was clearly marked in vermilion ink! Attached to the side were detailed procedures for mining, smelting, and casting.

"North-South Trade Route Concept" — Connecting the hinterland of the Great Zhou in the south and the various tribes of the grasslands in the north. Leveraging Cangbei’s geographical advantage to build it into a massive trade transit hub, exchanging the cattle, sheep, and furs of the Northern Barbarians for the silk and tea of the south, thereby earning enormous profits!
