Training troops, cultivating land, mining, trade...

Every step was crystal clear. Every detail had been meticulously calculated. Interlocking and mutually reinforcing, they formed an incredibly grand blueprint.

This was no longer the self-preservation strategy of a vassal king.

This was... the grand ambition of a founding monarch!

Shen Li’s mind went blank.

She stared blankly at everything before her, feeling only a chill in her hands and feet.

She finally understood why he had spared no cost to obtain warhorses, and why Su Wan had been able to produce the "strategy to conquer the heart" so easily.

Because all of this had already been in his plan!

Every one of them, every step they took, was merely cooperating with him to complete a piece of this massive puzzle.

He was not taking one step and looking at the next.

He had seen the final outcome before he had even made his first move.

"You..." Shen Li’s voice trembled uncontrollably. "When did you... start preparing all of this?"

Xiao Cheng raised his hand and pointed to the massive topographical map.

His finger traced across Cangbei, across the Northern Territory, and finally landed on the southernmost point of the map, the golden and resplendent city—the Capital.

His voice was cold, devoid of any warmth.

"Princess Consort, did you think I endured humiliation for over a decade just to survive?"

"No."

He shook his head slowly, his eyes erupting with monstrous hatred and ambition.

"I was waiting."

"Waiting for a chance to kill my way back and reclaim everything that should have been mine!"

He turned his head abruptly, his eyes, burning with black flames, staring fixedly at Shen Li.

"This path is destined to be paved with mountains of corpses and seas of blood, destined for eternal damnation."

"Are you willing to walk it with me?"

chapters.title: A Dead End Ahead, An Abyss Behind
chapters.content:
Inside the study, the atmosphere froze instantly.

Xiao Cheng’s question pressed heavily on Shen Li’s chest, making it almost impossible for her to breathe.

"Walk... with you?"

Shen Li’s voice was dry. She looked at this man who seemed so incredibly like a stranger, feeling only absurdity.

The husband who had been submissive in front of her, who had not even dared to meet her eyes, the good-for-nothing prince known to all in the capital, was now issuing her an invitation to vie for the world.

And the foundation beneath his feet was his decade of forbearance, countless precise calculations, and, more importantly, the illustrious military achievements of her Shen family, who had guarded the Northern Territory for generations.

He had used her. He had used the Shen family.

Thoroughly and completely.

Monstrous rage, mixed with the humiliation of being deceived and toyed with, rushed to her head instantly.

"Clang!"

With a clear, dragon-like resonance, the sword at Shen Li’s waist was unsheathed with force. The cold blade pointed directly at Xiao Cheng’s throat.

Her hand was perfectly steady.

Her eyes were cold.

"Xiao Cheng, what do you take my Shen family for? What do you take me for?"

"A stepping stone for your quest for the world?"

Facing the sharp tip of the sword, Xiao Cheng did not retreat.

He did not even blink.

He simply watched her quietly, watching her lips tremble slightly from anger.

On his face, there was no guilt or guilty conscience, only the same indifference as always.

"Princess Consort, from the day we were married, you and I have been one."

"The honor and disgrace of the Shen family have long been tightly bound to me. If I am King, you are the Princess Consort. If I am Emperor, you are the Empress."

"I thought you would have understood this long ago."

His voice remained as flat as ever, yet carried an indisputable sense of inevitability.

"Understand?"

Shen Li laughed in extreme anger.

"Understand that you have been acting all along? Understand that you kept me in the dark like a fool?"

"Xiao Cheng, you hide your intentions so deeply!"

Xiao Cheng did not respond to her questioning.

He merely raised his hand and used two fingers to gently pinch the blade pressed against his throat.

His movement was slow and light.

Shen Li tried to exert force to push the sword forward, only to find that the blade was firmly held, not moving an inch.

She was terrified.

This man was not only unfathomably calculating, but he also possessed such profound martial arts!

"Princess Consort, you cannot kill me."

Xiao Cheng’s voice carried a hint of warmth for the first time, as if sighing.

"Because you know better than I do. If you kill me now, Cangbei will immediately fall apart. The prestige you have just established, the last hope your father has in the imperial court, will all vanish in an instant."

He gently pushed the blade away from his neck.

"You and I are already grasshoppers on the same string. You have no other choice."

Shen Li’s hand gripping the sword hilt began to tremble uncontrollably.

Yes.

She could not kill him.

Not because she couldn't bring herself to do it, but because reason told her she couldn't.

Cangbei had just undergone a major purge, and the hearts of the people were not yet stable. All plans and all blueprints were tied to Xiao Cheng alone.

If he died, the Ning Prince would be the first to pounce and tear Cangbei to shreds.

Political enemies in the court would immediately seize the pretext to impeach her Shen family for "murdering the imperial heir and plotting rebellion."

By then, the Shen family would truly be doomed beyond salvation.

She hated it!

She hated this man’s deep calculations, which had trapped her firmly on his chessboard, unable to move.

She hated herself even more!

She hated that she had actually wavered for a moment because of his words: "My Princess Consort is meant for the battlefield."

So, that wasn't protection; it was merely a chess player asserting ownership over his most important piece.

Just as the atmosphere in the study reached a breaking point.

"Bang! Bang! Bang!"

A series of urgent, etiquette-defying knocks rang out.

"Your Highness! Princess Consort! An eight-hundred-li urgent military report from the capital!"

Outside the door, the guard’s voice was distorted by extreme panic.

Shen Li’s heart sank abruptly.

An eight-hundred-li urgent report!

Unless the border had fallen or the monarch had passed away, such a level of military report would never be used!

The capital...

Her family was all in the capital!

A sense of foreboding made her entire body cold.

A cold light of expectation flashed in Xiao Cheng’s eyes. He said in a deep voice, "Enter!"

The door was pushed open violently, and a guard scrambled in, holding a bamboo tube sealed with wax high above his head.

"Your Highness!"

Xiao Cheng did not reach for it.

He simply stepped aside to clear the way.

The guard was stunned for a moment before realizing, and he tremblingly presented the bamboo tube to Shen Li.

Shen Li’s fingers were ice cold.

Almost by instinct, she took the heavy bamboo tube.

She saw the unique emergency seal of the Shen family on the tube.

Her breathing stopped.

With trembling hands, she broke the wax and poured out a thin roll of silk.

She unfolded it.

The few short lines of text stung her eyes with every word.

"Duke of Zhen, Shen Wei, failed to discipline his subordinates, leading to the rise of a vassal king in the Northern Territory with treasonous intent. He is hereby stripped of all military power, placed under house arrest, and awaits further judgment."

"The Crown Prince’s faction has submitted a memorial, fabricating charges to have the entire Shen family executed to serve as a warning."

"Boom!"

Shen Li’s mind went blank.

The silk in her hand drifted to the floor.

Stripped of military power! House arrest! Execution of the entire family!

The father who had guarded the nation’s gates for a lifetime, who had spent his life in battle and remained loyal...

The family members in the capital, waiting for her news of victory...

The Emperor! The Crown Prince!

How dare they!

A fishy, sweet taste of blood surged up from her throat.

"Pfft—"

Shen Li could no longer suppress it, and a mouthful of blood sprayed out, staining the armor on her chest.

Her body swayed violently, and she almost lost her footing.

"Father..."

For the first time, her eyes revealed the panic and helplessness of a daughter.

That fragility lasted only for an instant.

The next second, monstrous killing intent and rage replaced everything!

"Prepare the horses! Muster the troops!"

She turned around abruptly, her eyes bloodshot, and roared at the door.

"All scout battalions! The Black Armor Guard! Assemble everyone!"

"I am going back to the capital!"

She had to go back! She had to kill her way back!

She would use the sword in her hand to sever the heads of those treacherous villains! She would use the iron cavalry of the Northern Territory to trample that filthy, corrupt imperial palace!

Save her father! Save her family!

However, a hand gripped her arm tightly.

"You cannot go back."

Xiao Cheng’s voice was cold, devoid of any emotion.

Shen Li turned back sharply, her eyes filled with ferocity.

"Let go!"

She roared, her other hand already gripping the hilt of her sword.

Xiao Cheng did not let go.

His strength was astonishing; no matter how Shen Li struggled, she could not break free in the slightest.

"I told you to let go!" Shen Li’s nails almost dug into Xiao Cheng’s flesh.

Xiao Cheng only looked at her coldly, his words chilling to the bone, shattering all her hope.

"Shen Li, calm yourself!"

"Look at the charges written in the military report! 'Failed to discipline subordinates, leading to the rise of a vassal king in the Northern Territory'!"

"That vassal king is me!"

"This is a trap! A trap tailor-made for you, for me, and for the entire Shen family!"

"They are dying for you to take troops back now! As soon as your troops leave the borders of Cangbei, the charge of rebellion will be immediately confirmed!"

"At that time, do you think you are saving your family?"

Xiao Cheng’s voice rose sharply, carrying a cruel, chilling tone.

“No! You are personally sending them to the guillotine!”

“If you go back, not only will you be unable to save anyone, but you yourself will become the best bargaining chip they have to threaten your father! And since we are husband and wife, your treason is my treason! They will use you to force me to submit!”

“When that time comes, we will all die! Not one of your family members will survive!”

These words made her calm down instantly.

All of Shen Li’s movements froze.

The color on her face drained away with visible speed.

Yes, a trap!

This was an incredibly vicious, yet incredibly brilliant, overt scheme.

If she advanced, she would die.

If she retreated, her family would die.

Ahead lay a mountain of blades and a sea of fire; behind lay a bottomless abyss.

She was completely pinned to the spot, with nowhere left to go.

“Then… what should I do?”

She looked at Xiao Cheng in a daze, her voice trembling with a plea she herself had not noticed.

“What should I do… my father… my family…”

Tears finally spilled from her eyes, which had always been so resolute, unable to be held back any longer.

In her entire life, she had never felt as desperate and powerless as she did at this moment.

Xiao Cheng watched her collapse, a flicker of imperceptible pain crossing his eyes, but it was quickly covered by a deeper coldness.

He released her arm.

He knew that the best way to defeat a God of War was not to beat her on the battlefield, but to destroy all the beliefs she fought for.

Now, the time had come.

He bent down, picked up the silk cloth stained with her blood, and calmly held it out to her.

“Princess Consort, now, you have only two choices.”

His voice was calm and cold, carrying a seductive undertone.

“First, you take your troops and charge back to the capital right now, confirming the charge of treason, and die together with your family.”

He paused, his gaze piercing deep into Shen Li’s soul.

“Second, stay.”

“Stay with me, and rule the world together.”

“On the day I ascend the throne, you shall personally clear your Shen family’s name and wash away their grievances before the world.”

“Ahead is a dead end, behind is an abyss. Princess Consort, make your choice.”

chapters.title: From Now On, I Am Your Blade
chapters.content:
The door to the study had been opened at some point.

Mixed with the cold wind, it rushed in violently.

The wind stirred the magnificent blueprints on the desk, making a “rustling” sound, mocking someone’s fate.

The wind also dried the already cold tear tracks on Shen Li’s cheeks.

Her expression was hollow, and she remained motionless.

She stood there, stiff and unmoving.

Xiao Cheng’s two cold choices weighed heavily upon her heart, leaving her nearly suffocated.

Go back, and die with her family.

Stay, and rule the world with him.

Ahead was a dead end, behind was an abyss.

He had blocked every path of retreat she had.

He had calculated her weakness, her sense of duty to her family, and he had calculated that she could not watch the century-old loyal soul of the Shen family be destroyed in a single day.

He had not even given her a third option.

I do not know how much time passed, but finally, she moved.

Shen Li did not look at Xiao Cheng again.

With stiff steps, she walked out of the study that made her feel so suffocated, one step at a time.

She did not pause, nor did she return to her own courtyard.

Instead, as if possessed, she walked toward the military training ground of the Prince’s mansion.

The night was deep, and the training ground was empty.

The cold moonlight spilled onto the racks of cold weapons, reflecting a grim, chilling light.

Shen Li picked up a heavy iron-backed bow, pulled an arrow from the quiver, nocked it, and drew the string.

The bow was pulled into a full moon.

“Hum—”

The bowstring vibrated, emitting a dull roar.

She did not aim at any target; she simply released her fingers toward the empty night sky.

The sharp arrow flew into the endless darkness with a shrill sound, disappearing in an instant.

One arrow.

Another arrow.

She seemed tireless, mechanically repeating the action.

She wanted to shoot out all the anger, humiliation, sorrow, and despair in her heart along with these whistling arrows.

The skin between her thumb and forefinger was worn raw by the rough bowstring, and bright red blood seeped out, but she was completely unaware.

In her mind, two voices were tearing at each other crazily.

One voice roared:

“Go back! Fight your way back! Even if it means death, you must die with your family! My Shen family has no cowards who fear death!”

The other voice sneered:

“Go back? How will you go back? With these few thousand troops under your command, fighting your way thousands of miles back to the capital? Before you even reach the city walls, the charge of treason will have been announced to the world. Your father, your clansmen, will be the first to be buried with you! Are you saving them, or harming them?”

Yes.

Harming them.

Xiao Cheng’s words were heart-piercing, but every word was reasonable.

This was a net cast by the Crown Prince and the Emperor working together, just waiting for her, the enraged moth, to throw herself into it regardless of the consequences.

Her impulsiveness would only become the best excuse for political enemies to attack the Shen family.

Her reckless bravery would only accelerate the destruction of her entire family.

“Father…”

Shen Li dropped the longbow in her hand and finally could not hold on any longer; her knees went weak, and she knelt powerlessly on the ground.

The cold stone floor made her knees ache.

She remembered her father’s face, which was always stern, and she remembered the fleeting warmth in his eyes when he looked at her.

She remembered his teachings since she was a child.

“A-Li, we of the Shen family are born as the shield of the Great Zhou, and die as the soul of the Great Zhou. Loyalty to the monarch and patriotism are our sacred duties.”

Loyalty to the monarch and patriotism?

How ridiculous!

The Shen family had been loyal for generations, and what did they get in return?

Suspicion, framing, and the monstrous crime of “failing to govern subordinates, allowing a vassal king to grow too powerful”!

That emperor, high above, did not need a sharp shield capable of holding its own.

What he needed was a docile, obedient dog!

When the light of the shield threatened his imperial power, he would not hesitate to smash it to pieces with his own hands!

Shen Li’s heart grew cold, inch by inch.

The loyalty to the royal family and the awe of the monarch that had been instilled in her since childhood crumbled and turned to dust in the face of cruel reality.

If the monarch is unjust, how can one speak of a subject’s loyalty?

If the whole world has betrayed my Shen family, why should I, Shen Li, shed another drop of blood for this world!

Then, only the second choice remained.

Stay.

Accompany Xiao Cheng on that path of rebellion, which was destined to be a mountain of corpses and a sea of blood.

Bet her own fate, and the lives of the entire Shen family, on the man who was so deep in his schemes and had deceived her for so many years.

How absurd! How ironic!

The “vassal king” who had driven her family into a desperate situation was now her only straw to clutch at.

Shen Li raised her head and looked at the cold crescent moon in the sky, smiling miserably.

She remembered the moment on the grasslands when Xiao Cheng pulled her behind him, using that arrogant posture to block everything for her.

The peace of mind at that moment was real.

The heartbeat at that moment was also real.

But looking back now, that peace of mind was more like a carefully woven net, luring her, the prey who was already covered in wounds.

He needed her.

He needed the military power in her hands.

He needed her, the sharpest war blade in the Northern Territory.

Therefore, he would bestow a little bit of “protection” and a little bit of “warmth” at the right time to buy her heart.

What a brilliant tactic!

He had long since seen through the little bit of feminine softness beneath her hard shell.

Does she hate him?

Yes.

She hates that he used her so thoroughly.

But now that things have come to this, what is the use of hate?

She closed her eyes, and the huge blueprint in Xiao Cheng’s study involuntarily appeared in her mind.

Training troops, reclaiming wasteland, opening mines, trade…

What a magnificent and meticulous plan it was.

This man was despicable and ruthless, but he… had the ability.

He had the ability to turn this barren land of Cangbei into an impregnable kingdom.

He had the ability to raise an iron army capable of contending with the world.

He also… had the ability to fight back to the capital one day and completely overthrow that corrupt dynasty.

Only then could the Shen family’s grievances be cleared.

Only then would her father and her family have a day to see the light again.

This was the only path.

A path… paved with betrayal and blood, a thorny road leading to hope.

The night grew deeper.

The cold wind on the training ground dried her last tears.

When the first ray of dawn pierced the darkness and illuminated Cangbei City, Shen Li slowly stood up from the cold ground.

In her eyes, there was no longer the struggle, anger, and despair of the previous night.

Only a kind of absolute calm remained.

It was the purest resolution that remained after seeing reality clearly and abandoning all illusions.

She straightened her disheveled armor, stood tall, and walked back toward the study.

…

Xiao Cheng had not slept all night.

He sat behind that huge desk, waiting quietly.

He knew what choice Shen Li would make.

He also knew how cruel this choice was for her.

When the door was pushed open and that familiar figure appeared before him again, his heart still tightened uncontrollably.

She looked no different from yesterday.

The same silver armor, the same posture.

Yet, Xiao Cheng keenly sensed that something had completely changed.

The fire in her had been extinguished.

In those eyes that were always bright, there was now only a bottomless, cold pool.

Shen Li did not speak.

She walked to the center of the study and stopped three steps away from him.

Then, under Xiao Cheng’s calm gaze, she slowly drew the sword at her waist.

“Clang—”

The blade left its sheath, flashing with cold light.

That sword was forged for her by her father’s own hands when she was sixteen. A simple, archaic character for "Loyalty" was engraved upon its blade.

She had once carried this sword, fighting north and south for the Great Zhou, winning glorious military merits.

And today, she would use this sword to sever her past.

Shen Li did not point the sword at Xiao Cheng.

She merely raised it, and with the sharp tip, she sliced through her own left palm without a moment’s hesitation.

Blood surged out instantly.

It trickled down her palm, drop by drop, landing on the cold floor tiles and blooming into mesmerizing flowers of blood.

She did not furrow her brow, completely indifferent to the pain.

She raised that blood-drenched hand and pointed it toward the window, toward the black dragon banner of the Prince’s Mansion fluttering in the wind.

Then, she spoke, word by word, in a voice devoid of any emotion, calm to the point of terror.

"I, Shen Li, hereby take an oath."

"From this day forth, I am no longer your wife."

These words pierced deeply into Xiao Cheng’s heart.

Shen Li’s gaze was fixed directly upon him, a look so foreign it made his heart tremble.

"I am the sharpest blade in your hand!"

"Wherever you point, I shall strike!"

"Where the blade falls, all rebels shall perish!"

She paused, her voice carrying the final trace of the obsession that belonged to "Shen Li."

"I only ask that on the day you ascend the throne, you keep your promise: restore the innocence of my entire Shen family and clear our name before the world!"

This was no longer a promise between husband and wife.

This was the heaviest and most resolute pledge of loyalty from a commander to the monarch of her choosing.

With her own blood, she had severed all emotional entanglements between them.

She had turned herself into a pure weapon, existing solely for revenge.

Xiao Cheng looked at her hollow, resolute eyes and the blood continuously dripping from her palm; a subtle yet distinct pain radiated from his heart.

He knew he had obtained it.

He had gained a peerless blade capable of helping him clear the thorns and conquer the world.

He had also, forever, lost the Shen Li who would grow angry at him, who would panic for him, and who would stand behind him with a look of bewilderment.

He had personally pushed her heart into an endless abyss.

Yet, his face could not show the slightest sign of being moved.

The path of an emperor is inherently lonely.

Meeting her icy gaze, he slowly rose from his chair.

He walked down the steps and came to stand before her.

He did not look at her bleeding hand, nor did he offer any words of comfort.

He simply nodded calmly.

"Very well."

Two words, concise and to the point.

He had accepted her loyalty, and he had accepted this new, cold, and ruthless relationship between them.

Having received his promise, Shen Li did not say another word.

She withdrew her hand, letting the blood soak the arm guards of her armor, sheathed her sword, turned, and walked out the door.

Her retreating figure was so resolute, without a hint of reluctance.

"Where are you going?" Xiao Cheng finally could not help but ask.

Shen Li’s footsteps faltered for a moment.

She did not look back.

"Since the blade has been unsheathed, it must, naturally, taste blood."

Her voice was bone-chilling.

"I am going to the barracks to reorganize the Black Armor Cavalry."

"Waiting for the Prince’s first command."

chapters.title: Want to Touch Me? Ask My Iron Cavalry First!
chapters.content:
The wind in Cangbei seemed to carry the scent of blood overnight.

The news that Prince Ning had assembled an army of thirty thousand, under the banner of "clearing the monarch's side and suppressing rebels," with his spearhead pointed directly at Cangbei City, struck this border town—which had only just caught its breath—like a massive boulder.

Panic spread like a plague.

The commoners in the city had only just emerged from the shadows of the Ma family and the Black Wind Stronghold, having just been allocated fields and property, and were full of hope for their future lives.

Now, an army of thirty thousand was pressing upon their borders.

Who was Prince Ning? He was a veteran feudal lord of the Northern Territory, with strong soldiers and sturdy horses, his strength far exceeding that of the still-unstable Cangbei.

Moreover, rumors were flying throughout the city.

"Have you heard? The Princess Consort’s family, the Duke of the State’s mansion in the capital, has fallen!"

"They say the Duke was lax in governing his troops, which allowed our Prince to grow too powerful, so the Emperor stripped him of his office and placed him under house arrest!"

"Doesn't that mean we in Cangbei have become rootless duckweed? Criminals of the imperial court?"

"Prince Ning is coming under the banner of 'suppressing rebels.' We’re finished; we’ll all be buried with them!"

The pillar of the Prince’s Mansion, the Shen family, had fallen.

This news was more despairing than the thirty thousand enemy troops themselves.

Within the city, hearts were filled with anxiety; some merchants even began to secretly pack their valuables, preparing to abandon the city at any moment.

Inside the Prince’s Mansion council hall, the atmosphere was even more oppressive.

All the civil and military officials of Cangbei who held any weight were gathered here.

Everyone wore a grave expression, filled with unease.

The newly appointed County Magistrate, an old official who had been pushed out of the capital, wiped the cold sweat from his forehead and spoke tremblingly.

"Pr... Prince, Prince Ning is powerful, with thirty thousand elite troops, while our army... has fewer than ten thousand capable soldiers, and more than half of those are newly surrendered troops. The morale is unstable."

"Furthermore, he carries the banner of the imperial court. If we resist, wouldn't that... wouldn't that truly confirm the charge of rebellion?"

"In this old official's humble opinion, perhaps... perhaps we should prepare a generous gift, plead guilty to Prince Ning, and cede some interests; perhaps... perhaps we can trade for a moment of peace."

These words voiced the inner thoughts of most of the civil officials present.

Surrender, sue for peace.

It was the only way they could think of to save their lives.

Several newly promoted military officers, though resentful, knew the vast disparity in strength and kept their heads bowed in silence.

The entire council hall was permeated with a sense of defeat.

Xiao Cheng sat upright in the main seat, his expression solemn.

He did not speak, merely scanning everyone calmly.

He saw their fear, their wavering, their cowardice.

He remained silent, letting this oppressive atmosphere grow even heavier.

Just then, the heavy doors of the council hall were pushed open with a creak.

A silver figure walked in, silhouetted against the light.

It was Shen Li.

She had changed into a brand-new set of armor, polished until it gleamed, the plates reflecting a cold light.

There was no expression on her face, and those eyes, once bright as fire, were now like two bottomless, icy abysses.

Her pace was not fast, but every step seemed to land on the heartbeats of those present.

She walked into the council hall, ignored everyone’s gaze, and went straight to the side of the sand table, standing quietly, her hand resting lightly on the hilt of her sword.

She was like a god of slaughter from the netherworld—silent, yet radiating a suffocating sense of oppression.

The County Magistrate, who had just been pontificating about surrender, was swept by her icy gaze, and his remaining words instantly stuck in his throat; he could not utter a single syllable.

The entire council hall was deathly quiet.

Finally, Xiao Cheng moved.

He slowly stood up and picked up the black iron tiger tally from the desk, which represented the highest military command in Cangbei.

He did not walk toward the bowed military officers, nor did he pay any heed to the trembling civil officials.

Step by step, he walked to Shen Li.

In the stunned gaze of everyone, Xiao Cheng held the tiger tally with both hands and solemnly presented it to Shen Li.

His voice was clear and steady, echoing through the council hall.

"From this moment on, the three armies of Cangbei, inside and outside the city walls, the power to mobilize all troops belongs solely to General Shen!"

General Shen!

He called her General Shen!

Not the Princess Consort!

This title exploded over their heads like a thunderclap!

They were all bewildered.

Had the Prince gone mad?

The Shen family had just lost power; not only did he not distance himself, but he had handed the lifeline of all of Cangbei into Shen Li’s hands?

This was a reckless gamble!

To stake his own life and the future of all Cangbei on a woman whose family had just been purged by the imperial court!

Yet, facing this heavy trust, Shen Li remained expressionless.

She did not decline, did not hesitate, and did not show the slightest sign of being moved.

She simply reached out with her metal-gauntleted hand, took the cold tiger tally, and gripped it tightly.

"Command accepted."

Two words, cold and crisp.

She turned to face the massive sand table, as if that were the only world that mattered.

"Pass my orders!"

Her voice rose sharply, filled with the majesty of a commander!

"Where is the commander of the Scout Battalion!"

A sturdy general leaped out and knelt on one knee: "This subordinate is here!"

"Order your unit to leave the city immediately, in groups of ten, and spread out within a hundred miles! I want to know within half an hour where the vanguard of Prince Ning’s army is, how many men they have, and who the commander is!"

"This subordinate obeys!"

"Where is the commander of the Black Armor Guard!"

"This subordinate is here!"

"Order your unit to take control of the four city gates. From this moment on, Cangbei City is open for entry but closed for exit! Anyone who attempts to desert in the face of battle, regardless of rank or status, shall be executed without mercy!"

"This subordinate obeys!"

The merchants and officials who had been thinking of fleeing felt a chill in their hearts.

"Where is the commander of the Garrison Army!"

"This subordinate is here!"

"Order your unit to reinforce the city defenses immediately! Rolling stones, logs, boiling oil, and arrows—get them all to the city walls! All laborers are to be organized into auxiliary battalions to assist in the defense! Any negligence will be dealt with by military law!"

"This subordinate obeys!"

Order after order was issued from her mouth, clear and swift.

There was not a hint of hesitation, not a moment of dragging her feet.

She did not even look at the sand table; every inch of the terrain around Cangbei City was already etched into her mind.

Those military officers who had been full of doubts and low morale felt their fear and unease being dispelled bit by bit under this series of decisive and stern commands.

In their place was a long-lost feeling called "fighting spirit"!

This was the God of War they were familiar with!

The General Shen who had led them to be invincible on the northern battlefields!

As long as she was here, the sky would not fall!

Finally, Shen Li’s gaze fell upon the commander of the cavalry unit that had been exchanged for three thousand warhorses.

"Black Armor Iron Cavalry, where are you!"

"Present!" The newly appointed cavalry commander, a fierce warrior promoted from the Shen family's personal guards, was flushed with excitement.

A glimmer of light finally ignited in Shen Li's eyes.

It was the flame of revenge.

"All personnel, armor up! Feed the warhorses! Stand by inside the West Gate!"

"I want you to become the... nightmare of Prince Ning's thirty-thousand-strong army!"

"We swear to obey, even unto death!"

The atmosphere in the council chamber surged.

The previous despondency and fear were swept away.

Every general stood tall, their spirits soaring.

After finalizing everything, Shen Li held the tiger tally and turned to leave.

She was going to the city walls herself to oversee the defenses.

As she passed Xiao Cheng, her footsteps paused, almost imperceptibly.

Their gazes met.

Around them, messengers and generals hurried back and forth; the world was a cacophony of noise.

But in this moment, they saw only each other.

Xiao Cheng watched her.

He watched the madness beneath her icy exterior—the desire to destroy everything.

He did not speak.

He simply met her gaze and, with his lips, silently mouthed four words to her.

"Waiting for your triumphant return."

Shen Li’s hand, gripping the tiger tally, tightened abruptly.

The cold metal pressed hard against her palm.

She did not respond, giving him only the slightest of nods before turning away.

Her silver armor disappeared decisively through the doorway of the council chamber.

...

Dusk.

On the West Gate tower of Cangbei City, the northern wind howled.

Shen Li stood alone behind the battlements, gazing at the distant horizon.

Behind her, there was no one else.

She had sent all her deputy generals away to their respective posts.

At this moment, she only needed silence.

Below the city tower lay a black ocean.

Three thousand Black Armor Iron Cavalry, with bits in their mouths and hooves wrapped, gathered silently within the massive gate tunnel.

Black armor, black warhorses, black spears.

They were like a group of ghosts from hell, quietly awaiting the order to attack.

This was her blade.

It was the blade of vengeance she had forged with her family's honor, her own marriage, and... a heavy price.

In the distance, a line of dust slowly rose.

The dust grew thicker and closer, eventually merging into a sky-filling cloud.

Prince Ning's army had arrived.

The sound of hooves was like thunder; banners stood like a forest.

An aura of slaughter swept toward them.

On the city walls, the sound of soldiers nervously swallowing could be heard.

But Shen Li smiled.

That smile, appearing on her face, looked eerie and grim.

This was the first battle of her revenge for her family.

It was also her first battle as a "blade."

She turned around and gave a cold order to the messenger behind her.

chapters.title: The Iron Cavalry Released
chapters.content:
"Open the city gates."

When these three words escaped Shen Li's lips, a deathly silence fell over the tower.

The messenger thought he had misheard; he widened his eyes, staring in disbelief at that silver-clad back.

"Gen... General?"

Open the gates?

Outside were thirty thousand tigers and wolves!

To open the gates now was no different from offering one's neck to the blade, a path to certain death!

Shen Li did not look back, her voice carrying a coldness that brooked no argument.

"I will say it again: open the city gates!"

The voice was not loud, but it struck heavily against everyone's hearts.

The messenger jolted, and no longer daring to hesitate, he raised his command flag and shouted with all his might toward the city below.

"The General orders—open—the—gates!"

"Creeeeeak—"

The massive gate, so heavy it required dozens of men to turn the winch, groaned as it slowly swung inward.

A beam of light pierced through the gap, illuminating the silent black ocean within the tunnel.

Prince Ning's army outside also noticed this strange scene.

The commotion in the vanguard soon reached the center army.

Prince Ning, Xiao Jing, was riding proudly beneath the commander's banner.

He wore golden armor and a haughty smile; in his eyes, Cangbei City was already in his grasp.

With the Shen family fallen, that waste Xiao Cheng was like a tiger with its claws broken, nothing to fear.

He had even planned how to humiliate his seventh brother—who had always overshadowed him in the capital—after breaking the city, and how to "enjoy" the world-renowned God of War of the North.

"Report—! Your Highness, the gates of... Cangbei City have opened!"

A scout rode up, his voice filled with shock and suspicion.

"Oh?"

Xiao Jing raised an eyebrow, his smile widening.

"What? Is that waste Xiao Cheng opening the gates to surrender so soon? I thought he could hold out for a few more days."

A strategist beside him stroked his beard and laughed, "It must be that morale in the city has collapsed, and knowing resistance is hopeless, they are opening the gates to beg for mercy and seek your Highness's forgiveness."

"Hahaha!" Xiao Jing laughed aloud. "He knows his place! Pass the order: tell the vanguard to prepare to enter the city. Remember, do not harm my Seventh Princess; I want her alive!"

However, his laughter had not yet faded.

A sudden change occurred!

From the slowly opening gates, it was not envoys bearing letters of surrender or soldiers kneeling for mercy that poured out.

It was a black torrent!

A torrent forged of steel and the will to kill, capable of swallowing everything!

Three thousand Black Armor Iron Cavalry surged out of the gate tunnel in silence!

No war drums, no horns, not even a shout.

Only the rhythmic, soul-shattering thunder of hooves!

"Boom—"

The earth trembled!

The three thousand cavalry formed a sharp, peerless conical battle formation.

And at the very tip of that formation, the sharpest, most dazzling spearhead, was Shen Li in her silver armor!

Her silver spear was leveled forward, the tip pointing directly at Prince Ning's massive commander's banner!

The northern wind whipped the blood-red cloak behind her!

Atop the city tower, Xiao Cheng stood with his hands behind his back.

He watched the heroic scene below calmly, watching that indomitable figure.

Su Wan stood behind him, her face pale.

She had envisioned countless strategies for defending the city—scorched earth, luring the enemy deep, divide and conquer...

She had never imagined that Shen Li would choose the most fierce, the most insane, and the most impossible one!

Three thousand against thirty thousand, a frontal charge!

"Your Highness... this... this is too risky!" Her voice trembled.

Xiao Cheng did not look back, only saying faintly, "This is not a risk."

"This is her war."

"As a blade, severing everything in front of her is her destiny."

His tone was calm, but the hand held behind his back was clenched tight, involuntarily.

Below the city.

The smile on Prince Ning Xiao Jing's face froze completely.

He was no fool.

When that black torrent appeared, when he felt that tangible, overwhelming killing intent rushing toward him, he knew he had been wrong.

Wrong beyond measure!

This was no surrender!

This was a fight to the death!

"Madwoman! She's a madwoman!"

Xiao Jing's face turned deathly pale, and he roared at the top of his lungs.

"Archers! Fire! Fire, quickly!"

"Vanguard! Hold the line! Hold the line for me!"

Prince Ning's vanguard consisted mostly of infantry and some light cavalry; they had been in a loose formation preparing to enter the city. How could they have expected such a terrifying cavalry charge?

The order was given, but how could a disorganized formation execute it effectively?

A sparse rain of arrows flew toward the black torrent, but it was like throwing stones into the sea.

The arrows struck the heavy armor of the Black Armor Iron Cavalry, creating a clattering sound before bouncing off, unable to cause any effective damage.

By now, the black spear formed by the three thousand cavalry had already slammed into the ranks of Prince Ning's army!

"Pfft—!"

There was no earth-shattering collision as one might imagine.

Only the dull, sickening sound of blades slicing into flesh.

The charge of the Black Armor Iron Cavalry was unstoppable!

The soldiers of Prince Ning's army who stood in their way were easily knocked aside and torn apart!

Shen Li led the charge, her silver spear turning into a streak of silver lightning!

She didn't even need to make any deliberate moves.

She simply held her spear level, maintaining her charging posture.

Any enemy in her path would, in the next instant, have their chest pierced by the sharp tip, only to be sent flying by the immense impact!

A captain of the Ning army, confident in his own strength, brandished a heavy blade, attempting to block her.

"Die!"

He roared, swinging his blade down.

Shen Li didn't even glance at him.

She merely flicked her wrist.

The shaft of her silver spear parried upward at an incredible angle.

"Clang!"

With a crisp sound, the captain felt an irresistible force travel from the blade; his hand split open instantly, and the sword flew from his grip.

Before he could even feel terror, the silver spearhead flashed across his throat.

A head soared into the sky!

Blood sprayed out, splashing all over Shen Li.

Her expression did not change in the slightest.

Cold, decisive.

The Black Armor Iron Cavalry behind her were even more like precision killing machines.

They moved in groups of three and teams of five, their coordination flawless to the extreme.

Spears thrust, sabers slashed.

They cut through the enemy lines without effort.

The formation of Prince Ning's army was pierced through in an instant!

Panic began to spread.

"Demons! They are demons!"

"We can't stop them! We can't stop them at all!"

The soldiers of the vanguard completely collapsed.

They dropped their weapons, screaming and turning to flee.

And this flight triggered a total rout.

Men trampled over men.

The previously orderly formation turned into chaos in an instant.

In the center army, Prince Ning Xiao Jing watched his vanguard being slaughtered with ease, watching that silver figure drawing closer and closer, his heart nearly leaping out of his throat.

"Trash! A bunch of trash!"

He drew his sword in a fit of rage and cut down a retreating soldier who had tried to flee toward him.

"Center army! The center army must hold! Elite guard battalion! Stop her for this Prince!"

"Stop that madwoman!"

However, the army's morale had already collapsed, and the defeat was like a landslide.

Shen Li's goal had been crystal clear from the very beginning.

—Decapitation!

Ignoring the scattered, fleeing soldiers, she led her most elite cavalry along the gap she had just torn open, moving with unwavering determination, driving straight toward the commander's flag of Prince Ning's center army!

Standing in her way was Prince Ning's elite guard battalion.

These were the most elite forces at his disposal, well-equipped and highly trained.

"Form ranks! Fire arrows!"

The commander of the elite guard battalion shouted his orders, his voice hoarse.

Hundreds of guards quickly formed a dense phalanx, attempting to use their flesh and blood to block this black torrent of iron.

Looking at the wall of shields and spears flashing with cold light ahead, a cold sneer curled the corners of Shen Li's mouth.

She abruptly thrust her silver spear into the holster beside her saddle.

Then, to the horror of everyone watching, she took a massive iron-backed bow from her back!

She bent the bow and nocked an arrow.

Three wolf-tooth arrows were placed on the bowstring at once!

Her arms erupted with astonishing strength, drawing the bowstring into a full moon!

"Hum—"

The bowstring vibrated, emitting a roar like a wild beast!

She was not aiming at the ordinary soldiers.

She was aiming at the commander of the elite guard battalion who was currently issuing orders!

"Fire!"

The three sharp arrows, flying in a triangular formation, tore through the air with a shrill whistle!

The commander only saw three cold stars rapidly enlarging before his eyes; he instinctively raised his shield.

"Thud! Thud! Thud!"

Three muffled sounds followed, almost simultaneously!

The first arrow pierced through the shield in his hand!

The second arrow pierced through the armor on his chest!

The third arrow passed through his body, exiting from his back!

The expression on the elite guard commander's face froze at that moment.

He looked down at the three bloody holes in his chest, his eyes filled with disbelief.

Then, he fell straight backward.

The commander had fallen!

The elite guard battalion's phalanx fell into fatal chaos!

Shen Li did not give them any chance to reorganize.

She dropped the iron-backed bow, gripped her silver spear once more, and dug her legs into her horse's flanks!

"All troops—charge!"

Her cold voice rang across the battlefield!

"Kill!"

Three thousand black-armored cavalrymen let out the first roar since the battle began!

The roar converged into a monstrous wave of sound, completely shattering the enemy's final psychological defense!

The black torrent slammed fiercely into the elite guard battalion's phalanx.

This time, it was a total crushing!

Shen Li led the charge, her silver spear pointing the way, unstoppable!

She could already see, not far away, the massive golden commander's flag that represented Prince Ning's status!

She could also see the man beneath the flag, dressed in golden armor, his face deathly pale, panicking as he prepared to turn his horse and flee!

Xiao Jing!

A terrifying murderous intent erupted in Shen Li's eyes!

She raised her blood-stained silver spear, pointed it from afar at the commander's flag, and with all her might, issued her first—and bloodiest—bounty as a "blade"!

"Whoever cuts down the commander's flag shall be rewarded with a thousand gold pieces and promoted three ranks!"

"Whoever kills Xiao Jing shall be enfeoffed as a Marquis of Ten Thousand Households!"

chapters.title: A Legend Born in Battle
chapters.content:
This tempting bounty exploded over the roaring battlefield like a thunderclap!

Every word turned into the hottest stimulant, injected fiercely into the veins of the three thousand black-armored cavalrymen!

Marquis of Ten Thousand Households!

That was the pinnacle that countless soldiers dared not even dream of in their entire lives!

And now, this monumental achievement was right before them!

It was right there on the man in golden armor who had already begun to panic!

"Kill!"

It was unclear who shouted first.

The next moment, a roar like a crashing tsunami erupted from the chests of the three thousand cavalrymen!

"Kill! Kill! Kill!"

Their eyes turned blood-red in an instant!

These were no longer the eyes of soldiers, but of a pack of starving wolves that had caught the scent of blood and spotted the fattest prey!

The cone-shaped battle formation, already sharp and peerless, seemed at this moment to be infused with a will to destroy everything!

The speed was faster!

The killing intent was thicker!

The black torrent had gone completely berserk!

The Prince Ning's elite guard battalion standing in their way felt the pressure instantly.

It was a terrifying sense of oppression that felt as if it would crush their very souls!

They were elites, too; they had been valiant as well.

But in the face of this iron torrent composed of three thousand beasts driven completely mad by the promise of becoming a "Marquis of Ten Thousand Households," their formation and their courage were as fragile as paper!

"Hold! Hold for this Prince!"

Prince Ning, Xiao Jing, had completely lost the composure of a prince. He brandished his sword, his voice becoming shrill and piercing due to fear.

He watched that silver figure moving through his elite guard formation as if it were empty space, drawing closer and closer to him.

That woman!

The woman he had once teased at a banquet, the woman he had dismissed as nothing more than a pretty ornament for his useless seventh brother!

At this moment, she had transformed into an Asura returned from hell!

Every swing of her silver spear brought up a mist of blood!

Every collision of her warhorse sent several guards flying!

She wasn't fighting; she was harvesting!

Xiao Jing's heart hammered wildly, threatening to burst from his chest.

He was afraid.

He was truly afraid!

He couldn't understand how a woman could be this strong!

And he couldn't understand even more how that waste, Xiao Cheng, dared to entrust military power to such a madwoman!

Charging out of the city?

Three thousand against thirty thousand?

Was this something a normal person could do?

"Squelch!"

Another guard commander attempted to use his own body to block Shen Li's horse, only to be pierced through, armor and all, by her spear!

Shen Li flicked her wrist, tossing the corpse off the tip of her spear, her cold gaze piercing through the crowd and locking onto Xiao Jing!

Their eyes met.

Xiao Jing felt a chill run through his entire body!

What kind of eyes were those!

No anger, no hatred, only a hollow, pure murderous intent!

It was as if, in her eyes, he was already a dead man!

"Stop her! Someone stop her for this Prince!"

Xiao Jing screamed hysterically, and he even instinctively shrank back.

The guards around him rushed forward one after another, fearless of death, attempting to use their flesh and blood to buy their Prince even a fleeting moment of respite.

However, it was useless.

In the face of absolute combat superiority and a fanatical will to win, all resistance seemed pale and weak.

The black-armored cavalry behind Shen Li had completely pierced through the elite guard battalion's defenses.

They were like sharp scalpels, precisely cutting and dismantling Prince Ning's final barrier.

The warhorses of the Snow Eagle Tribe displayed their unparalleled advantages.

They were taller and had more stamina than the horses of the Central Plains, with faster sprinting speeds and greater impact force!

Combined with the battle formation designed specifically for cavalry charges by the Shen family army, it was a match made in heaven!

Prince Ning's army formation was bloated and massive; it looked intimidating but was actually fragile.

And Shen Li's three thousand cavalrymen were a red-hot, poisoned steel blade!

With one stroke, they could easily cut it in two!

"Your Highness! We can't hold them!"

"Your Highness, flee! As long as the green hills remain, there's no need to worry about firewood!"

A deputy general, his face covered in blood, rushed to the front of Xiao Jing's horse and shouted desperately.

These words completely shattered Xiao Jing's psychological defenses.

Flee?

Yes! Flee!

He couldn't die here!

He still had a bright future, he still had endless wealth and glory!

How could he die at the hands of such a madwoman!

"Flee! Quickly, flee!"

Xiao Jing grabbed onto the suggestion like a lifeline. He threw away his sword, ripped the golden helmet that symbolized his status from his head, and smashed it onto the ground.

He turned his horse around and, with all his might, whipped the horse's rump!

The warhorse, stung by pain, let out a neigh and carried him, fleeing in a pathetic scramble toward the rear!

He didn't even issue a single order for his army to retreat!

Under the gaze of tens of thousands of soldiers, he was the first to run!

The commander-in-chief had fled the battlefield!

This scene was more devastating than any news of defeat!

Every soldier of Prince Ning's army who was still struggling to hold on saw it.

They saw their Prince pathetically abandon them to save his own life.

Their faith collapsed at that moment.

"The Prince has run away!"

"Prince Ning has been defeated! He ran away first!"

Cries of despair rose one after another in the chaotic army.

The morale of the army collapsed completely!

Shen Li looked at the fleeing back and smiled coldly.

She did not pursue.

Because her goal, from beginning to end, was never Xiao Jing's worthless head.

It was the massive commander's flag behind him, which represented Prince Ning's majesty and power!

To catch the bandits, first catch the king.

If the king has fled, cutting down his commander's flag would have the same effect!

"Whoever cuts down the commander's flag shall be rewarded with a thousand gold pieces and promoted three ranks!"

Her cold voice rang out once again!

A centurion of the black-armored cavalry, closest to the commander's flag, heard the order, and a terrifying glint erupted in his eyes!

He didn't dare dream of being a Marquis of Ten Thousand Households, but a promotion of three ranks and a thousand gold pieces were equally massive temptations!

"Brothers! Follow me!"

He roared, leading a dozen of his cavalrymen, and charged forward without hesitation toward the golden flag still fluttering in the wind!

The soldiers guarding the flag had already lost all will to fight after seeing their commander flee.

They offered only symbolic resistance before being easily torn apart by these dozen tigers!

The centurion took the lead. Without even dismounting, the moment his warhorse reached the flagpole, he leaped from the saddle!

Mid-air, the saber in his hand traced a brilliant, icy arc!

“Crack!”

A sharp snap!

The massive flagpole, which would have required several men to encircle, broke instantly.

The enormous golden commander’s banner fell slowly, powerlessly, toward the ground.

Finally, with a dull thud, it slammed into the blood-soaked, muddy earth.

It was soiled.

Completely ruined.

The moment the banner fell, the entire battlefield went deathly still.

Every soldier in the Ning King’s army stopped what they were doing, staring blankly at the fallen flag.

Their expressions shifted from confusion to terror, and finally, into absolute despair.

The commander’s banner is the soul of an army.

Without a soul, the army is dead.

“It’s over…”

“We’ve lost…”

Someone, it was unclear who, was the first to drop their weapon.

“Clang!”

The crisp sound became the spark that ignited a chain reaction.

“Clang! Clang! Clang!”

Thousands upon thousands of soldiers threw down their armor and weapons, crying out as they turned and fled.

The defeat was like a collapsing mountain!

The army of thirty thousand completely disintegrated in that moment.

They were no longer an army; they were a flock of terrified sheep, scattering in every direction, wishing only that their parents had given them more legs to run with.

Men shoved men; men trampled men.

The casualties caused by their own stampede were even more severe than those caused by the charge of the Black Armor Cavalry!

Atop the city gate tower.

Su Wan stood with her mouth agape, her pretty face deathly pale, unable to close it for a long time.

She had envisioned countless outcomes.

A pyrrhic victory, a narrow escape, or even being forced back.

The only thing she had never imagined was a complete, crushing, absolute victory like this!

Three thousand defeating thirty thousand!

And doing so through the most incredible method: a direct frontal charge!

This had transcended the realm of military strategy.

This was pure, unreasonable, overwhelming combat power!

She looked at the figure standing amidst the thousands, clad in silver armor and holding a long spear, and for the first time, a feeling called “awe” stirred in her heart.

So, this was the true God of War.

So, this was the kind of war that belonged to Shen Li.

Xiao Cheng stood with his hands behind his back, his expression remaining calm.

Yet, deep within his profound eyes, waves that outsiders could not fathom were surging.

There was admiration, pride, and a trace of possessiveness that was difficult to detect.

This was his blade.

A peerless weapon capable of making the entire Northern Territory tremble!

On the battlefield.

Shen Li slowly raised the silver spear in her hand.

All the Black Armor Cavalry came to a halt, surrounding her in a black ring.

They looked at her back, their eyes filled with fanatical worship!

“Do not pursue a desperate foe.”

Shen Li’s voice was not loud, yet it reached everyone’s ears clearly.

“Clean up the battlefield, round up the prisoners, and tally the losses.”

Orders were issued methodically from her lips.

She was not intoxicated by victory.

Her composure stood in stark contrast to the chaos around her.

The sun set in the west.

The blood-red afterglow bathed the entire battlefield.

Corpses lay everywhere; blood flowed like a river.

Shen Li stood alone on her horse amidst the sea of blood and mountains of corpses.

Her silver armor had long since been stained red with blood.

The northern wind whipped the blood-red cloak behind her, snapping loudly.

She had won.

With a hearty and thorough victory, she had broken the spine of the Ning King and established the prestige of Cangbei.

From this day on, there would be no more Ning King in the North.

And her title, the “God of War of the North,” would from this day forward spread across the entire northern land in a brand-new, more iron-blooded, and more domineering way!

This was the first time she had earned a glorious reputation that truly belonged to her, Shen Li, alone!

chapters.title: My Wife Has Come of Age
chapters.content:
When the first rays of the morning sun fell upon the weathered walls of Cangbei City, the massive city gates slowly opened once again.

This time, there was no grim atmosphere of a desperate charge.

Instead, there were cheers like a crashing sea!

“We won! We won!”

“Long live General Shen! Long live the Prince!”

The people of the city spontaneously poured into the streets, crowding the roadsides, craning their necks, their faces glowing with the wild joy of survival and heartfelt reverence.

At the end of the street, the black iron tide was slowly returning.

The three thousand Black Armor Cavalry still had the blood and dust of yesterday on their armor, and their brows still carried the lingering aura of slaughter.

Their pace was the pace of victors.

Their chests were held high!

They surrounded the silver figure.

Shen Li was still in her blood-stained silver armor. She wore no helmet, and her long, ink-black hair was somewhat disheveled by the northern wind. A few dried bloodstains on her stunning face only added a touch of breathtaking color.

She had returned.

She had returned with a glorious victory worthy of being recorded in history!

The people looked at her with unreserved fanaticism and worship in their eyes.

They threw flowers and shouted her name.

“General Shen!”

“God of War of the North!”

Listening to these shouts, Shen Li’s expression remained calm, though a faint glimmer seemed to flicker deep within her cold eyes.

When the procession reached the entrance of the Prince’s Mansion, the crowd automatically parted to form a path.

In front of the mansion, Xiao Cheng stood in his black princely robes, hands behind his back.

Behind him were Su Wan and a group of Cangbei civil officials.

All eyes were focused on the two of them.

One was the nominal ruler of Cangbei.

The other was the commander who had just cemented her name as the God of War with an extraordinary victory.

Under everyone’s gaze, Xiao Cheng moved.

He did not stand still and wait; instead, he took a step, walking forward, step by step, to meet Shen Li’s warhorse.

The surrounding cheers gradually subsided.

Everyone held their breath, watching the scene.

Xiao Cheng reached the front of Shen Li’s horse and stopped.

He looked up at the woman sitting high in the saddle.

In his eyes, there was no trace of princely airs, only undisguised, pure admiration and immense pride.

Then, he performed a shocking action.

He reached out and, as naturally as could be, took the reins from Shen Li’s hand.

He was leading the horse for her!

With the dignity of a Prince, he was leading the horse for his General, his Princess!

“Boom!”

The crowd erupted completely!

The Black Armor Cavalry, who had just experienced a bloody battle, were so excited their faces turned red; they pounded their chest plates, creating a thunderous roar!

This was the highest honor their lord could bestow upon their commander!

And it was the supreme glory for all of them!

Shen Li was also stunned.

She looked down at the man holding her reins, a smile on his lips.

The sunlight fell on his profile, outlining his features with perfect clarity.

His hand was warm and strong.

That warmth seemed to pass through the cold reins and into her palm.

Her heart, which had become hardened by the destruction of her family and her blood oath, felt an uncontrollable crack appear at that moment.

A trace of warmth quietly seeped in through that crack.

She opened her mouth, wanting to say something, but found her throat dry.

In the end, she remained silent, allowing him to lead her warhorse, step by step, into the gates of the Prince’s Mansion.

This scene was deeply etched into the hearts of every soldier and citizen of Cangbei.

The Prince and the Princess, the lord and the general, were of one heart and one mind.

Cangbei was as secure as a fortress!

…

That night, the Prince’s Mansion held a grand banquet to celebrate the victory.

The entire city of Cangbei was immersed in the joy of triumph.

However, when the noise of the banquet faded, the study of the Prince’s Mansion remained brightly lit.

Beside the massive sand table, Xiao Cheng and Su Wan stood facing each other.

Spread out before them was not a map of Cangbei City, but a detailed map of the entire Northern Territory.

“Your Highness, in this battle, we captured three hundred thousand shi of grain and fodder from the Ning King’s army, nearly one million taels of gold and silver jewelry, countless armor and weapons, and nearly ten thousand prisoners.”

Su Wan’s voice was calm and clear as her slender fingers traced lightly over the map.

“After this battle, the Ning King has suffered a severe blow to his vitality. He will have no strength to move south for at least three years. This has bought us precious time for development.”

“Among the prisoners, we can select the strong to replenish our various battalions. The rest can be put to work on our next plan.”

Her finger pointed to a mountainous area east of Cangbei City.

“The iron ore here has astonishing reserves. It was previously monopolized by the Ma family, and the mining efficiency was low. Now, we can concentrate our manpower to mine on a large scale and establish our own weapon workshops.”

Her finger moved to a wilderness in the west.

“Here, we can emulate the previous dynasty and implement military colonies. Let the prisoners and some of the garrison troops be soldiers in wartime and farmers in peacetime. Within three years, Cangbei will be self-sufficient in grain and no longer at the mercy of others.”

Xiao Cheng listened quietly, his eyes shining with excitement.

These were exactly the things he had in mind!

Every word Su Wan spoke hit the precise nodes of his plan.

This intellectual resonance, this tacit understanding in planning the future together, gave him an unprecedented sense of satisfaction.

“And the trade routes,” Xiao Cheng added. “Our dealings with the Snow Eagle Tribe cannot stop at just warhorses and grain. Furs, medicinal herbs, and even their tribal battle tactics can become our commodities.”

“We can establish a massive commercial network centered on Cangbei, radiating throughout the entire Northern Territory and even beyond the pass. We will use economics to completely control this land!”

Su Wan’s eyes lit up.

“Your Highness is wise! In this way, we can support war with war and support our army with commerce, forming a virtuous cycle! By then, let alone a Ning King, the entire Northern Territory will be in your grasp!”

The two looked at each other and smiled; everything was understood without words.

Xiao Cheng looked at the magnificent blueprint on the sand table, which started from Cangbei and was constantly expanding outward, his heart filled with soaring ambition.

He turned his head and looked deeply at Su Wan, his voice carrying a trace of undisguised excitement and emotion.

"Su Wan, this world will eventually see our radiance."

"The era that belongs to us is about to begin."

"Us"…

He said these two words so naturally, so matter-of-factly.

And this scene, as it happened, fell into the eyes of someone at the doorway.

Shen Li had changed out of her military uniform and put on plain, everyday clothes.

She had just bathed, washing away the blood and fatigue from her body.

Returning in triumph, the grand gesture at the city gate had indeed warmed her heart.

The leading of her horse at the city gate and the cheers throughout the city had indeed shown signs of melting her frozen heart.

She had even thought that being a "blade" was not necessarily so cold.

At least, the one who wields the blade knows how to cherish it.

After finishing her military duties, she had come to the study, almost as if by instinct.

She thought she could talk to him about the follow-up handling of the remnants of Prince Ning’s forces and how to settle the wounded soldiers.

However, just as she reached the door, she saw the scene inside.

She saw him standing side by side with Su Wan, pointing out the landscape.

She saw the tacit understanding in their smiles at each other.

And she heard that incomparably clear sentence—"The era that belongs to us."

Us.

So, that was his "us."

One planning the strategy, one mapping out the world.

They were the architects of the blueprint, the pioneers of the future.

And what about her?

She was the blade outside that blueprint, responsible for clearing obstacles.

The warmth that had just risen at the city gate vanished in an instant, leaving nothing behind.

She understood.

The horse-leading during the day was for the soldiers and civilians of the entire city to see; it was to win over the hearts of the army, to pay a high price to buy the bones of a fine horse.

It was a monarch’s favor to a meritorious official.

Not a husband’s cherishing of his wife.

Shen Li stood in the shadows outside the door, motionless.

The light from the study illuminated the ground in front of her, while behind her was endless darkness.

A single step away, two different worlds.

She watched silently, looking at the two figures shining brightly under the lamplight, her eyes gradually dimming.

She did not go in.

Nor did she make a sound.

She simply turned around, quietly and resolutely.

With a straight back, she walked step by step back into that boundless darkness that belonged only to her.

chapters.title: Envoy from the Capital
chapters.content:
The cheers in Cangbei City lasted for three full days.

The news of Prince Ning’s defeat and the disintegration of his thirty-thousand-strong army spread quickly to every corner of the Northern Territory.

The title "God of War of the North" once again resounded through the heavens.

Shen Li.

These two words became the new totem of Cangbei.

However, as the creator of all this, Shen Li locked herself in the training grounds of the Prince’s mansion.

She did not participate in any of the celebratory banquets, nor did she pay any attention to the generals who came to pay their respects with fervent eyes.

Day after day, she used a piece of rough burlap to wipe her armor and long spear over and over again.

The moment Xiao Cheng led her horse when welcoming her outside the city, her frozen heart had indeed developed a crack.

Those eyes full of appreciation and pride had made her almost believe that everything she had done was worth it.

But that trace of warmth lasted less than half an hour.

When she saw Xiao Cheng and Su Wan standing side by side before the sand table in the study, planning the future with high spirits and discussing that magnificent blueprint, that crack was instantly frozen over again by endless ice.

"The era that belongs to us is about to begin."

Xiao Cheng’s voice seemed to still be echoing in her ears.

Our era.

The era of him and Su Wan.

Shen Li’s movement of wiping the spear tip paused slightly.

She suddenly understood.

She was not the one who created the era.

She was just a blade, clearing the thorns for that era.

A blade does not need to have warmth, let alone thoughts.

It only needs to be sharp; that is enough.

"General."

A personal guard walked quickly into the training ground and knelt on one knee.

"The Prince has ordered that you go to the council hall immediately; there is an urgent matter to discuss."

Shen Li slowly placed the silver spear back onto the weapon rack without looking back.

"What is it?"

"Reporting to the General, someone has arrived from the capital."

...

When Shen Li changed into her everyday clothes and walked into the council hall, the atmosphere inside was completely different from the celebrations of the previous days.

An invisible pressure hung over everyone’s heads.

Xiao Cheng sat in the main seat, his expression calm.

Su Wan stood by his side, her delicate brows slightly furrowed, as if she were pondering something.

Below, the core civil and military officials of Cangbei City were all present, each with a grave expression.

Seeing Shen Li enter, everyone bowed one after another.

"Princess."

Shen Li nodded slightly, walked straight to her place, and stood still, her gaze fixed on Xiao Cheng.

Xiao Cheng looked up, met her eyes, and spoke in a steady voice.

"Just half an hour ago, an urgent message arrived from the capital by eight-hundred-mile courier."

"His Majesty learned of the great victory in Cangbei and was greatly pleased. He has sent his trusted eunuch, Eunuch Li, to come and proclaim the imperial decree of reward."

"Calculating the time, he will arrive in Cangbei City by noon tomorrow."

Rewards?

In the council hall, a few newly promoted young generals showed a trace of joy on their faces.

Winning a battle and receiving rewards from the imperial court was a matter of course.

However, the experienced officials’ faces became increasingly ugly.

The new County Magistrate, an old official who had been squeezed out of the capital, stepped out tremblingly.

"Your Highness, forgive this old official for speaking bluntly. A reward at this time... I fear the visitor does not come with good intentions."

"Oh? How so?" Xiao Cheng asked calmly.

The Magistrate wiped the sweat from his forehead and continued: "Your Highness, think about it. The Shen family has just fallen, and in the eyes of the imperial court, your foundation in Cangbei is already like water without a source. Yet, at this very moment, we have crushed Prince Ning with thunderous force."

"In His Majesty’s eyes, this is not a merit, but rather... rather a grave offense!"

"A vassal king who has lost control but possesses such formidable combat power. This... this is the great taboo of an emperor!"

"This Eunuch Li who has been sent is the most favored eunuch before the throne, known for being ruthless. He comes in the name of rewarding, but in reality, I fear he is a pair of eyes and a sharp blade sent by His Majesty!"

These words made the atmosphere in the hall even colder.

Everyone understood.

This was a Hongmen Banquet.

Xiao Cheng nodded and turned his gaze to Su Wan.

"Su Wan, what do you think?"

Su Wan stepped forward, her voice cold and rational.

"The Magistrate is absolutely right. His Majesty’s intentions are nothing more than to test and divide."

"The test is to see whether you, Your Highness, will become arrogant and domineering after achieving such a great victory, or remain as submissive as before."

"The division is to plant a nail here in Cangbei City, to stir up hearts and minds, so that we cannot be twisted into a single rope."

She paused and continued to analyze: "Therefore, regarding tomorrow’s reward, the content of the imperial decree will likely have much hidden meaning. We must respond carefully."

Xiao Cheng nodded in approval and looked around at everyone.

"Did you all hear that? Tomorrow, everyone give me your utmost attention."

"No matter what is written on that imperial decree, no matter what that Eunuch Li says, there is only one thing you need to do."

His voice suddenly turned cold.

"And that is to obey my orders. If I tell you to smile, you smile. If I tell you to kneel, you kneel."

"Anyone who dares to cause even the slightest trouble for me in public, do not blame me for not remembering the bond between monarch and subject!"

"Understood!"

Everyone felt a chill in their hearts and replied in unison.

Xiao Cheng’s gaze finally fell on Shen Li.

He looked at her expressionless face, his lips moved, as if he wanted to say something.

In the end, he said nothing.

Shen Li also just looked at him calmly, her eyes holding neither questions nor expectations.

As if all of this had nothing to do with her.

The next day, at noon.

The south gate of Cangbei City was thrown wide open.

Xiao Cheng led all the civil and military officials of Cangbei to welcome them ten miles outside the city.

A long honor guard slowly appeared from the end of the horizon.

Leading them was a middle-aged eunuch dressed in a bright red python robe, with a fair face and no beard.

He rode a tall horse with an arrogant demeanor, followed by hundreds of imperial guards and a long line of carriages loaded with "rewards."

It was the imperial eunuch, Li Shun.

"Your subject, Xiao Cheng, leads the civil and military officials of Cangbei to respectfully welcome Eunuch Li!"

Xiao Cheng dismounted and bowed deeply to Li Shun.

The officials and generals behind him also knelt down in unison.

Li Shun sat on his horse and did not get down immediately.

He looked down at Xiao Cheng from his high position, then swept a glance at the dense crowd behind him, especially the generals clad in armor with fierce auras.

A trace of imperceptible malice flashed in his narrow eyes.

After a long while, he slowly got off his horse, put on a fake smile, and said in his unique, sharp, thin voice.

"Oh my, Seventh Prince, this won't do, this won't do! You are the ruler, and I am a servant; how can I let you perform such a great ceremony?"

Although he said it wouldn't do, his body steadily accepted the bow.

Xiao Cheng straightened up, a gentle and humble smile on his face.

"The Eunuch is an envoy sent by the Emperor, representing imperial grace; it is only right for Xiao Cheng to welcome you respectfully."

"Hahaha, the Prince is truly becoming more and more eloquent."

Li Shun patted Xiao Cheng’s shoulder with a fake smile, his gaze passing over him to land on Su Wan and Shen Li behind him.

His gaze lingered for only a moment on Shen Li’s plain clothes and cold face before immediately turning to the gentle-tempered Su Wan beside her.

"I presume this must be the 'heaven-sent talent' who made Prince Ning’s thirty-thousand-strong army vanish into thin air, Miss Su?"

Li Shun’s tone was filled with undisguised admiration and warmth.

Su Wan was startled and quickly lowered her head.

"The Eunuch is too kind with his praise; this humble woman does not deserve it."

"Oh, Miss Su, why be so modest? Your great name is now known to everyone in the capital—there isn't a soul who hasn't heard of you! His Majesty himself praised you in the Imperial Study, calling your talent capable of reshaping the world!"

Li Shun’s enthusiasm caused the surrounding military generals to furrow their brows.

Yet, he acted as if Shen Li, standing right beside them, did not exist; he did not even offer a single greeting.

Xiao Cheng seemed not to notice the awkwardness of the situation and continued to smile, trying to smooth things over.

"You have had a long journey, Eunuch. I have prepared some light refreshments; please, enter the city and rest."

"No rush, no rush."

Li Shun waved his hand and took a scroll of bright yellow imperial silk from the young eunuch behind him.

He cleared his throat, the smile on his face vanishing instantly, replaced by a solemn and grave expression.

"Seventh Prince Xiao Cheng, and all officials of Cangbei, receive the decree!"

"Clatter—"

Xiao Cheng took the lead again, and everyone knelt down in unison.

Only Shen Li, as the Princess Consort, was permitted to stand to receive the decree.

She stood there, solitary and alone.

Li Shun unfurled the imperial decree and began to read it, word by word, in his sharp, piercing voice.

"By the grace of Heaven, the Emperor decrees:"

"The Seventh Prince, Xiao Cheng, stationed in Cangbei, has pacified the people and expanded the borders with distinguished merit. Now, with the force of a thunderbolt, he has quelled the rebellion of Prince Ning, elevating the prestige of our nation. My heart is greatly comforted..."

The first half of the decree was filled with standard praise and rewards for Xiao Cheng.

Gold, silver, silk, and fertile land—the list was long and exhaustive, showing the utmost favor.

Everyone knew that the real point was yet to come.

Sure enough, Li Shun’s tone suddenly rose by an octave, filled with dramatic, rhythmic passion.

"...Most worthy of commendation is the Prince’s advisor, Su Wan!"

"Though born of humble origins, this woman possesses a brilliant mind, a talent capable of reshaping the world, and the aptitude of a king-maker! She is truly a virtuous talent bestowed upon our Imperial House by Heaven!"

"I have heard that the rise of Cangbei is primarily due to the efforts of Su Wan! It was her strategic planning and decisive command from behind the scenes that led to the magnificent prosperity of Cangbei today!"

"Therefore, I hereby confer upon Su Wan the title of 'Lady Wende,' with a fiefdom of three hundred households, one thousand taels of gold, and one hundred bolts of fine silk! It is my hope that she will continue to assist the Seventh Prince and share the burdens of the state!"

"Boom!"

These words struck everyone’s mind like a thunderclap!

A Lady of the County!

A daughter of a disgraced official with no family background whatsoever had been granted the title of a Lady of the County against all precedent!

What an honor! What immense favor!

Even more devastating was that the decree attributed the primary credit for the great victory in Cangbei entirely to Su Wan alone!

The military generals kneeling on the ground were all stunned.

Their bodies trembled slightly with rage.

They had fought through blood and fire, facing death at every turn, only for the credit of their victory to be handed to a woman who had stayed in the rear—a woman most of them had barely seen?

How absurd! What a humiliation!

Su Wan, kneeling on the ground, was so terrified that her face turned pale and her body went cold.

She knew this was a "killing by praise"!

They were putting her on a fire to roast!

She wanted to speak up and defend herself, but a stern look from Xiao Cheng, cast from beside her, stopped her dead in her tracks.

Li Shun watched the crowd’s reaction with satisfaction and smiled smugly.

He paused, as if just remembering something, and read the final paragraph of the decree in a flat, almost perfunctory tone.

"As for the Princess Consort, Lady Shen, for her bravery in the heat of battle and her valiant fighting, she has not disgraced the spirit of her military lineage, and I am also comforted. I hereby bestow upon her one phoenix-headed hairpin as a reward."

"This is the decree—"

Finishing the last two words, Li Shun slowly closed the scroll.

The whole world seemed to fall silent.

An eerie silence.

Valiant and brave, not disgracing the spirit of her military lineage.

One phoenix-headed hairpin.
