This was the entirety of the evaluation and reward for the "God of War of the North," who had led three thousand heavy cavalry to pierce through an army of thirty thousand and personally severed the commander’s flag of Prince Ning.

It was light and airy, as if he were dismissing a servant who had performed a minor chore.

Everyone’s gaze subconsciously converged on the solitary silver figure standing alone.

They wanted to see her anger, her resentment, her outburst.

However, there was none.

There was no expression on Shen Li’s face.

She just stood there quietly, as if the person mentioned in the imperial decree was not her at all.

Her gaze did not even fall on Li Shun, nor did it look at Xiao Cheng.

She was simply looking into the distance, at the vast, desolate sky that belonged to Cangbei.

It was as if all the honor and disgrace in this world had nothing to do with her.

The more she acted this way, the more suffocating the invisible pressure became.

"Your subject, Xiao Cheng, thanks the Emperor for his boundless grace!"

Xiao Cheng’s voice broke the silence.

He kowtowed respectfully, then held his hands high, preparing to receive the decree.

"Your Highness, please rise."

Li Shun smiled, personally helping Xiao Cheng up, and as he handed him the decree, he said with a pointed tone:

"Your Highness, you are truly blessed. With a brilliant woman like Lady Wende to assist you, why worry about failing in your great cause? His Majesty is quite envious!"

Xiao Cheng smiled, his expression flawless.

"It is all due to my Imperial Father’s boundless fortune."

He turned to Su Wan, who was still kneeling on the ground, and said gently:

"Lady Wende, why are you still dazed? Get up and thank the Emperor."

Su Wan’s body trembled. She looked up at Xiao Cheng with a deathly pale face.

In his eyes, she saw a bottomless, calm stillness.

She understood—this was an order.

She could only grit her teeth, kowtow, and offer her thanks.

"The... subject, Su Wan, thanks the Emperor for his boundless grace."

As she stood up, she felt countless cold, angry, and disdainful gazes piercing into her.

She knew that from this moment on, she had been pushed to the opposite side of all the soldiers of Cangbei.

Li Shun watched this scene, smiling even more happily.

He had achieved the effect he wanted.

In this atmosphere of eerie harmony, Shen Li moved.

She did not greet anyone.

She simply turned around in silence.

Then, she took a step and began walking back toward the city gate, step by step.

Her silhouette remained proud and solitary.

The silver fabric of her clothes fluttered in the wind like a silent flag.

Just like that, under the gaze of everyone, she left this "reward" ceremony—filled with calculation and humiliation—far behind her.

chapters.title: A Family Banquet and Leftovers
chapters.content:
She did not look back.

Behind her were Li Shun’s sharp, grating laughter, Xiao Cheng’s gentle and slick responses, Su Wan’s fearful and uneasy expressions of gratitude, and the heavy, suppressed breathing of the military generals holding back their rage.

None of this had anything to do with her anymore.

She walked, step by step, back into that majestic city.

The people on both sides of the street had not yet recovered from the dramatic scene they had just witnessed.

They had seen the Prince holding the horse for the Princess Consort, and they had heard the shocking rewards for Su Wan in the imperial decree, as well as the dismissive humiliation of the Princess Consort.

They were confused; they were bewildered.

They watched the silver figure walking back alone, their eyes complex.

There was sympathy, awe, and a hint of alienation.

Shen Li felt these gazes, but her pace did not falter in the slightest.

She did not need sympathy, and she cared even less for alienation.

She was a blade; a blade only needs to be used, not understood.

That evening, the Prince’s mansion was brightly lit, with the sound of music filling the air.

To welcome the imperial inspector from the capital, Xiao Cheng had set up a grand family banquet.

Inside the banquet hall, it was warm and cozy, with incense curling in the air.

Yet, this warmth was divided by an invisible wall into two completely different worlds.

At the head of the hall was a large round table.

Xiao Cheng sat in the center, with the smiling inspector Li Shun on his left.

And on his right, unexpectedly, sat Su Wan, who had just been titled "Lady Wende."

Su Wan had changed into a gorgeous palace gown, one of the gifts that came with the imperial decree. Woven from cloud brocade and adorned with pearls and jade, it made her look even more refined and ethereal.

But on her face was a hint of undisguised awkwardness and unease.

Several times she wanted to get up and return to her seat as an advisor, but each time, Xiao Cheng pressed her back down with a gentle, unquestionable look.

The three of them, along with several civil officials of Cangbei, chatted and laughed, the atmosphere lively.

On the other side of the hall, near the entrance, several long, rectangular tables were set up.

Shen Li sat at the very head of these.

Beside her were the commanders of the Black Armor Cavalry, the leaders of the scout battalion, and all the core generals who had fought and bled on the battlefield just yesterday.

They had not changed out of their military uniforms, only removed their heavy armor.

Their aura of slaughter was completely out of place with the decadent music filling the room.

In front of them, the tables were also laden with delicacies and fine wine.

No one touched their chopsticks.

They simply sat in silence, downing strong liquor, cup after cup.

Every time Li Shun’s sharp laughter drifted over from the main table, their hands gripping their wine cups would tighten.

The fire of rage burned in the chest of every military general.

They were the heroes who had earned the victory.

Yet, at this victory banquet, they were like guests waiting to be fed, isolated from the true inner circle.

Their General—the God of War who had led them to create miracles—was left on the sidelines, as if she were an irrelevant outsider.

Was this a family banquet?

It was clearly a banquet of leftovers.

It was the General’s leftovers, the leftovers of all the soldiers who had bled for this victory.

Shen Li did not drink.

She simply held a cup of clear tea, watching the scene at the main table with calm eyes.

She watched how Xiao Cheng skillfully steered the conversation, making Li Shun praise Su Wan’s "wisdom" endlessly.

"Eunuch Li, you may not know, but for this great victory, Lady Wende deserves the greatest credit. Whatever I could think of, she had already thought of. Whatever I couldn't think of, she would fill in for me."

Xiao Cheng’s voice was filled with admiration.

"When Prince Ning’s army pressed upon our borders and the people in the city were in a panic, it was Lady Wende who offered the strategy of 'strengthening the walls and clearing the fields to wait for the right moment,' which stabilized the situation."

"The grain and supplies captured after the battle were also allocated by Lady Wende, who worked through the night to draft a plan. By opening mines and encouraging farming, Cangbei will be completely transformed within three months."

Li Shun nodded repeatedly, his eyes growing even more fervent as he looked at Su Wan.

"Oh my, I heard back in the palace that Lady Su possessed talent capable of governing the world. Seeing you today, I realize the rumors were true! Your Highness, you have truly struck gold!"

Su Wan’s face turned from red to white.

She opened her mouth, wanting to defend herself.

"Eunuch, you flatter me. These... these are all due to His Highness’s far-sightedness; I merely..."

"Oh, Lady Su, there is no need for such modesty!"

Xiao Cheng interrupted her with a smile and handed her a cup of wine.

"Your contributions, I see them, and His Majesty sees them as well. This cup of wine, I offer to you."

Su Wan looked at the cup, then at Xiao Cheng’s deep, unfathomable eyes. In the end, she could only take it with trembling hands and drain it in one gulp.

*Clang!*

At the table of military officers, a hot-tempered general finally lost his patience and slammed his bronze wine goblet heavily onto the table.

The massive sound caused the boisterous banquet hall to fall silent instantly.

All eyes turned toward them.

The general’s eyes were bloodshot, his breathing heavy, as he stared fixedly at the main table.

"Your Highness!"

His companion beside him quickly grabbed him, whispering harshly, "Sit down! What do you think you’re doing?"

Xiao Cheng’s gaze swept over them indifferently.

In that gaze, there was no reprimand, nor was there any comfort—only a cold, icy calm.

He did not even speak.

Yet, the general felt as if a basin of ice water had been poured over his head; all his rage was extinguished in an instant.

He slumped back into his seat, grabbed a wine flagon, and began to guzzle it down.

Li Shun watched this scene and smiled coldly.

This was exactly the effect he wanted.

He picked up his wine cup, stood up slowly, and let his gaze sweep across the faces of Shen Li and the group of military officers one by one, finally settling back on Xiao Cheng.

"Your Highness, let me speak from the heart."

He wiped the corner of his mouth with a handkerchief and continued in a measured tone.

"Governing the world and fighting on the battlefield are not the same thing. Fighting relies on the brute courage of common men, charging forward without hesitation. But governing the world relies on the mind, on strategy."

His voice was not loud, yet it carried clearly throughout the entire hall.

"With a brilliant and virtuous woman like Lady Su by your side to offer counsel and manage internal affairs, it is no wonder that Your Highness has been able to bring order to the barren Cangbei in such a short time, turning decay into something miraculous."

He paused, shifted his tone, and looked at Shen Li with a hint of vague pity.

"As for the Princess Consort..."

He deliberately drew out his tone, a look of regret appearing on his face.

"Being able to fight is a good thing. After all, she is the daughter of a military family, and it does not tarnish the prestige of the Duke of Zhen’s estate."

"However... a woman, in the end, must still treat her husband as her heaven; managing the household and raising children is the proper path. Playing with swords and guns is, after all... not something that belongs in polite society."

This sentence was like a resounding slap, struck hard across the faces of all the military officers.

It was even more like a poisoned dagger, precisely piercing Shen Li’s heart.

The entire hall was deathly silent.

The fists of all the military officers were clenched so tightly they creaked.

Their eyes seemed ready to spit fire.

They looked in unison at Xiao Cheng, waiting for their King to speak a word of justice for their General.

However, Xiao Cheng merely held his wine cup, a perfectly measured, gentle smile on his face.

As if what Li Shun had said were pearls of wisdom.

He did not utter a word.

No rebuttal, no defense, not even a hint of displeasure.

His silence was his acquiescence.

His smile was his tacit approval.

In that instant, Shen Li felt the teacup in her hand become searingly hot.

She slowly raised her eyes.

Her gaze crossed the long distance, past the flickering candlelight, and landed on Xiao Cheng’s face.

She looked at him.

She looked at that handsome face, the one that had once made her heart flutter for a moment.

She looked at that smile on his lips, a smile carefully calculated for the sake of the big picture, for the sake of his grand ambitions.

She suddenly felt it was somewhat laughable.

So, this was the art of imperial governance.

To appease the hound sent by the Emperor, he could, without hesitation, trample his own wife and the dignity of the soldiers who had bled for him underfoot.

It was not that he didn't know this was an insult.

He simply felt that this insult was worth it.

The knuckles of the hand Shen Li used to hold the teacup turned white from the force.

She felt no anger, no sorrow.

Her heart, at this moment, turned completely cold.

Cold as a block of eternal, unmeltable black ice.

She slowly drained the tea in her cup in one gulp.

Then, she stood up.

*Swish—*

As she rose, all the military officers behind her stood up in unison, as if by reflex.

They were like a pack of silent wolves, guarding their wolf king.

The music in the banquet hall had stopped at some point.

Everyone’s gaze was focused on Shen Li.

A flash of vigilance crossed Li Shun’s eyes.

Su Wan’s face was filled with worry.

On Xiao Cheng’s face, that smile finally stiffened.

Shen Li did not look at anyone.

She merely gave a slight nod toward the main seat, toward the man who, in name, was still her husband.

It was not a bow of respect.

It was merely a cold, emotionless notification.

Then, she turned.

She took a step and walked toward the outside of the hall.

Her pace was steady and firm.

Her silver hem swept across the cold floor without making a sound.

"General!"

The commander of the Black Armor Cavalry let out a low growl and, without a second thought, immediately followed her.

One, two, three...

All the military officers sitting in that row, without the slightest hesitation, followed silently behind Shen Li.

They formed a silent torrent, following their General, resolutely exiting this banquet that did not belong to them.

In the blink of an eye, the once lively banquet hall was more than half empty.

Only the civil officials at the main table, looking at each other in dismay, and the triumphant-looking Li Shun remained.

Xiao Cheng stood there, holding his wine cup, motionless.

He watched that silver silhouette disappear into the night outside the door, watching those fierce generals who should have belonged to him follow her away without a hint of reluctance.

A storm surged in his eyes.

In the end, it only turned into a barely audible sigh.

Li Shun clapped his hands and laughed.

"Hahaha, Your Highness, look, I told you. These military men are just a bunch of unrefined brutes who don't know their place; they are wild and hard to tame!"

"But it doesn't matter. With Lady Su here, Your Highness's grand cause is secure!"

Xiao Cheng slowly set down his wine cup, the smile on his face becoming gentle once more.

"The Eunuch is right."

He lifted the wine flagon and personally filled Li Shun’s cup.

"Come, let us continue to drink."

Yet, no one saw the murderous intent that flashed in the depths of his eyes the moment he lowered his gaze.

chapters.title: Xiao and Su's Blueprint
chapters.content:
The music and laughter inside the banquet hall were cut off by the heavy doors.

Shen Li led her generals into the cold night of the Prince’s estate.

No one spoke.

But the oppressive silence carried more weight than any angry roar.

They did not disperse, but instead, as if by mutual agreement, followed Shen Li’s footsteps to the training grounds.

This was their place.

The cold weapon racks, the rough sandy ground, the air permeated with the scent of sweat and rust.

"General!"

The general who had smashed his wine goblet at the banquet had bloodshot eyes, his voice filled with irrepressible humiliation and rage.

"His Highness... how could he do this! We follow you and risk our lives out there, and this is what we get in return?"

"That eunuch with the surname Li, what kind of thing is he! How dare he insult you!"

"And that Su Wan! A woman who only knows how to talk on paper, why is the greatest merit hers! Why is she allowed to be a Lady!"

The questions echoed in the silent night.

This was the sentiment of them all.

They did not fear death; what they feared was dying without dignity, fearing that their blood had been shed in vain.

Shen Li did not turn back; she simply walked to the weapon rack and took down her silver spear.

She slowly stroked the cold shaft of the spear with her palm, feeling that familiar, reassuring texture.

"His Highness has his own considerations."

Her voice calmed all the noise behind her.

"That eunuch is the Emperor’s eyes. What His Highness did today was for the Emperor to see."

"The more Cangbei appears to have discord between sovereign and subject, and contempt between civil and military officials, the more at ease the Emperor will be."

The generals were stunned.

They were soldiers, accustomed to being direct; how could they understand such convoluted political schemes?

"But... but this is still too stifling!" someone said, unwilling to let it go.

Shen Li turned around, her gaze sweeping across each of their faces.

"Stifling?"

She gave a mocking smile.

"On the battlefield, when the enemy’s blade cuts into you, is it not stifling?"

"When your comrade-in-arms dies in your arms, is it not stifling?"

"We are soldiers. A soldier’s duty is to protect the home and defend the country, to win the war. It is not to haggle over merit, and certainly not to care about those empty titles."

Her words were like a basin of cold water, extinguishing the internal fire in everyone’s hearts.

Yes, they were soldiers.

Since when did they start caring about these empty titles of the imperial court?

Watching them gradually calm down, Shen Li’s expression did not soften.

She knew that Xiao Cheng’s approach, from the perspective of a Prince, might be correct.

Endurance, showing weakness, paralyzing the enemy.

But her heart still felt blocked.

That frustration was not because she had been insulted, but stemmed from a deeper sense of unease.

She felt that the invisible chasm between her and Xiao Cheng was growing wider and wider.

She thought of the defenses of the Northern Frontier.

Although Prince Ning had been defeated, the true threat to the Northern Frontier had never been these infighting vassal kings.

It was the barbarian tribes on the grasslands, watching like tigers eyeing their prey.

In particular, the newly risen Golden Wolf Tribe—their iron cavalry is a hundred times more ferocious than King Ning’s army.

They must prepare early.

She placed her silver spear back onto the weapon rack and issued orders to those present.

"Pass the word down: all battalions are to heighten their guard. The scout battalion is to push their reconnaissance range one hundred miles to the north, with a primary focus on monitoring the movements of the Golden Wolf Tribe."

"Starting tomorrow, the entire army will resume training, with the intensity doubled."

"Yes!"

The officers responded in unison, their voices ringing out with strength and resolve.

The frustration in their hearts seemed, in this moment, to have transformed into the motivation to prepare for war.

After arranging the military affairs, Shen Li left the training grounds alone.

She did not return to her own courtyard; instead, as if guided by some unseen force, she walked toward the study.

She thought she should go and speak with Xiao Cheng.

Not about what happened at the banquet, but about the military defense of the Northern Frontier.

This was her duty.

The night was deep and quiet, and the corridors of the Prince’s mansion were empty.

The cold, pale moonlight stretched her shadow long across the ground.

Before she even reached the door of the study, she heard the faint sound of voices coming from within.

It was Xiao Cheng and Su Wan.

Her footsteps stopped instinctively, and her body retreated into the shadows of a nearby pillar.

"Your Highness, today’s events... it was I who made things difficult for you and the General."

It was Su Wan’s voice, thick with self-reproach and anxiety.

"I am unworthy of the title of County Princess. Tomorrow, I will submit a petition to resign and return the credit to the General and the soldiers."

"Foolish!"

Xiao Cheng’s voice rang out, carrying a trace of unquestionable authority.

"The Emperor’s imperial decree is a golden promise; how can you simply resign from it just because you want to?"

"If you resign now, you are explicitly telling the Emperor that we in Cangbei are of one mind and united as a single block. Do you want the Emperor to move against us immediately?"

"I..." Su Wan was at a loss for words.

"I know you feel wronged, and I know the soldiers are resentful," Xiao Cheng’s voice softened, carrying a hint of consolation.

"But you must remember: to achieve great things, there must be sacrifices. Temporary grievances are the price for long-term goals. We must keep this thorn, Li Shun, satisfied; we must let him see what he wants to see."

"As for those military officers... they are just a group of rough men who only know how to fight and kill; it is enough to appease them. They are incapable of achieving anything grand."

Outside the door, Shen Li’s heart constricted violently upon hearing these words.

So, in Xiao Cheng’s heart, the comrades who had bled and fought alongside her were merely a group of "rough men."

How laughable that she had still wanted to fight for them.

Inside the study, after a brief silence, Su Wan’s voice sounded, laced with tears.

"But Your Highness, I am afraid... I am afraid I cannot do it well. I have been pushed to the forefront, becoming a thorn in the side of all the military officers, I..."

"With me here, what are you afraid of?"

Xiao Cheng interrupted her, his voice filled with unprecedented firmness and trust.

"Su Wan, you are different from the others. What they see is the immediate military merit, the gain or loss of a city. But you, like me, see the future ten or twenty years from now!"

His voice rose slightly with excitement.

"Have you forgotten our previous plans? The iron ore mining cannot just be for weapons; we must smelt refined steel and sell it to the wealthy merchants within the Pass to trade for a constant stream of gold!"

"As for the grain from the military colonies, apart from self-sufficiency, the surplus must be used to open distilleries. Our strong liquor will become the hardest currency in the entire Northern Frontier!"

"And the trade routes! The Snow Eagle Tribe is only the beginning; I want to open a golden trade route connecting to the Western Regions! Silk, porcelain, tea... all of these can be turned into our warhorses and armor!"

"We will also build schools. We won't just teach the Four Books and Five Classics; we will teach mathematics, natural sciences, and water conservancy! I want every child in Cangbei to know our philosophy and become the cornerstone of our future!"

Xiao Cheng’s voice was filled with longing and fanaticism for the future.

He grabbed Su Wan’s hand and said excitedly, "Su Wan, only you understand me! What I want to build is not a regional fiefdom tucked away in a corner, but an entirely new dynasty!"

*Boom!*

This last sentence struck Shen Li’s mind like a thunderbolt from the heavens.

An entirely... new dynasty.

She stood in the shadows outside the door, her whole body ice-cold.

The light from the study illuminated the ground in front of her, while behind her lay endless darkness.

One step away, two different worlds.

She finally understood.

She had thought she was guarding this man’s fiefdom and protecting the homes of the people of Cangbei.

In the end, all she was guarding was one man’s ambition to overthrow the current dynasty.

She listened to the sovereign and his subject inside, excitedly planning their grand blueprint.

Trade routes, mines, schools, economy, people's livelihoods...

What a magnificent future that was.

It was just that, in that blueprint, from beginning to end, there was no place for her—this "blade."

No, perhaps there was.

Her place was outside the blueprint.

When enemies wanted to destroy this blueprint, she was to be unsheathed to clear the obstacles.

Once the clearing was done, she was to return quietly to the scabbard and wait to be used again.

The entire meaning of her existence was to ensure the smooth construction of this blueprint.

Nothing more.

The heart that had just been burning hot with strong liquor and rage turned completely cold and silent in this moment.

She remembered the military defense regarding the Golden Wolf Tribe that she had come to discuss.

Now, it seemed so laughable.

That, too, was just a part of the blueprint—a link they had already planned out that required her to execute.

She did not linger any longer.

She did not make a sound.

She simply turned around, quietly and decisively.

Her straight back walked, step by step, back into that boundless darkness that belonged to her.

The moonlight spilled onto her silver armor, casting a cold, pale light.

Her shadow was stretched thin and long, appearing incomparably lonely.

chapters.title: The Golden Wolf Attacks
chapters.content:
Since turning away from outside the study that night, Shen Li never set foot in the back courtyard of the Prince’s mansion again.

She moved back to the military camp.

That camp, located west of Cangbei City, dusty all year round and filled only with the sounds of bugles and slaughter, was her true home.

She did not see Xiao Cheng again, nor did she see Su Wan.

That family banquet, that conversation, and that door had completely isolated her from them.

She poured all her time into training.

On the training grounds, she was more frantic than any soldier. The long spear in her hands was no longer a tool for practice, but a lethal weapon for life-and-death struggle. Every move, every stance, carried a sense of desperate ruthlessness.

The soldiers saw it in their eyes and felt it in their hearts.

They did not know what had happened between the General and the Prince, but they could feel the increasingly heavy, cold loneliness emanating from the General.

It was not sorrow, but a silence that follows a dead heart.

This silence was completely shattered three days later, at dawn, by the sound of urgent bugles.

"Woo—woo—woo—"

The desolate bugles, carrying a bloody warning, were passed along from the beacon towers in the north.

The entire Cangbei camp was instantly jolted awake from its slumber.

Countless soldiers rushed out of their tents, quickly donning their armor and searching for their units.

Shen Li, in her silver armor, was already standing on the command platform.

A scout, covered in blood, crawled and scrambled up to the platform, his voice hoarse and urgent.

"General! The Golden Wolf Tribe... fifty thousand of their iron cavalry have crossed the Black Water River and are charging at full speed toward the heart of Cangbei!"

*Boom!*

As the news spread, the expressions of the officers below the platform changed drastically.

The Golden Wolf Tribe!

They were the true overlords of the Northern Frontier grasslands!

Their ferocity and cruelty were far beyond that of internal warring factions like King Ning.

Half an hour later, in the Prince’s mansion council hall.

The atmosphere was so heavy it felt as if it could drip water.

Xiao Cheng sat in the main seat, his face gloomy.

Beside him stood Su Wan, who was equally pale.

Below, civil and military officials were lined up on both sides.

Shen Li and her officers stood at the head of the military officials. The armor she wore still carried the chill of the early morning, looking completely out of place in the warm council hall.

The military supervisor, Li Shun, was also present, which was unprecedented. He sat in a guest seat to the side, holding a teacup, wearing the expression of someone watching a show.

"Everyone, the military situation is urgent; I assume you are all aware."

Xiao Cheng’s voice broke the silence.

"The Golden Wolf Tribe has mobilized their entire force; fifty thousand iron cavalry are coming with fierce intent. This battle concerns the life and death of our Cangbei. Su Wan, tell everyone your plan."

"Yes."

Su Wan stepped forward, forcing herself to remain calm.

She walked to the massive sand table, where the topography of Cangbei was laid out in full view.

"Your Highness, my lords, General."

Her voice was clear and rational, carrying a sense of theoretical confidence.

"According to intelligence, the Golden Wolf Tribe’s southern invasion this time aims to retaliate against our alliance with the Snow Eagle Tribe and intends to destroy our foundation. Although their force is numerous, their logistics line is long, which is their fatal weakness."

"Therefore, the strategy I have formulated is: strengthen the walls and clear the fields, lure the enemy deep, cut off their supplies, and achieve victory in a single battle."

She picked up a long, thin bamboo rod and pointed it at the sand table.

"First, we will immediately issue an order: all villages and towns in the red-marked areas on the sand table must organize the people at once, take all grain and livestock, and retreat into the nearby garrisons and cities. If they cannot, burn everything in place; do not leave the enemy a single grain of rice or a blade of grass."

"Secondly, we will abandon all unnecessary outposts on the periphery and consolidate our forces, concentrating them in the three fortified cities of Black Stone, Iron Gate, and Cangbei, forming a mutually supporting formation. Relying on these strongholds, we will continuously send out small groups of elite cavalry to harass the enemy, exhausting them."

"The Golden Wolf iron cavalry is good at attacking but not at defending, and even worse at sieges. As long as we hold our ground and do not come out, in a month at the shortest, or two at the longest, they will not be able to seize supplies, and their morale will inevitably decline. At that time, we will wait for them to tire, then send out our three armies, coordinate with the Black Armor cavalry to flank them, and cut off their retreat. This battle can be decided in one stroke!"

Su Wan’s plan was clear, logical, and rigorous.

From a strategic perspective, this is a nearly perfect defensive counter-attack plan. It maximizes Cangbei’s defensive advantages, avoids the risks of open-field combat with the grassland cavalry, and minimizes casualties.

Several civil officials nodded repeatedly after hearing this, their faces showing approval.

"Lady Su’s plan is extremely sound! These are the words of a seasoned strategist!"

"Indeed, with our current strength, going head-to-head with fifty thousand grassland barbarians is unwise. Wearing them down is the superior strategy!"

Xiao Cheng listened to the discussion, a look of satisfaction appearing on his face.

He looked at Shen Li, seemingly waiting for her agreement.

"Princess, what do you think?"

Shen Li’s gaze had been fixed on the sand table from the very beginning.

She looked at the areas marked in red by Su Wan, the regions about to be "cleared."

There, hundreds of villages existed, home to tens of thousands of Cangbei’s people.

She finally spoke, her voice cold and devoid of emotion.

"I object."

With those two words, the council chamber fell silent.

Everyone’s eyes were focused on her.

Su Wan’s face turned even paler.

Xiao Cheng’s brow furrowed.

"Reason," he said coldly.

"This plan is nothing but armchair strategy and wishful thinking."

Shen Li did not mince words, dismissing Su Wan’s perfect plan as worthless in a single sentence.

She stepped forward, picked up a bamboo rod, and pointed heavily at the sand table.

"First, you have underestimated the mobility of the Golden Wolf tribe. Fifty thousand iron cavalry are not infantry. They can travel a hundred miles a day, spreading out in a fan shape like a plague of locusts. How long will it take for your so-called 'scorched earth' orders to reach the villages? How fast can the commoners travel while dragging their families along? Before they can even evacuate, the Golden Wolf scimitars will already be at their throats."

"Second, you have overestimated our execution and underestimated the fundamental nature of humanity. Asking the people to abandon homes they have cultivated for generations and burn their own houses and grain? They will not agree. Even if we force it, how is that any different from the slaughter of the Golden Wolf? Public morale will collapse before the enemy even arrives."

"Third, and most fatal of all."

Shen Li’s gaze swept over Su Wan like a blade before finally landing on Xiao Cheng’s face.

"You have treated the Golden Wolf tribe as if they were an army like Prince Ning’s. They do not need long supply lines because wherever they go, the land itself is their granary! They will slaughter villages, seize everything they can, kill our men, and abduct our women and children! Luring them into our heartland is not 'luring the enemy deep'—it is inviting the wolf into the house!"

"Your perfect plan uses the bones of tens of thousands of innocent people and the scorched earth of a thousand miles of Cangbei to trade for a theoretical victory. I do not agree to this cost."

Her words were piercing.

Each word struck Su Wan’s heart like a heavy hammer.

Su Wan swayed, her body trembling. She bit her lip and defended herself: "War inevitably involves sacrifice. For the sake of final victory, local losses are..."

"Sacrifice?"

Shen Li interrupted her, her tone carrying undisguised mockery.

"Easy to say. Because the ones being sacrificed are not you, sitting in the Prince’s mansion, pointing at the sand table and dictating the fate of the nation."

"You!" Su Wan was so angry her face turned red, tears welling in her eyes.

"Enough!"

Xiao Cheng slammed the table and stood up.

His face was filled with rage.

"Shen Li! This is a military council, not a place for you to vent personal grievances!"

He walked over to Su Wan, shielding her behind him, and glared at Shen Li.

"Then what is your brilliant suggestion?"

"Fight."

Shen Li said only one word.

"Block the enemy outside the borders of Cangbei. Let them die where they came from."

"Absurd!" a civil official immediately objected. "The enemy is many and we are few; a proactive attack is no different from throwing an egg against a rock!"

"Exactly, General Shen, the courage of a brute is not to be encouraged!"

Shen Li ignored them, looking only at Xiao Cheng.

"I will personally lead the Black Armor Cavalry to meet the main force of the Golden Wolf head-on. The other units will flank from both sides to divide the battlefield. Although our numbers are small, we have the advantage of terrain and the determination to defend our homes. We are not without a chance."

Her plan was simple, direct, and filled with bloody madness.

But the generals behind her felt a burning desire for battle ignite in their eyes.

This was the style of warfare they were familiar with—the style of a true general!

Xiao Cheng looked at Shen Li, at her eyes burning with fire, and a sense of inexplicable irritation rose within him.

He admitted that Shen Li’s analysis had merit.

But he could not accept it.

Adopting Shen Li’s plan would be equivalent to negating Su Wan.

In front of the imperial supervisor sent by the Emperor, negating the "chief strategist" he had personally promoted was akin to slapping his own face.

More importantly, he could not allow Shen Li and the military achievements of her subordinates to continue to grow.

A general whose achievements overshadow the master and who refuses to follow orders is more terrifying than any foreign enemy.

His gaze gradually turned cold.

"This Prince believes Lady Su’s plan is more prudent."

He spoke word by word, his voice not loud, but carrying unquestionable resolve.

"In this battle, Lady Su will have full authority over strategic planning. All soldiers must execute it unconditionally."

He looked at Shen Li, his eyes sharp as knives.

"This is an order. You must trust the commander-in-chief and execute the plan in its entirety. Anyone who dares to feign compliance or shake the morale of the army will be executed without mercy!"

"The Prince is wise!"

The civil officials echoed in unison.

Li Shun, standing to the side, clapped and laughed, his eyes full of admiration.

On the side of the military generals, there was silence.

Everyone’s face was filled with disappointment and resentment.

Shen Li looked at Xiao Cheng, at the cold, resolute look in his eyes.

She suddenly understood.

It wasn't that he didn't know her plan was more effective.

It was simply that he no longer needed a blade so sharp that it might cut him.

The last remaining warmth in her heart was completely extinguished.

She did not argue further.

She did not say another word.

She simply bowed to Xiao Cheng, slowly and formally.

"This subordinate obeys."

After saying this, she turned around and, with the silent generals behind her, strode out of the council chamber.

As she stepped out the door and was bathed in the sunlight, she knew that some things had changed forever.

The horn of war had sounded.

The defense of Cangbei began to contract according to Su Wan’s plan.

Order after order was issued from the Prince’s mansion, spreading across the vast northern territory.

However, only one day later.

The first battle report arrived like a loud slap across everyone’s faces.

The Golden Wolf cavalry had ignored the fortified cities entirely.

They bypassed all defensive strongpoints, transforming into dozens of black torrents that surged into the heartland of Cangbei, which had not yet been "cleared."

Countless villages were reduced to ashes in the flames of war.

Smoke signals of distress rose from all directions.

chapters.title: The Collapse of the Defense Line
chapters.content:
The course of the war, just as in Shen Li’s coldest prophecy, took a sharp turn for the worse.

Su Wan’s plan, which had looked seamless on the sand table, was torn to shreds under the iron hooves of the Golden Wolf tribe.

One distress signal after another rose from the vast land of Cangbei, staining the sky a desperate, ash-gray black.

The villages marked for "scorched earth" had no time to evacuate.

The Prince’s mansion’s orders were still on the way, but the Golden Wolf scimitars had already drunk their fill of blood.

The Golden Wolf cavalry broke into small units, bypassing all fortified cities and garrisons. They had no interest in sieges; their targets were clearly the wealthy and defenseless villages.

Plundering, burning, slaughtering.

The entire heartland of Cangbei became their granary and pasture.

In the council chamber of the Prince’s mansion, the atmosphere was suffocating.

Su Wan stood before the massive sand table, her face deathly pale.

The sand table that once represented her wisdom and strategy had now become a massive piece of evidence against her.

It was covered in small black flags representing "villages destroyed," dense and shocking to behold.

She kept moving the pieces representing their own troops on the sand table with a bamboo rod, trying to build a new defensive line to plug the gaps.

But no matter how she moved them, it was to no avail.

The defense line was full of holes; it could not stop the enemy at all.

"How could this be... how could this be..." she muttered to herself, her body trembling uncontrollably. "Their speed is too fast, they aren't following any logic..."

Xiao Cheng sat in the main seat, his face so gloomy it seemed it could drip water.

Battle reports stained with blood, sent back from the front lines, were slammed onto the floor by him.

"Report! Your Highness! Heilin Village has fallen, not a single one of the three hundred households survived!"

"Report! Your Highness! Zhang Family Fort has been breached, the granary burned, the entire garrison wiped out!"

"Report! Your Highness! A unit of the Golden Wolf has bypassed Iron Gate Pass and is heading toward Xiliangchuan in our heartland!"

Every piece of news struck him hard.

The prestige he had built, his trust in Su Wan, and the prudent victory he had envisioned had all become a joke in the face of the bloody reality.

"Useless! All of you are useless!"

He suddenly swept the teacup off the table, and it shattered with a crisp sound.

Rage burned in his chest, not just because of the failure on the battlefield, but because of a panic born of losing control.

He discovered that the orders he issued were met with no response.

Nine out of ten messengers sent out never returned, intercepted and killed on the road by roaming enemy cavalry.

For the first time, he, the Prince sitting at the center of power, had lost control of the war.

The supervisor, Li Shun, standing to the side, sipped his tea slowly and spoke in a sarcastic, mocking tone.

"Oh my, Your Highness, you must calm your anger. This servant thinks Lady Su’s strategy was good; it’s just that those barbarians are illiterate, haven't read the art of war, and don't know how to cooperate."

His words were filled with gloating mockery.

Xiao Cheng turned his head sharply, staring at him with fierce eyes.

The murderous intent in that gaze made even Li Shun shrink his neck and shut his mouth in embarrassment.

Unlike the chaos and rage in the Prince’s mansion, the front-line commander’s tent where Shen Li was stationed was filled with a profound stillness.

Shen Li, clad in silver armor, stood before a crude military map.

On the map, the intertwined positions of the enemy and their own forces were outlined in cinnabar and ink.

The generals behind her all bore armor stained with blood and dust, their faces etched with anxiety and fury.

"General! We cannot wait any longer!"

Wang Zheng, commander of the Black Armor Cavalry—the man who had once smashed a wine goblet in rage at a banquet—clenched his fists until his knuckles cracked.

"If we continue to follow the Prince’s orders, the brothers won't die on the battlefield; they’ll be suffocated to death in this defensive line!"

"Indeed, General! We watch as those villages are burned and the people are slaughtered, yet we are forced to sit idle here. What kind of soldiers are we?"

"General, give the order! Let us fight them to the death!"

The crowd was seething with indignation.

Shen Li did not turn back; her gaze never left the map.

She knew that Xiao Cheng’s orders had been wrong from the very beginning.

Yet, she had to execute them.

Because to disobey was to commit mutiny, to shake the morale of the army, and to provide Li Shun and the Emperor with the perfect pretext.

She could disregard her own reputation, but she could not gamble with the foundation of the entire Cangbei region.

However, when reality had already proven the orders wrong, and when the consequence of executing them was destruction, then blind loyalty was the greatest betrayal of the land she stood upon.

Just then, the tent flap was violently thrown open.

A scout scrambled in, crawling on his hands and knees. One of his arms was missing, his body was covered in blood, and his voice was hoarse.

"Gen... General! Black Stone Pass... has been breached!"

"What!"

Every general in the tent turned pale.

Black Stone Pass was the throat of the defensive line connecting the east and west of Cangbei, and the main artery for communication between the Prince’s mansion and the front lines.

The implications of its fall were self-evident.

The scout used his final ounce of strength to shout: "At least five thousand Golden Wolf elites have broken through the pass... and are charging toward... toward Yulong Granary! Our communications... are completely severed!"

With that, his head slumped, and he collapsed, dead.

Yulong Granary!

That was the largest stockpile of grain and fodder for the Cangbei army!

Once destroyed, the tens of thousands of troops on the front lines would collapse without a fight in less than ten days!

The entire defensive line would crumble completely.

A terrifying silence fell over the tent.

Everyone understood that they had been driven into a desperate situation, fighting as a lone force.

The orders from the Prince’s mansion would not come again.

They had been abandoned.

All eyes focused on Shen Li’s back.

In this moment, she was their only pillar of strength.

Shen Li slowly straightened up.

She turned around, her gaze sweeping calmly over the face of every general.

In that gaze, there was no panic, no fear—only a resolution to burn the boats and break the cauldrons.

"The orders from the Prince’s mansion will not come again."

Her voice was not loud, yet it reached every person clearly.

"From now on, here, I am in command."

*A general in the field is not bound by the orders of his sovereign.*

She did not say the words, but everyone in the tent understood.

A long-suppressed will to fight reignited in every chest.

"Wang Zheng!" Shen Li’s voice turned sharp.

"Present!" Wang Zheng stepped forward and knelt on one knee.

"I order you to lead ten thousand infantry and five thousand archers. Abandon all outer outposts, consolidate your forces, and at all costs, hold the main position at Iron Gate Pass!"

Shen Li’s bamboo pointer tapped heavily on the most critical pass on the map.

"Your mission is not to kill the enemy, but to delay them! Use your flesh and blood to buy me three days!"

Wang Zheng was stunned. He looked up sharply: "General! What about you? What about the Black Armor Cavalry?"

Shen Li did not answer him. Her gaze drifted past the chaotic battlefield on the map, toward the far north—that vast, endless expanse of the Gobi Desert.

"The Black Armor Cavalry has another mission."

She walked to the weapon rack and took down the silver spear that had accompanied her for years.

"I am going to deliver a gift to the Golden Wolf King—one he will never forget."

Her voice carried a frantic, murderous intent.

She did not explain the plan, nor did she need to.

The generals present, seeing the way she gripped her spear and the fire burning in her eyes, already understood her determination.

"General! You cannot!"

"General, it is too risky!"

"I am willing to follow you, General!"

Shen Li only coldly spat out two words.

"This is an order."

The unquestionable majesty silenced all further protest.

Wang Zheng, his eyes red, bowed his head heavily.

"I... obey! Please, General... take care!"

"Obey!"

All the generals knelt on one knee in unison, their voices ringing out.

Half an hour later.

The night was deep.

Three thousand Black Armor Cavalry gathered silently outside the Cangbei camp.

There was no pre-battle mobilization, no impassioned slogans.

Only the white mist of breath from men and horses, and the occasional soft clatter of armor plates.

Shen Li swung onto her horse, her silver armor shimmering with a cold light under the faint starlight.

She took one last look at the land behind her, engulfed in the flames of war.

There lay her comrades, the innocent people, and the man she had once hoped to entrust her life to.

Now, all of this required her to save it with a desperate gamble.

She withdrew her gaze, her eyes no longer harboring a shred of hesitation. She turned her horse and faced the boundless Gobi Desert, a symbol of death and the unknown.

She raised her silver spear and pointed it forward.

"Move out."

With the order, three thousand cavalrymen silently surged into the vast night and vanished.

Carrying an unstoppable resolve, they went to seek the only chance to decide the outcome of the war.

### Chapter 39: A Thousand-Mile Raid

These three thousand men were the soldiers Shen Li had raised herself, the elite of the Black Armor Cavalry. Every one of them had been pulled back from the brink of death by Shen Li.

Their lives belonged to the General.

Now, they were willing to use their lives to follow the General in this insane gamble.

Shen Li always charged at the very front.

She ate the same dry rations and drank the same water as her soldiers. Her lips were cracked, and her face was marked by small cuts from the wind and sand, but her eyes remained bright.

She knew this land too well.

Where there were dried-up riverbeds for a quick passage, where there were hidden sand dunes to escape the sun, where there were abandoned ancient wells that might hold water.

This knowledge had been measured out, step by step, over the past decade as she patrolled the borders countless times.

She was like the most experienced alpha wolf, leading her pack through the harshest environment, silently closing in on their prey.

Five days.

Five full days and nights of forced marching.

When they rounded a massive red mountain range, a completely different scene appeared before them.

The Gobi had vanished, replaced by a lush basin filled with water and grass.

And in the center of the basin, a massive city of tents, stretching for miles, stood in plain sight.

Countless cattle and sheep grazed lazily nearby, and innumerable flags snapped in the wind.

The clamor of voices, the laughter and curses of women, and the crying of children could be heard from far away.

This was the Khan’s Royal Court of the Golden Wolf tribe.

It was their base camp, the place where they stored all their wealth and housed their families.

The Golden Wolf King could never have imagined that while his fifty thousand troops were rampaging and reveling in the heart of Cangbei, an army would appear directly at his heart from the direction he deemed most impossible.

The soldiers of the Black Armor Cavalry looked at the massive camp, flames of vengeance burning in their eyes.

They remembered the burned villages and the slaughtered compatriots.

Shen Li slowly raised her right hand.

The three thousand cavalrymen reined in their horses in silence, their movements uniform and precise.

She did not order the charge immediately.

She was waiting.

Waiting for the perfect moment.

Time ticked away, and the sun slowly sank in the west, staining the sky and the earth a deep, bloody hue.

Dusk was the time for the wolf pack to hunt.

It was also the time when human vigilance was at its lowest.

Wisps of smoke rose from the camp, and the aroma of roasted meat mixed with the sour scent of mare’s milk wine drifted through the air.

Many Golden Wolf warriors were already drunk, holding the women they had seized and laughing wantonly in front of their tents.

Now was the time.

Shen Li drew the sword at her waist, its blade reflecting a blinding light in the twilight.

She did not look back, but issued the order in a cold voice.

"Black Armor Army!"

"Present!"

The response of three thousand men was low and suppressed, like the rumble before a thunderstorm.

"Target: The Golden Wolf King’s tent!"

"Follow me, charge!"

The moment the words fell, she dug her heels into her horse’s flanks, and the steed shot forward like an arrow from a bow, the first to charge down the slope.

Behind her, the three thousand cavalrymen, like a black flood released from a dam, let out a roar they had suppressed for five days and surged downward.

"Kill!"

The earth-shattering battle cry instantly tore through the tranquility of the camp.

The Golden Wolf warriors, who had been drinking and making merry, looked up in a daze, only to see what appeared to be demons emerging from hell.

They saw the black battle flag with silver patterns, and the iconic black heavy armor.

"It’s the Black Armor Army! It’s Shen Li!"

Fear instantly gripped everyone.

They could not understand how this army had fallen from the sky.

However, the Black Armor Cavalry gave them no time to think.

It was a total massacre.

Three thousand elite cavalrymen, filled with pent-up rage, charging into an unprepared camp—the destructive power was devastating.

Shen Li led the charge, her silver spear flashing out with lightning speed; every strike claimed several lives.

Her goal was clear: she aimed directly for the most luxurious golden tent in the center of the camp.

*To capture the bandits, first capture their leader!*

The warriors of the Golden Wolf tribe were no cowards. After the initial chaos, they began to organize resistance spontaneously.

However, their resistance appeared so fragile before the charging formation of the Black Armor Cavalry.

Their charge formation was invincible, and Shen Li was the sharpest point of the spear.

Every enemy who stood in her way, no matter who they were, was pierced through by her spear and flung aside.

"Protect the Khan!"

"Stop them!"

Countless personal guards of the Golden Wolf poured in from all directions, attempting to use their flesh and blood to halt the advance of this death cavalry.

The slaughter, under the blood-red dusk, entered its most brutal stage.

Shen Li was bathed in blood—some of it the enemy's, some her own.

Her arm had begun to go numb, but her grip on the spear remained steady.

The Golden Tent was within reach.

Just then, the tent flap was violently thrown open.

A man of exceptionally burly build, clad in golden armor, stepped out, surrounded by a crowd of personal guards.

He was Borita, the Khan of the Golden Wolf tribe.

He looked at the army currently slaughtering his people, then at the female general in silver armor stained with blood. His eyes were first filled with shock, which then transformed into a towering rage.

"Shen Li!"

He roared her name in broken Han Chinese.

He did not flee; instead, he took a massive golden bow from one of his guards.

That bow, which required three strong men to draw, was the symbol of power and kingship on the grasslands.

Borita slowly pulled back the bowstring, the bow frame emitting a harsh, grating sound.

From his quiver, he drew an arrow unlike any other.

It was an arrowhead polished from a wolf's tooth, carved with eerie runes, its tip gleaming with an ominous, dark-green hue under the setting sun.

Deadly poison.

He poured all his strength into this single shot.

His target was none other than the silver figure fighting through the crowd.

Shen Li, who was directing the charge, suddenly felt a sharp, stinging sensation in her back.

It was an instinct for lethal danger honed by long years on the battlefield.

She whipped her head around, locking eyes with Borita, whose gaze was filled with malice and hatred.

She saw the golden bow pulled to a full moon, and she saw the wolf-tooth arrow aimed directly at her.

It was too fast.

And it was too close.

In front of her, a Golden Wolf warrior was raising his blade to strike.

She had only enough time for one choice.

To dodge, or to kill.

She did not hesitate for a second.

The spear in her hand thrust out violently, piercing through the chest of the enemy before her.

At that very same instant.

"Hum!"

The sound of the bowstring vibrating seemed to ring right against her ear.

A wolf-tooth arrow, carrying the most vicious curse of the grasslands, tore through the air and slammed into her back.

Her heavy armor was like paper before that terrifying force.

The arrowhead sank deep into her body.

A searing pain erupted from her back, instantly spreading through her entire frame.

Shen Li’s body stiffened abruptly, and a muffled groan escaped her lips.

Before her eyes, the blood-red dusk began to spin and distort.

Her strength was rapidly draining from her body along with her blood.

She felt herself growing cold.

No.

I cannot fall.

With her final ounce of willpower, she drove her spear deep into the ground beneath her, using the shaft to steady her body as it threatened to collapse.

She raised her head, looking at the Xuanjia soldiers who were showing signs of panic because she had been struck.

She opened her mouth and, with all the strength she had left, roared out her final command as their commander.

"All forces, full assault! Leave... no survivors!"

The roar echoed across the battlefield.

After the shout, she could no longer hold on.

Her hand, gripping the spear shaft, loosened powerlessly.

The entire world plunged into darkness before her.

The silver figure fell heavily from her warhorse.
